November 3, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Tang Seng (黨聲) Party Voice) published the following article in its Volume 2, issued 17:-

THE SHANGHAI INCIDENT

At about 8.30 p.m. September 23, 1936, a Japanese marine was killed and two others were wounded on Haining Road. A large number of Japanese marines and tanks were rushed to the scene and emergency measures were immediately adopted. A congee hawker and two brothers employed in a certain printing shop were taken into custody by the Japanese marine authorities and were later handed over to the Shanghai Municipal Police. This affair is now known as the Shanghai Incident.

Despite the fact that the incident took place in the International Settlement and in a district partolled by Japanese police, the Japanese authorities held the Chinese Government responsible for the incident. Furthermore, several days after the affair, the Japanese newspapers published fabricated reports to the effect that 30,000 members of the Chinese Peace Preservation Corps in plain clothes had arrived in Shanghai and that Chinese troops were being concentrated in the vicinity of Soochow and Kashing. All such reports were refuted by the Chinese Authorities. The only thing that actually tool place was the arrival in Shanghai of reinforcements for the local Japanese Naval Landing Party.

Since the end of August up to the present time, unfortunate incidents occurred at Changtu, Pakhoi, Swatow, Hankow and Shanghai. Of course, we deplore such incidents as they all happened in Chinese territory. In the year 1931 a large area of the Three Eastern Provinces was lost to China.

We naturally regret any incident that befalls a foreign resident in China, but we hope that the "unfortunate events" befalling China during the past few years will also receive attention from our "friendly neighbour". The world has expressed its sympathy towards China's misfortune. Our "nearest neighbour" is well aware of the cause of China's distress.

《党声》（Tang Seng）在其第2卷第17期上发表了以下文章：-

上海事件

1936年9月23日晚8时30分左右，一名日本海军陆战队员在海宁路被杀，另两名受伤。大批日本海军陆战队员和坦克迅速赶至现场，并立即采取了紧急措施。一名粥贩和某印刷店的两名兄弟被日本海军当局拘留，随后移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处。此事现被称为“上海事件”。

尽管该事件发生在公共租界内，且位于日本警察巡逻的区域，但日本当局仍要求中国政府对该事件负责。此外，在事发数天后，日本报纸发布了捏造的报道，声称有3万名便衣中国保安队成员抵达上海，且中国军队正在苏州和嘉兴附近集结。所有这些报道均遭到中国当局的驳斥。实际发生的唯一情况是，当地日本海军陆战队增援部队抵达上海。

自8月底至今，在长图（Changtu，原文不清，或指长春/昌图）、北海、汕头、汉口和上海发生了不幸事件。当然，我们对这些发生在中国领土上的事件表示痛惜。1931年，中国失去了东北三省的大片领土。

我们自然对任何在华外籍居民遭遇的不幸事件表示遗憾，但我们希望我们的“友好邻邦”也能关注过去几年降临在中国的“不幸事件”。世界已对中国的遭遇表示同情。我们的“最近邻邦”很清楚中国苦难的根源。

NOT GUILTY

Accused of Concealing Gun
That Killed Japanese

Chang Yoong-hwo, a food hawker,
charged in the First Special Dis-
trict Court with concealing in a
sand-box a Mauser pistol that had
been used in the murder of A.
Taminato, a Japanese sailor, on
Haining Road, on September 23, was
found not guilty of the charge by
Judge Tsoong yesterday.

The prisoner, however, was order-
ed to be returned to custody as
the police, represented by Mr. T. T.
Tsang, Assistant Municipal Advocate,
reserved the right to appeal against
the decision. The Mauser pistol
which the hawker was found in the
act of concealing was ordered to be
confiscated. The hawker was arrest-
ed immediately after the shooting of
the Japanese sailor which caused
great excitement in the Hongkew
District. He was handed over to
the S.M. Police after being detained
for some time by the Japanese
naval landing party.

食品小贩被判
无罪

被控藏匿杀害日本人的枪支

食品小贩张荣和（Chang Yoong-hwo），因被控在沙箱中藏匿一把用于9月23日在海宁路谋杀日本水手田凑（A. Taminato）的毛瑟手枪，而在第一特区法院受审，昨日被宗法官（Judge Tsoong）裁定该项指控不成立。

然而，被告被命令还押候审，因为由助理市政检察官曾先生（Mr. T. T. Tsang）代表的警方保留了对该判决提出上诉的权利。该小贩被发现藏匿的毛瑟手枪被下令没收。在该日本水手被枪击引发虹口区极大骚动后，该小贩立即被捕。他在被日本海军陆战队拘留一段时间后，被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处。

粥贩张荣和（Chang Yung Woo），他因涉嫌与名为田凑的日本海军陆战队员谋杀案有关而被警方逮捕，并于11月30日获释，发表如下声明：-
“当我被捕并被带到乍浦路日本海军岗哨时，我遭到殴打，面部和身体因殴打而肿胀。8点钟，我再次被带到那里，遭受殴打和审讯，直到凌晨2点，之后我被送往日本海军陆战队总部。随后我被护送到一个警察局。当我离开总部时，一名医生检查了我的伤势，并给我打了两针。”

November 2, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

The "Chinese Saturday Post" published the following comment
on Oct.31:

THE SOONG KUNG YUAN ROAD INCIDENT

After the Hongkew Incident on September 23
nearly all the extra-Settlement roads have been occupied
by Japanese marines; Chinese controlled territory is being
frequently patrolled by Japanese armed forces; Japanese
plain clothes men have often created troubles in Chinese
territory, one of which resulted in the so-called Soong
Kung Yuan Road Incident.
The facts in this incident are as follows:-
On the morning of October 21, two Japanese military officers
in mufti were noticed loitering in the vicinity of Soong
Kung Yuan and Yung Shing Roads taking down the house numbers.
When the people asked them whether they were from the Bureau
of Public Safety and, if so, why they were not in uniform
when engaged in census-taking, the two men replied in
Japanese. As the people did not understand Japanese they
attempted to take the two men to the Bureau of Public Safety
so that enquiries might be made, but the two Japanese refused
to go. A quarrel ensued and this drew a policeman to the
scene. The officer politely escorted the Japanese to the
North Station Branch of the Public Safety Bureau, where,
after being asked a few questions by the Officer in charge,
they were allowed to return to the Naval Landing Party
Headquarters.
These plain clothes men who had unlawfully
entered Chinese territory were courteously treated by the
Chinese authorities. Yet our enemy is not satisfied. In
the afternoon Japanese Consul Terasaki called at the City
Government and lodged a protest. He declared this to be
a serious case and demanded that the assailants of the two
Japanese officers be arrested and that a guarantee be
given against a recurrence of such incidents. Mr. O.K. Yui,
Chief Secretary of the City Government, expressed his
"deep regret".
As a matter of fact, the plain clothes men
were not attacked at all; on the contrary, they were given
every protection by the authorities. Do the Japanese
regard as contrary to law the action of the Chinese officers
in preventing their plain clothes men from carrying out
the kind of activities they were undertaking?
We are of the opinion that the demands had
been presented in order to give their plain clothes men
some legal standing. When they presented such demands,
they had in mind the fact that Chinese officials had
always stood in fear of Japan. Chinese officials should
realize that they have been paid by the Chinese people to
protect the Chinese people; that the activities of such
plain clothes men are not only harmful to peace and order,
but are liable to bring about the downfall of the Chinese
people. Owing to the Shanghai Truce, we cannot station
troops in Shanghai. If the Chinese authorities will not
allow the Chinese people to use lawful and peaceful means
to put a stop to the activities of Japanese plain clothes
men, our enemy will then do what they like and induce
ignorant people to conspire with them until one day the

1936年11月2日。下午译文。

《中文星期六邮报》（Chinese Saturday Post）于10月31日发表了以下评论：

宋公园路事件

在9月23日虹口事件之后，几乎所有租界以外的道路都被日本海军陆战队占领；中国控制区经常有日本武装部队巡逻；日本便衣人员经常在中国领土上制造麻烦，其中之一导致了所谓的宋公园路事件。
该事件的事实如下：-
10月21日上午，有人注意到两名身穿便服的日本军官在宋公园路和永兴路附近徘徊，记录门牌号码。当人们询问他们是否来自公安局，如果是，为何在进行户口调查时不穿制服时，这两人用日语回答。由于人们不懂日语，他们试图将这两人带到公安局以便进行查询，但这两名日本人拒绝前往。随即发生争吵，引来了一名警察。该警官礼貌地将日本人护送至公安局北站分局，在那里，经过负责人询问几个问题后，他们被允许返回海军陆战队总部。
这些非法进入中国领土的便衣人员受到了中国当局的礼遇。然而，我们的敌人并不满意。当天下午，日本领事寺崎（Terasaki）前往市政府提出抗议。他宣称这是一起严重案件，并要求逮捕袭击两名日本军官的人，并保证不再发生此类事件。市政府秘书长俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui）表示了“深切遗憾”。
事实上，便衣人员根本没有受到攻击；相反，他们得到了当局的充分保护。日本人是否认为中国官员阻止其便衣人员进行此类活动是违法的？
我们认为，提出这些要求是为了给他们的便衣人员某种法律地位。当他们提出这些要求时，他们考虑到中国官员一直畏惧日本这一事实。中国官员应该意识到，他们是受中国人民雇佣来保护中国人民的；此类便衣人员的活动不仅有害于和平与秩序，而且可能导致中国人民的覆亡。由于《上海停战协定》，我们不能在上海驻军。如果中国当局不允许中国人民使用合法和平的手段制止日本便衣人员的活动，那么我们的敌人就会为所欲为，并诱使无知的人与他们勾结，直到有一天

whole of China will be occupied by them.
In our opinion, it will be impossible for
the Shanghai City Government to arrest the assailants for
the very good reason that there are no assailants; further-
more, it cannot give a guarantee to our enemy that such
an incident will not happen again. The City Government
should, instead, encourage the people to prevent the
activities of the plain clothes men by peaceful means and
present a counter-demand to the Japanese authorities that
they give a guarantee that such unlawful activities as
those that were being carried out by the two Japanese
officers in mufti in Chinese controlled territory will cease.

整个中国都被他们占领。
在我们看来，上海市政府不可能逮捕袭击者，理由非常充分，即根本不存在袭击者；此外，它也不能向我们的敌人保证此类事件不会再次发生。市政府反而应该鼓励人民通过和平手段阻止便衣人员的活动，并向日本当局提出反要求，即要求其保证停止那两名日本便服军官在中国控制区内进行的此类非法活动。

Hwa Kei Wan Pao dated October 30 :-

THE LOCAL SITUATION

Under the pretext of according protection to the lives and property of Japanese residents following the murder of a Japanese marine named Taminato on Haining Road on September 23, the Japanese authorities recently attempted to extend their police rights, while the Japanese Naval Landing Forces posted marines on every street, thereby creating a reign of terror in Shanghai. The situation appears to be normal now.

The Japanese marines stationed in the Japanese Brewery behind the Rokusan Garden have not yet been withdrawn, while certain plainclothes ronins, under the cloak of fishing at Dah Zang (大场), have been inspecting the Chinese military preparations at Dah Zang. Some of the ronins are disguised as monks; several use bicycles to facilitate the transmission of messages.

The Japanese Naval Landing Forces have been reorganized into a mixed regiment. It now has 5,500. They have five aviation squadrons, each consisting of eight aeroplanes. Three hundred and fifty Japanese residents will be recruited and will be stationed at certain places in Hongkew and Chapei to render guide service to the marines who arrived in Shanghai recently.

After his return from North China, Mr. Kusumoto, Chief of the Special Affairs Organ of the Japanese Land Force in Shanghai, has held two secret conferences with special affairs officers who came here from various districts in Central China. Some 60 officers were present. Ten resolutions were passed. No information was given to the Press.

Information secured by a reporter of the Ta Kung News Agency shows that the military training of Japanese citizens of military age in Shanghai will be commenced from November 9. The training will take place in the Japanese Youths School. The Japanese Consulate-General will inspect the men on November 14 when senior officers of the Japanese Naval Landing Forces etc. will also be present.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking telegram) :-

Malicious Reports in Japanese Press; Ministry of Foreign Affairs Issues Warning

Following the assassination of General Yang Yung Tai, Chairman of the Hupeh Provincial Government, the Japanese newspapers have been publishing malicious and insulting reports. It is understood that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the National Government has detailed an official to give a stern warning to the Japanese Embassy and to demand the suppression of such reports.

Since October 26, the Japanese forces stationed in Peiping and Tientsin have been holding manoeuvres on a large scale in the districts of Peiping and Tientsin including the northern section of the Peiping-Hankow Railway and with Fengtai as the centre of operations. The operations will last 10 days. About 7,000 Japanese soldiers are taking part. The Japanese have forcibly occupied about 300

10月30日的《华报》（Hwa Kei Wan Pao，音译）：-

本地局势

以9月23日一名名为田凑的日本海军陆战队员在海宁路被杀为由，日本当局近期试图扩大其警察权，同时日本海军陆战队在每条街道部署陆战队员，从而在上海制造了恐怖统治。目前局势看似正常。

驻扎在六三花园背后日本啤酒厂的日本海军陆战队尚未撤走，而某些便衣浪人以在大场捕鱼为掩护，正在视察大场的中国军事准备情况。部分浪人伪装成和尚；几人使用自行车以便于传递消息。

日本海军陆战队已重组为一个混成团。现有兵力5,500人。他们拥有五个航空中队，每个中队由八架飞机组成。将招募三百五十名日本居民，并驻扎在虹口和闸北的某些地点，为最近抵达上海的海军陆战队员提供向导服务。

日本陆军上海特务机关长楠本（Kusumoto，音译）从华北返回后，与来自华中各地区的特务官员举行了两次秘密会议。约有60名官员出席。通过了十项决议。未向新闻界提供任何信息。

大公通讯社记者获得的消息显示，在上海的适龄日本公民的军事训练将于11月9日开始。训练将在日本青年学校进行。日本总领事馆将于11月14日检阅人员，届时日本海军陆战队的高级军官等也将出席。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：-

日本报纸的恶意报道；外交部发出警告

继湖北省政府主席杨永泰将军遇刺后，日本报纸一直发布恶意和侮辱性报道。据悉，国民政府外交部已指派一名官员向日本大使馆提出严厉警告，并要求压制此类报道。

自10月26日以来，驻扎在北平和天津的日本部队一直在北平和天津地区，包括平汉铁路北段，以丰台为中心，举行大规模演习。演习将持续10天。约有7,000名日本士兵参加。日本人强行占领了约300

dwelling houses on the outskirts of Tientsin; they have
also commandeered food and other things. It is learned
that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has lodged a protest
with the Japanese Embassy against the action of the
Japanese troops for it constitutes a violation of Inter-

Hwa Mei Wan Pao published the following comment on October 30 :-

Japan Should Withdraw Her Landing Forces from North China
As Soon As Possible

According to reports published by Japanese
newspapers, there are only a little more than 20,000
Japanese residents, including Koreans, in North China,
especially in Tientsin, Peiping and Shanhaikwan. However,
more than 7,500 men of the Japanese landing forces are
stationed in North China between Tientsin and Peiping, to
saying nothing of the puppet forces in Eastern Hopei and
North Charhar.

According to the Japanese authorities,
the Japanese garrisons in North China have been reinforced
for the purpose of safeguarding Japanese residents in
North China. But is it reasonable and legitimate for
Japan to station 7,500 soldiers to protect about 20,000
Japanese residents?

According to the terms of the Boxer
Protocol, foreign Powers are allowed to station their
troops in Peiping, Tientsin, Chinwangtao and Shanhaikwan
for the purpose of protecting the Legation quarters in
Peiping and keeping open communication between Peiping
and the sea. During the past few years, most of the
important officials of the Japanese Embassy have remained
in Shanghai because of the removal of our Government to
Nanking. This fact makes Japan's action in stationing
7,500 soldiers in North China more unreasonable.

During the Sino-Japanese negotiations for
an adjustment of the relations between the two countries
last month, the Japanese authorities demanded that China
suppress the anti-Japanese movement. In the meantime,
the Japanese landing forces in North China were holding
extensive autumn manoeuvres in Peiping and Tientsin.

According to Reuter and other special
telegraphic reports, over 2,000 Chinese peasants have been
forced to vacate their homes by Japanese troops engaged
in the manoeuvres and were further forced to supply horses
and vehicles to the Japanese. Now let us ask Japan: will
not such activities on the part of her landing forces in
North China create a bad impression and ill-feeling in
the minds of the Chinese people?

It is being said that the object of these
manoeuvres is to intimidate our Government. Then we have
to remind Japan that her action will create bad feeling
among the Chinese people. If Japan desires to bring about
an amicable settlement of all outstanding Sino-Japanese
issues through diplomatic negotiations, then she should
withdraw as soon as possible her forces in North China.

天津郊区的住宅；他们还征用了食物和其他物品。据悉，外交部已就日军此举向日本大使馆提出抗议，因为该行为构成对国际法的违反，并损害了中国的主权权利。

《华美晚报》于10月30日发表如下评论：—

日本应尽快从华北撤走登陆部队

据日本报纸报道，在华北，特别是在天津、北平和山海关，包括朝鲜人在内的日本居民仅有2万余人。然而，在天津与北平之间的华北地区，驻扎着7,500多名日本登陆部队士兵，这还不包括冀东和察北的伪军。

据日本当局称，加强在华北的驻军是为了保护华北的日本居民。但是，日本派遣7,500名士兵来保护约2万名日本居民，这合理且合法吗？

根据《辛丑条约》的规定，外国列强被允许在北平、天津、秦皇岛和山海关驻扎军队，目的是保护北平的使馆区，并保持北平与出海通道的畅通。在过去几年中，由于我国政府迁往南京，日本大使馆的大部分重要官员都留在上海。这一事实使得日本在华北驻扎7,500名士兵的行为更加不合理。

在上个月中日两国为调整双边关系进行的谈判中，日本当局要求中国镇压反日运动。与此同时，日本在华北的登陆部队正在北平和天津举行大规模的秋季演习。

据路透社及其他特约电报报道，2,000多名中国农民被迫离开家园，为参与演习的日军腾出空间，并进一步被迫向日本人提供马匹和车辆。现在我们要问日本：其登陆部队在华北的此类活动，难道不会在中国民众心中造成不良印象和恶感吗？

据说，这些演习的目的是恐吓我国政府。那么我们必须提醒日本，其行为将在中国人民中引起反感。如果日本希望通过外交谈判友好地解决所有悬而未决的中日问题，那么她应尽快撤走在华北的部队。

October 31, 1936. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:-

THE HAINING ROAD MURDER CASE : ACCUSED FOUND NOT GUILTY

Chang Yung Woo (張榮和), native of Taichow, a congee hawker, was detained by Mr. Tadashi Horie at 8.20 p.m. September 23 for concealing in a sand box near the entrance of Lane 15, Haining Road, a Mauser pistol that was used in the killing of a Japanese marine named Taminato on Haining Road. He was charged by Hongkew Police Station before the Shanghai First Special District Court under Article 165 of the Chinese Criminal Code with destroying evidence. The accused was defended by lawyer Shuan Yoeh Hwa (单毓華).

At 2 p.m. yesterday the case again came up for hearing before Judge Tsong Ching (鍾清) of the Shanghai First Special District Court who found the accused not guilty and ordered the confiscation of the pistol.

Mr. Chang Sze Tsoh (張師竹), Assistant Municipal Advocate, informed the Court that the Police would consider whether an appeal would be filed or not and requested that the accused be detained at the Police Station. The request was granted by the Court.

1936年10月31日。晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：—

海宁路谋杀案：被告被判无罪

张荣和（Chang Yung Woo），台州人，粥贩，于9月23日晚8时20分被堀江正（Tadashi Horie）先生拘留，原因是他在海宁路15弄入口附近的沙箱内藏匿了一把毛瑟手枪，该手枪曾被用于在海宁路杀害一名名为田凑（Taminato）的日本海军陆战队员。虹口捕房依据《中华民国刑法》第165条，在上海第一特区地方法院指控其毁灭证据。被告由律师单毓華（Shuan Yoeh Hwa）辩护。

昨日下午2时，该案再次在上海第一特区地方法院钟清（Tsong Ching）法官面前开庭审理，法官判决被告无罪，并命令没收该手枪。

助理市检察官张师竹（Chang Sze Tsoh）先生告知法庭，警方将考虑是否提起上诉，并请求将被告羁押于捕房。法庭批准了这一请求。

17280
THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 31, 1936
Hawker Freed In
Haining Rd. Case
7538
31 10 36
Acquitted Of Concealing
Gun Used In Killing
Bluejacket
IS BEING HELD AS
MATERIAL WITNESS
Aged Father Breaks
Into Tears; Japan-
ese In Court
Tseng Yoong-ho, age 21, the food
hawker charged with concealing the
Mauser pistol, which he knew had
been used in the Haining Road
shooting on the night of September
23, heard the case against him dis-
missed by the First Special District
Court yesterday afternoon but he is
still not a free man. He will con-
tinue to be held in custody as a
material witness to the crime which
resulted in the death of Warrant
Officer Asamitsu Taminato, of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party and
the wounding of two other Japan-
ese bluejackets.
The case came up for judgment
at 2 p.m. yesterday and before a
courtroom crowded with Tseng's
relatives, Japanese naval observers
and police, Tseng listened in silence
as the court informed him that he
would not be sent to prison. He
was warned not to hide guns in
sand-boxes in the future, if he
wished to save himself and others
a lot of trouble but to report to
the police.
Father Breaks Into Tears
Hanging his head, the youth
mumbled something that might
have been his promise to be more
careful in the future, or his thanks
to the court for being exonerated
of any crime. His voice was so low
that no one could catch all that he
said. But Tseng was not the hap-
piest man in the court. His aged
father, seated in the rear of the
courtroom, a constant spectator
and an attentive listener at every
hearing of the case, broke into
tears as judgment was pronounced.
Shortly after his son was ar-
rested, the elder Tseng stated, when
interviewed by newspapermen, that
Yoong-ho was the youngest of nine
sons. The others had all died and
the hawker was the only child he
had left.
Tseng was arrested a short time
after the shooting had occurred.
According to his story, he was
walking along the street when he
found a Mauser pistol, lying on
the pavement near the entrance to
an alleyway on Haining Road, only
a few yards from where the mur-
derer had stood when he opened
fire on the bluejackets.
Hid Pistol
The hawker picked up the pistol
and hid it in a sandbox. His action
was observed by a Japanese civilian
standing nearby. The latter rushed
over to Tseng, grabbed him by the
shoulder with one hand and dug
into the sandbox with the other,
getting possession of the pistol.
Tseng was turned over to the Naval
Landing Party and handed over to
the Shanghai Municipal Police the
following day.
At first, Tseng denied that he
knew anything about the gun. He
was merely standing by the sand-
box when the Japanese civilian
grabbed him. He had never seen
the gun, and he insisted that he
had been unjustly arrested.
He changed his story in a few
days, however, declaring that he
had found the gun, had picked it
up and had hidden it. He con-
tinued that he expected to inform
the police as soon as the situation
had become less tense. The reason
he didn't notify them immediately,
he declared, was because he was
afraid he might be linked with the
killing.

被控藏匿用于杀害水兵的枪支，获判无罪
作为重要证人被拘留
老父泪流满面；日本人出庭

曾永浩（Tseng Yoong-ho），21岁，食品小贩，被控藏匿一把毛瑟手枪，他明知该枪曾用于9月23日晚的海宁路枪击案。昨日下午，第一特区地方法院驳回了对他的起诉，但他仍未获得自由。他将继续被拘留，作为导致日本海军陆战队准尉浅光田凑（Asamitsu Taminato）死亡及另外两名日本水兵受伤一案的重要证人。

该案于昨日下午2时开庭宣判，法庭内挤满了曾某的亲属、日本海军观察员和警察。当法庭告知他不会入狱时，曾某静默聆听。法庭警告他，如果希望为自己和他人避免许多麻烦，将来不要将枪支藏在沙箱里，而应向警方报告。

父亲泪流满面

年轻人低着头，喃喃自语，内容可能是承诺今后会更加小心，或是感谢法庭免除其罪行。他的声音太低，没人能听清他说的所有内容。但曾某并非法庭上最快乐的人。坐在法庭后排的老父亲，作为每次庭审的常驻旁观者和专注的倾听者，在宣判时泪流满面。

曾父在接受记者采访时曾表示，儿子被捕后不久，永浩是九个儿子中最小的一个。其他儿子均已去世，这名小贩是他仅存的孩子。

枪击发生后不久，曾某即被捕。据他陈述，当时他正沿街行走，发现一把毛瑟手枪躺在海宁路一条巷口附近的人行道上，距离凶手向水兵开火时所站的位置仅几码远。

藏匿手枪

小贩捡起手枪并将其藏在沙箱中。他的举动被附近的一名日本平民目睹。后者冲向曾某，一手抓住他的肩膀，另一手伸进沙箱，夺得了手枪。曾某随后被移交给海军陆战队，并于次日移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处。

起初，曾某否认对该枪有任何了解。他说当那名日本平民抓住他时，他只是站在沙箱旁。他声称从未见过那把枪，并坚持认为自己是遭到不公正逮捕。

然而，几天后他改变了说法，声称他发现了那把枪，捡起来并藏了起来。他接着说，他打算在局势不那么紧张后立即通知警方。他宣称没有立即通知警方的原因是因为他害怕自己会与杀人案产生关联。

Jil

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 31, 1936
17272

HAWKER ACQUITTED
OF HIDING GUN

Police Intend To File
Appeal; Man Held
In Murder Case

Tsang Yoong-ho, 21-year-old
congee seller, who was charged
with concealing the heavy calibre
Mauser pistol, which he knew had
been used in the murder of a Jap-
anese seaman and the wounding of
two others on Haining Road on
the night of September 23 last, was
declared not guilty by Judge
Tsoong in the First Special Dis-
trict Court yesterday morning.
Dissatisfaction was expressed by
police officials present at the court
finding the hawker not guilty on a
charge of concealing evidence un-
der Article 167 of the Chinese
Criminal Code, and it was intimat-
ed that an appeal will be filed
against the Court's decision.
Tsang, in the meantime, was or-
dered by the Court to be detained
during the period of appeal.
Tsang was arrested by a Japan-
ese civilian in Lane 15, on the
north side of Haining Road, near
Woosung Road, a few minutes
after an unidentified gunman had
fatally shot First Class Seaman
Taminato, of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party, and wounded two
other marines. When seized,
Tsang was alleged to have just
thrown the heavy Mauser pistol
used in the shooting into a sand
box.
He first denied any knowledge
of the shooting or of having
thrown the gun into the sand box,
but at a court hearing on October
16, he declared that he arrived on
the scene of the crime after the
shooting had taken place and, see-
ing a Mauser pistol lying on the
pavement, he picked it up and hid
it in the sand box. He stated that
he did so with the sole purpose of
handing it over later to the auth-
orities with the idea of collecting a
reward.
After being arrested by a Japan-
ese civilian, he was handed over
to the Japanese Naval Landing
Party and, after being questioned
by them, he was handed over to
the Shanghai Municipal Police and
brought before the Chinese tri-
bunal together with two other sus-
pects, since released.
Tsang's 60-year-old father, mo-
ther and wife were in court yester-
day and tears streamed down the
father's eyes when he heard that
his son was acquitted. He will,
however, be detained for the next
10 days pending the filing of an
appeal by the police.

（批：gil / osr）

《上海泰晤士报》，1936年10月31日，星期六
17272

小贩因藏匿枪支获判无罪

警方拟提起上诉；男子在谋杀案中被拘留

曾永浩（Tsang Yoong-ho），21岁，粥贩，被控藏匿一把大口径毛瑟手枪，他明知该枪曾用于去年9月23日晚在海宁路谋杀一名日本水兵并致另外两人受伤。昨日上午，钟（Tsoong）法官在第一特区地方法院宣判其无罪。

出席庭审的警方官员对法庭依据《中华民国刑法》第167条判决小贩藏匿证据罪名不成立表示不满，并暗示将对法院的决定提起上诉。

在此期间，法庭命令在上诉期间拘留曾某。

在一名身份不明的枪手致命射杀日本海军陆战队一等水兵田凑（Taminato）并打伤另外两名陆战队员几分钟后，曾某在海宁路北侧、靠近吴淞路的15弄被一名日本平民逮捕。据称，在被抓获时，曾某刚刚将用于射击的那把重型毛瑟手枪扔进沙箱。

他最初否认对枪击案或将枪扔进沙箱有任何知情，但在10月16日的庭审中，他声称自己在枪击发生后到达现场，看到人行道上有一把毛瑟手枪，便捡起并藏在沙箱里。他表示，他这样做唯一的目的是为了日后将其交给当局，以期获得赏金。

被一名日本平民逮捕后，他被移交给日本海军陆战队，在接受讯问后，又被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，并与另外两名嫌疑人（此后已释放）一同被带上中国法庭受审。

曾某60岁的父亲、母亲和妻子昨日出庭，当听到儿子被判无罪时，老父热泪盈眶。然而，在警方提起上诉期间，他将被继续拘留10天。

（批：gil / osr）

October 31, 1936. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:-

THE HAINING ROAD MURDER CASE : ACCUSED FOUND NOT GUILTY

Chang Yung Woo (張榮和), native of Taichow, a congee hawker, was detained by Mr. Tadashi Horie at 8.20 p.m. September 23 for concealing in a sand box near the entrance of Lane 15, Haining Road, a Mauser pistol that was used in the killing of a Japanese marine named Taminato on Haining Road. He was charged by Hongkew Police Station before the Shanghai First Special District Court under Article 165 of the Chinese Criminal Code with destroying evidence. The accused was defended by lawyer Shuen Yoeh Hwa (单毓華).

At 2 p.m. yesterday the Case again came up for hearing before Judge Tsong Ching (鍾清) of the Shanghai First Special District Court who found the accused not guilty and ordered the confiscation of the pistol.

Mr. Chang Sze Tsoh (張師竹), Assistant Municipal Advocate, informed the Court that the Police would consider whether an appeal would be filed or not and requested that the accused be detained at the Police Station. The request was granted by the Court.

1936年10月31日。晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：—

海宁路谋杀案：被告被判无罪

张荣和（Chang Yung Woo），台州人，粥贩，于9月23日晚8时20分被堀江正（Tadashi Horie）先生拘留，原因是他在海宁路15弄入口附近的沙箱内藏匿了一把毛瑟手枪，该手枪曾被用于在海宁路杀害一名名为田凑（Taminato）的日本海军陆战队员。虹口捕房依据《中华民国刑法》第165条，在上海第一特区地方法院指控其毁灭证据。被告由律师单毓華（Shuen Yoeh Hwa）辩护。

昨日下午2时，该案再次在上海第一特区地方法院钟清（Tsong Ching）法官面前开庭审理，法官判决被告无罪，并命令没收该手枪。

助理市检察官张师竹（Chang Sze Tsoh）先生告知法庭，警方将考虑是否提起上诉，并请求将被告羁押于捕房。法庭批准了这一请求。

No. D 7538.
Date 30. / 10. / 36

October 30, 1936. Morning Translation.

It is now learned that rebel Woo Yi Ting first
detailed a man named Yang (楊 ) to Shanghai to establish
a number of traitorous organs; he will come to Shanghai
later.

Sin Wan Pao (Swatow telegram):
Japanese Photographs Transportation of Troops
On October 28 a certain Japanese surreptitiously
photographed the transportation of the troops of the 10th
Division at Swatow. He was ordered to hand over the
negatives.
The matter was reported to the authorities
concerned and a protest will be lodged with the Japanese
Consul.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated Oct. 29:
The Local Situation: Activities of Japanese Marines
At 1.30 p.m. October 28, five Japanese armoured
cars, three motor cycles, three small tanks and five trucks
moved along Hungjao Road from west to east. At 6 p.m.
another truck was seen on this road and at 9 p.m. several more
trucks again passed along this road. The movements of
Japanese marines along Hungjao Road had something to do with
an experiment conducted by an American airman flying an
aeroplane of the China National Air Corporation in laying
a smoke screen in the air on the morning of October 28.
On the morning of October 29, about 150 Japanese
marines were sent in five trucks to the Japanese Brewery.
In all, about 200 Japanese marines are now stationed in
Chapei.

The National Herald and other local newspapers:
UNSUCCESSFUL ATTEMPT BY JAPANESE TO ESTABLISH A STOCK
EXCHANGE
Reports were current recently that Japanese
merchants in Shanghai were planning to establish a stock
exchange to disturb the money market. In 1917 or 1918
"Wu Da Woo Leung" (烏大五郎) and a number of other
Japanese made huge profits by establishing an exchange in
Shanghai. This exchange was dissolved about ten years
ago.
About a month ago a number of local Japanese
merchants approached certain Chinese commercial leaders
with a view to reviving this exchange, but the Chinese
merchants refused to co-operate with the Japanese.

1936年10月30日。晨间译件。

现获悉，叛军吴义亭（Woo Yi Ting）首先派遣一名姓杨（楊）的男子前往上海建立若干汉奸机关；他本人稍后将抵达上海。

《新晚报》（汕头电报）：
日军运兵照片
10月28日，一名日本人在汕头秘密拍摄了第十师团部队运输的情况。当局责令其交出底片。
此事已报告有关当局，并将向日本领事提出抗议。

10月29日《华美晚报》：
本地局势：日本海军陆战队的活动
10月28日下午1时30分，五辆日本装甲车、三辆摩托车、三辆小型坦克和五辆卡车沿虹桥路由西向东行驶。下午6时，在该路上又见到一辆卡车，晚上9时，又有几辆卡车经过此路。日本海军陆战队在虹桥路的行动，与10月28日上午一名驾驶中国航空公司飞机的美国飞行员在空中进行烟雾屏蔽试验有关。
10月29日上午，约150名日本海军陆战队员分乘五辆卡车被派往日本啤酒厂。目前驻闸北的日本海军陆战队员总数约为200人。

《国民日报》及其他本地报纸：
日本人设立证券交易所企图未遂
近期有传闻称，在沪日商正计划设立一家证券交易所以扰乱金融市场。1917年或1918年，“乌大五郎”（音译）及其他一些日本人通过在上海设立交易所赚取了巨额利润。该交易所大约在十年前解散。
约一个月前，一些在沪日商接触某些中国商界领袖，试图恢复该交易所，但中国商人拒绝与日本人合作。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 7538.
October 29, 1936. Morning Translation Date 29/10/36

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-
An Open Letter to Japanese Residents
At a meeting held by the Shanghai First Special District Citizens' Federation at 3 p.m. October 28, it was resolved that the Federation publish an open letter addressed to the Japanese residents announcing that as the National Government is endeavouring to bring about an adjustment of Sino-Japanese problems, and as several unexpected incidents had occurred recently, the Federation hopes that Japanese residents will refrain from doing anything that is liable to give rise to trouble, but to abide by the spirit of friendship and the principle of mutual existence and prosperity so as to improve the relations between the two countries.

Sin Wan Pao Evening Edition published the following comment on October 28 :-
Activities of Plain Clothes Japanese
After the occurrence of the Haining Road murder case, large parties of Japanese marines were mobilized and precautionary measures were adopted as if they were about to deal with a big enemy force. A panic was created. Although the local situation has now slightly improved, Japanese marines are still entering Chinese controlled territory. This has given rise to much uneasiness among the people.
Several Japanese in civilian dress were discovered at Dah Zang Village undertaking a certain mission under the pretext of fishing. Special attention should be paid to the activities of such Japanese for their acts show them to be spies. The Chinese Authorities should not allow free movements in Chinese controlled territory to persons who conduct secret activities. Japanese are now visiting the districts adjacent to Shanghai without first notifying the Chinese Police. Such visits are liable to arouse the suspicions of villagers and trouble will occur because of language difficulties and misunderstanding. The Chinese Authorities should take proper precautions; they should also lodge a protest with the Japanese Authorities and demand that the movements of Japanese be restricted.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-
TRAITORS ARRESTED AT NANTAO
Of late, traitors have been very active in this city and many of them have been arrested by the Public Safety Bureau.
Towards the evening of October 27, the Jih Loh Poo Branch of the Public Safety Bureau at Nantao received a secret report to the effect that many traitors are daily frequenting the Tsung Zay Tea Shop (春生茶楼), Nantao, to fabricate rumours and to procure military information. The Officer-in-Charge of the Branch Bureau sent a large party of detectives to the tea shop and arrested 9 suspects who were later handed over to the Headquarters of the Public Safety Bureau for investigations.

编号 D 7538。
1936年10月29日。晨间译件 日期 36年10月29日

《新晚报》及其他本地报纸：
致日侨的公开信
上海第一特区市民联合会于10月28日下午3时举行会议，决议由该会发表一封致日侨的公开信，宣布鉴于国民政府正努力调整中日问题，且近期发生数起意外事件，本会希望日侨避免从事任何可能引发事端的行为，而是秉持友好精神及共存共荣原则，以改善两国关系。

《新晚报》晚刊于10月28日发表如下评论：
便衣日本人的活动
海宁路谋杀案发生后，大批日本海军陆战队被动员起来，并采取预防措施，仿佛要对付强大的敌军。这造成了恐慌。虽然本地局势现已略有改善，但日本海军陆战队仍在进入中方控制区域。这在民众中引起了极大的不安。
在大场村发现几名身着便服的日本人，借口捕鱼执行某种任务。应特别注意此类日本人的活动，因为其行为表明他们是间谍。中国当局不应允许从事秘密活动的人员在中方控制区域内自由行动。日本人现在在未事先通知中国警察的情况下访问上海邻近地区。此类访问容易引起村民的怀疑，并会因语言障碍和误解而发生麻烦。中国当局应采取适当预防措施；还应向日本当局提出抗议，并要求限制日本人的行动。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：
南市逮捕汉奸
近期，汉奸在本市活动频繁，其中许多人已被公安局逮捕。
10月27日傍晚，南市公安局日晖港分局接到密报，称许多汉奸每日频繁出入南市众友茶楼（Tsung Zay Tea Shop），制造谣言并搜集军事情报。分局主管派遣大批侦探前往该茶楼，逮捕了9名嫌疑人，随后将他们移交公安局总部进行调查。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 7538
Date 29 / 10 . 36

October 29, 1936. Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers:-

ACTIVITIES OF LOCAL JAPANESE MARINES

At 9.40 a.m. yesterday, two Japanese
military trucks, three tanks Nos. 11, 12 and 14, and four
Japanese officers on motor cycles mounted with machine guns
proceeded along the Soochow Creek at a high speed from west
to east from the direction of the Jessfield Village.

The Japanese troops stationed in North
China are conducting manoeuvres on a large scale, while the
local Japanese forces are also showing signs of activity.
Japanese in civilian clothes have been found engaged in
secret activities. At 10.40 a.m. yesterday, four Japanese
armoured cars were noticed on Robison Road in the Western
District. At 3 p.m. three armoured cars and three motor
cycles patrolled the vicinity of North Szechuen Road.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部登记处。
编号 D 7538
日期 36年10月29日

1936年10月29日。晨间译件。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

本地日本海军陆战队的活动

昨日上午9时40分，两辆日本军用卡车、第11、12和14号三辆坦克，以及四名骑着装有机关枪的摩托车的日本军官，从极司菲尔村（Jessfield Village）方向沿苏州河高速由西向东行驶。

驻扎在华北的日军正在进行大规模演习，而本地日军也显示出活跃迹象。发现身着便服的日本人从事秘密活动。昨日上午10时40分，在西区罗别根路（Robison Road）发现四辆日本装甲车。下午3时，三辆装甲车和三辆摩托车在四川北路附近巡逻。

近期，汉奸在本市活动频繁，其中许多人已被公安局逮捕。

October 28, 1936. Morning translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao (27/10):

JAPANESE MISTAKEN FOR CHINESE TRAITORS AT DAH ZANG VILLAGE

The Shanghai Nichi Nichi, a local Japanese daily, published on the morning of October 27 an article stating that on October 25 an incident took place at Dah Zang Village between six Japanese and a party of students and members of the Peace Preservation Corps.

According to an investigation made by a reporter of this paper, it was ascertained that the incident took place at Dah Zang Village on the afternoon of October 25, when six Japanese, on their way back to Shanghai after fishing in the vicinity of that village, noticed some posters containing patriotic slogans on the walls of the Shan Hai School. Thinking that the slogans were anti-Japanese, the six Japanese tore them down. Their action was noticed by a number of villagers and young students who became suspicious. The Japanese were in foreign civilian clothing, but as the villagers were unaware that they were Japanese subjects, they mistook the Japanese for Chinese traitors, because during the past few days Chinese traitors have been very active in that village. Thus a large crowd at once surrounded the Japanese.

Upon learning of the trouble, members of the Peace Preservation Corps stationed in the vicinity of the village were immediately detailed to the scene. After dispersing the villagers and students, officers interrogated the six Japanese and upon finding that they were really Japanese subjects, the Peace Preservation Corps immediately notified the North Railway Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety of the affair. Subsequently the six Japanese were sent to Shanghai under an escort of Police and members of the Peace Preservation Corps.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

The Local Situation

The Japanese marines stationed in the Japanese Brewery, Chapei, have been active during the past few days. Occasionally, the marines, after disguising themselves, used to visit Ze Dien Road, Pah Sz Jao and Dah Zang to make a secret inspection of the district.

At 2 p.m. October 26 a batch of 85 armed Japanese marines led by five officers patrolled Dong Chi Road as far as Pah Sz Jao and made sketches.

At 9 a.m. yesterday, two trucks carrying some 30 armed Japanese marines left the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters and proceeded to the Japanese Brewery, Chapei. Japanese transportation trucks and patrol cars have been very busy in Chapei.

The situation in Hongkew is quiet although Japanese marine posts are still to be found.

At noon yesterday, some 60 armed Japanese marines from the Japanese Headquarters in Hongkew in five military trucks passed through North Szechuen Road, Haining Road, Seward Road, the Garden Bridge, the Bund, Avenue

1936年10月28日。晨间译件。

《华美晚报》（10月27日）：

大场村日本人被误认为汉奸

当地日文日报《上海日日新闻》于10月27日上午刊登一篇文章，称10月25日在大场村发生了一起六名日本人与一群学生及保安队成员之间的事件。

据该报记者调查查明，事件发生于10月25日下午，当时六名日本人在该村附近钓鱼后返回上海途中，注意到山海学校墙壁上贴有一些包含爱国口号的海报。这六名日本人认为这些口号是反日的，便将其撕下。他们的举动被一些村民和年轻学生注意到并引起怀疑。这些日本人穿着西式便服，但由于村民不知道他们是日本臣民，便将这些日本人误认为是汉奸，因为过去几天里汉奸在该村活动非常频繁。因此，一大群人立即包围了这些日本人。

得知骚乱后，驻扎在村庄附近的保安队成员立即被派往现场。在驱散村民和学生后，警官讯问了这六名日本人，在确认他们确系日本臣民后，保安队立即将此事件通知公安局北站分局。随后，这六名日本人在警察和保安队成员的护送下被送往上海。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

本地局势

驻扎在闸北日本啤酒厂的日本海军陆战队在过去几天里活动频繁。偶尔，陆战队员在乔装打扮后，会前往狄思威路、八字桥和大场对该地区进行秘密视察。

10月26日下午2时，一批由五名军官率领的85名武装日本海军陆战队员巡逻东熙华德路直至八字桥，并绘制草图。

昨日上午9时，两辆载有约30名武装日本海军陆战队员的卡车离开日本海军陆战队总部，前往闸北日本啤酒厂。日本的运输卡车和巡逻车在闸北非常繁忙。

虹口的局势平静，尽管仍可见到日本海军陆战队的哨所。

昨日中午，约60名来自虹口日本总部的武装日本海军陆战队员乘坐五辆军用卡车，经过北四川路、海宁路、西华德路、外白渡桥、外滩、爱多亚路

S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 7538.
Date 27 / 10 / 36
Afternoon Translation.

October 27, 1936.

NICHI NICHI

ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST JAPANESE COMMITTED BY CHINESE PEOPLE

The anti-Japanese feeling among the Chinese people has become worse since the increase in the number and the equipment of the Peace Preservation Corps in the vicinity of Shanghai. Outrages against Japanese subjects have frequently occurred.

On October 25, 6 Japanese had a narrow escape when they were surrounded by some 100 students and members of the Peace Preservation Corps at Dah Zang Ching. As they were about to be assaulted they were rescued by members of the Bureau of Public Safety.

On October 25, Y. Yamanaka, 362 Chapoo Road, K. Murai, 375 Woosung Road and four other Japanese went to Dah Zang Ching to fish. At about 4 p.m., as they were waiting for a motor-car at Yu Ching Tsu (余慶裏), Y. Yamanaka secured one of the many anti-Japanese posters posted in the vicinity. A girl who noticed his act called in a party of the Peace Preservation Corps who surrounded the Japanese. Later a party of students arrived in a motor truck shouting "Kill the Japanese," "Assault the Japanese". After about half an hour, the Japanese were forced to accompany the members of the Peace Preservation Corps to their station. On arrival at the station the members of the Peace Preservation Corps pointed their pistols at the six Japanese and took them to the station in Miao Hong Ching in a motor truck. On the way to Miao Hong Ching, the members of the Peace Preservation Corps told the students, who were following them, that the Japanese would be severely punished. Upon reaching the station in Miao Hong Ching, a member of the Bureau of Public Safety reported the affair to the North Station Sub-Station of the Bureau. The Japanese returned to their homes at 11 p.m. and made a report to the Japanese Consular Police on October 26.

1936年10月27日。

《日日新闻》

中国人对日本人实施的暴力行为

自上海附近保安队的数量和装备增加以来，中国民众中的反日情绪日益恶化。针对日本臣民的暴行时有发生。

10月25日，6名日本人在大场泾被约100名学生和保安队成员包围，险些遇险。就在他们即将遭到袭击时，被公安局成员救出。

10月25日，住在乍浦路362号的Y. Yamanaka（音译）、住在吴淞路375号的K. Murai（音译）以及其他四名日本人前往大场泾钓鱼。下午4时许，当他们在余庆里等候汽车时，Y. Yamanaka（音译）撕下了附近张贴的众多反日海报中的一张。一名注意到他这一举动的女孩叫来了一队保安队成员，他们将这几名日本人包围。随后，一队学生乘卡车赶到，高喊“打死日本人”、“殴打日本人”。大约半小时后，这些日本人被迫随保安队成员前往其驻地。到达驻地后，保安队成员用枪指着这六名日本人，并用卡车将他们送往庙行镇的警局。在前往庙行镇的途中，保安队成员告诉跟随他们的学生，这些日本人将受到严厉惩罚。抵达庙行镇警局后，一名公安局人员将此事件报告给公安局北站分所。这些日本人于晚上11时返回家中，并于10月26日向日本领事馆警察报案。

No. D 7538.
Date 26. 10. 36.

October 26, 1936.    4    Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:

Public Safety Bureau Uses Written Language To Avoid
Misunderstandings with Japanese

Since the Haining Road affair, disputes between
Japanese and Chinese have frequently occurred. The
principal cause of such troubles is, in the opinion of the
Public Safety Bureau, due to language difficulties. For
this reason, the Bureau, on October 24, instructed policemen
at the North Railway Station to carry with them while on
duty the following questions in the Japanese and Chinese
languages:-
1) Where are you going? Please write a note.
2) The place farther on is a desolate spot, please don't
go there.
3) I am escorting you to the Police Station to find a
Japanese speaking man to talk with you.
4) Have you a name card? Please give me one.
5) Please wait here for a moment, I will find a man who
understands the Japanese language.
6) I will telephone for a Japanese speaking man to talk
to you.
7) Please state your nationality, name and address.
8) Your action is liable to create misunderstanding on the
part of the people. I shall accompany you to the Police
Station where I can find a Japanese speaking man to talk
with you.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

SUN SIN MILLS TO RESUME OPERATIONS

After they had been entrusted by the Sun Sin
Textile Manufacturing Company to operate its Nos. 2 and 5
Cotton Mills, the Bank of China and the Shanghai Commercial
Savings Bank inaugurated a Control Committee, while Yong
Erh Zung (葉尔仁 ) was appointed to take charge of the
Mills.
The Mill will register male and female workers
between October 26 and 28 and will formally start operations
on October 29. About 2,300 hands will be employed.
Preparations for a resumption of operations by
the No.5 Cotton Mill on Ward Road are under way.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

MEETING OF SHANGHAI DISTRICT ASSOCIATION

The Shanghai District Association held an urgent
meeting at the Ta Chuan Foh (大全福) Restaurant, Zao Chia
Road, Nantao, at 11 a.m. yesterday. About 80 persons
attended. Zing Nien Yia presided.
After some discussion, certain decisions regarding
the maintenance of peace and order in the district were
reached.

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

申新纺织厂恢复运营

中国银行和上海商业储蓄银行受申新
纺织制造公司委托经营其第二和第五棉
纺厂后，成立了一个管理委员会，并任命

该厂将于10月26日至28日登记男女
工人，并于10月29日正式开工。预计雇
佣约2,300名工人。
华德路第五棉纺厂恢复运营的准
备工作正在进行中。

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

上海区协会会议

上海区协会于昨日上午11时在南市
赵家路大全福餐馆召开紧急会议。约80
人出席。郑念义主持。
经讨论，就维护该区治安达成若干
决定。

October 24, 1936. Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE HAINING ROAD MURDER CASE : JUDGMENT TO BE DELIVERED ON OCTOBER 30.

Chang Yung Woo(張榮和), native of Taichow, a congee hawker, was arrested for concealing in a sand box near Lane 15, Haining Road, a Mauser pistol which had been used in the fatal shooting of a Japanese marine named Taminato on Haining Road near Woosung Road on September 23. He is now being charged in the Shanghai First Special District Court with concealing and destroying evidence, contrary to Art.165 of the Chinese Criminal Code.

The hearing of the case was resumed yesterday afternoon before Judge Tsong Ching(鍾清).

Chang Vung San(張文山), age 60, father of the accused Chang Yung Woo, has engaged two lawyers named Shuan Yoeh Hwa(單毓華) and Ching Chih Ts(金植之) to defend his son.

Chang Ss Tsoh(張師竹), Assistant Municipal Advocate, informed the Court that no developments had taken place during the period of remand.

Questioned by the Court, the accused stated that when he heard the pistol shots, he thought that a fellow provincial named Zang Tai(長太) had been wounded and so he went forward to make an investigation. When he reached a point close to the scene of the crime, his foot kicked against a pistol. He picked it up and concealed it in a sand box with the intention of giving information to the Police later on.

The Judges: After concealing the pistol, did you intend to sell it or to secure a reward or to destroy the evidence for the murderer?

The Accused: I intended to give information to the Police later on. As to the question of a reward, it is matter entirely for the Police. I did not conceal or destroy evidence for others.

The Court then ordered both the prosecution and the defence to submit their arguments.

Assistant Municipal Advocate Chang Ss Tsoh said: "The pistol seized in the case has been established to be the weapon that was used in the shooting of the Japanese marines. The accused has openly admitted to the Police and to the Court that he had concealed the pistol, which fact is further proved by the evidence of Horie and others. There is thus no doubt whatever about his offence. The object of his action is also quite clear because the accused, knowing that the pistol was the murder weapon, had attempted to conceal it. His motive to secure a reward or to sell it does not affect the existence of the offence. The Court is requested to deal with the case in accordance with Article 165 of the Chinese Criminal Code."

Judge to the accused: How long after the pistol shots did you proceed to the scene of the crime?

Accused: About "half a cigarette's time".

《大公报》及本地其他报纸：-

海宁路谋杀案：将于10月30日宣判。

台州籍粥贩张荣和（Chang Yung Woo），因在9月23日于海宁路近吴淞路处一名名为田凑（Taminato，音译）的日本海军陆战队员被枪杀案中，将作案用的毛瑟手枪藏匿于海宁路15弄附近的一个沙箱内而被捕。他目前在上海第一特区地方法院被控犯有隐匿及毁灭证据罪，违反《中华民国刑法》第165条。

该案昨日下午在钟清（Tsong Ching）法官面前复庭审理。

被告张荣和之父、60岁的张文山（Chang Vung San），已聘请单毓华（Shuan Yoeh Hwa）和金植之（Ching Chih Ts）两位律师为其子辩护。

助理市检察官张师竹（Chang Ss Tsoh）向法庭陈述，在还押期间案情并无新进展。

经法庭讯问，被告称，当他听到枪声时，以为同乡长太（Zang Tai，音译）受伤，便上前查看。当他走近案发地点附近时，脚踢到了一把手枪。他捡起手枪并藏入沙箱，打算随后向警方报告。

法官问：藏匿手枪后，你是打算出售、获取赏金，还是为凶手毁灭证据？

被告答：我打算随后向警方报告。至于赏金问题，这完全由警方决定。我并非为他人隐匿或毁灭证据。

法庭随即命令控辩双方提交辩论意见。

助理市检察官张师竹称：“本案中查获的手枪已确认为射击日本海军陆战队员的凶器。被告已向警方及法庭公开承认其藏匿手枪的行为，这一事实另有堀江（Horie，音译）等人的证词进一步证实。因此，其罪行毫无疑问。其行为目的也十分明确，因为被告明知该手枪是凶器仍试图将其藏匿。其动机是为了获取赏金还是出售，并不影响罪行的成立。请法庭依据《中华民国刑法》第165条处理此案。”

法官问被告：枪响后多久你才前往案发现场？

被告答：大约“抽半支烟的时间”。

October 24, 1936.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Morning Translation & REGISTRY.
No. D
Speaking for the defence, lawyer Shuan
Yoch Hwa said: "Article 165 of the Chinese Criminal Code requires circumstance of destruction. The accused is a congee hawker and his intelligence can be easily estimated. According to the statement made by the accused, he concealed the pistol with the intention of securing a reward; he did not intentionally conceal or destroy the evidence. Art. 165 provides the concealment or destruction of evidence in a criminal case in which another person is implicated. There was no other man implicated at the time because the incident had just occurred and the Police had not yet commenced their investigation. Therefore, Article 165 cannot be applied. I request the Court to find the accused not guilty. The accused has a large family all the members of which depend on him for a living. He has been in custody for a long time and even should the Court find him guilty of the charge, the Court is requested to have pity on his ignorance and deal leniently with him."
Procurator Daung Pei Yeu(唐海猷)
requested the Court to deal with the case according to law.
Judge Tsong announced that judgment would be delivered at 2 p.m. October 30.

China Times and other local newspapers :-
THE "OFFER A DAY TO THE COUNTRY" MOVEMENT
The other day the "Lih Pao" suggested an "Offer A Day to the Country" Movement. Later the Standing Committee of the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce passed a resolution supporting the suggestion. The Chamber will take steps to promote the movement. Various public bodies have since expressed their sympathy with the movement.
Yesterday forty-two Chinese factories which had sent goods for exhibition to the Shanghai Native Goods Exhibition and the Native Goods Emporium, the Commercial and Vocational School established by the Chamber of Commerce passed resolutions to enforce the movement and issued manifestoes to that effect.
The Shanghai Citizens National Goods Promotion Association has issued a circular to its members urging them to participate in the movement.

Lih Pao publishes the following article contributed by "Woo Tsoo":
SUPPRESSION OF GUIDE SERVICE AGENCIES
I could not but express my joy when I read in newspapers reports to the effect that the Bureau of Social Affairs was taking steps to suppress the guide service agencies. It is stated that the Bureau will conduct an investigation and will suppress all the guide service agencies, except the bona fide ones. It seems to me that the first step to be taken by the authorities should be to place restrictions upon the advertisements of these agencies for they depend upon advertisements to secure customers. The advertisements include photographs of girl guides and the wording is usually exaggerated. If strict suppressive measures are not taken, then these agencies will continue their improper business to the detriment of the bona fide ones.
Furthermore, guide service is an important contributor to the prosperity of a district, but it should be undertaken concurrently by travel organizations, such as the China Travel Service, etc.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
晨间译件 & 登记处。
编号 D
辩护律师单毓华（Shuan Yoch Hwa）发言称：“《中华民国刑法》第165条要求具备毁灭情节。被告是一名粥贩，其智力水平显而易见。根据被告的供述，他藏匿手枪的目的是为了获取赏金；他并非故意隐匿或毁灭证据。第165条规定的是在涉及他人的刑事案件中隐匿或毁灭证据。当时并未牵涉其他人，因为事件刚刚发生，警方尚未开始调查。因此，第165条不能适用。我请求法庭判决被告无罪。被告家庭人口众多，全家均靠他维持生计。他已被羁押很长时间，即使法庭认定其罪名成立，也恳请法庭体谅其无知，从轻发落。”
检察官唐海猷（Daung Pei Yeu）请求法庭依法处理此案。
钟法官宣布，判决将于10月30日下午2时宣读。

《时事新报》及本地其他报纸：-
“献金一日”运动
日前，《立报》建议开展“献金一日”运动。随后，上海总商会常务委员会通过决议支持该建议。商会将采取措施推动此运动。各界公共团体此后纷纷对该运动表示同情与支持。
昨日，四十二家曾向上海国货展览会及国货商场送展商品的中国工厂，以及由商会创办的商业职业学校，均通过决议执行该运动，并发布了相关宣言。
上海市民提倡国货协会已向其会员发出通告，敦促他们参与该运动。

《立报》刊登了“伍佐”撰写的以下文章：
取缔向导社
当我在报纸上看到社会局正采取措施取缔向导社的报道时，不禁感到欣慰。据悉，社会局将进行调查，除正规合法的向导社外，其余一律取缔。在我看来，当局应采取的第一步措施是限制这些机构的广告，因为它们依赖广告来招揽顾客。这些广告包括女向导的照片，措辞通常夸大其词。如果不采取严格的取缔措施，这些机构将继续进行不正当经营，损害正规向导社的利益。
此外，向导服务是地区繁荣的重要贡献者，但应由旅行社等机构同时开展，例如中国旅行社等。

October 24, 1936.

Shanghai City Government issues proclamation on
Sino-Foreign Relations

The following is a translation of a proclamation issued
by the Shanghai City Government on October 22 over the seal
of Mayor Wu Teh-chen, which was published in the Chinese
press on October 23:-

"Recently cases of misunderstanding and conflict
between the people and foreign residents have occurred in
Chinese controlled territory because of language difficulties
at present time when the country is being confronted
with many difficulties, an imprudent act is liable to give
rise to trouble. In the interests of peace and order,
the people are hereby warned strictly to observe law and
order and not to create trouble. Offenders will be
severely pubished."

October 24, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated October 23 :-

THE LOCAL SITUATION : JAPANESE ACTIVITIES IN CHAPEI

Owing to the fact that during the past few days, Japanese bluejackets in plain clothes have been very active in conducting secret activities and making observations at various places in Chapei, the situation in that area has once more become serious. Japanese have been very active at places within the jurisdiction of the Sin-Zah Branch of the Bureau of Public Safety and of the North Railway Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety, such as Kung Ho Sin Road, Sze Dien Road, Pah Sz Jao, Dung Chi Road and Kingwan Road. When they arrive at a place, they used to note in a book the names of the roads, the telephone numbers and the numbers on the house plates, and sometimes they even take a census. All this has created much uneasiness among the residents. Japanese marines in plain clothes have also conducted similar activities on Chungsan Road, Jessfield Road and at Chenju.

At 9 a.m. to-day (October 23), a large number of Japanese bluejackets and more than 80 military officers arrived at the Japanese Cemetery at Pah Sz Jao in Chapei. Their arrival gave rise to great excitement among the inhabitants. An investigation into the presence of this large number of Japanese bluejackets at that place revealed that October 23 was a date set for the offering of sacrifice to deceased Japanese marines. The Japanese marines withdrew at 11.30 a.m.

During the ceremony, precautionary measures were adopted in the vicinity of the Japanese Cemetery by the police of the two sub-police stations at Pah Sz Jao and near the Rokuson Garden under control of Liang Fu Tsoh, Officer-in-Charge of the North Railway Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety, and many other senior police officers.

Tung Nan Wan Pao dated October 23 :-

Japanese Military Trucks Knock Down A Ricsha

At 7 a.m. October 22, a ricsha (Settlement licence No. 13028 and Chinese territory licence No. 3028) was knocked down at the corner of North Szechuen and Range Roads by two military trucks numbered 6 and 7 of the Japanese Naval Landing Forces. The tyres of the ricsha were damaged.

The drivers of the trucks alighted and slapped the coolie and otherwise assaulted him.

Min Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking Telegram) :-

FACTORY INSPECTION

The Ministry of Industry has already finished its examination of the revised text of the draft agreement for the inspection of factories in Shanghai. The Shanghai City Government has been notified of this and has been instructed to resume the negotiations with the Settlement authorities on the basis of the views of the Ministry and of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

1936年10月24日。晨间译件。

10月23日《华美晚报》：-

本地局势：日军在闸北的活动

鉴于过去几天，便衣日本水兵在闸北各地频繁进行秘密活动和侦察，该地区局势再次变得严峻。日军在公安局辛扎分局（Sin-Zah Branch，音译）和北站公安分局辖区内的各处非常活跃，如共和新路（Kung Ho Sin Road）、四殿路（Sze Dien Road，音译）、八字桥（Pah Sz Jao）、东熙路（Dung Chi Road，音译）和京宛路（Kingwan Road，音译）。他们到达某地时，常在笔记本上记录路名、电话号码和门牌号码，有时甚至进行户口调查。这一切引起了居民的极大不安。便衣日本海军陆战队员也在中山路、极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）和陈家渡（Chenju，音译）进行了类似活动。

今日（10月23日）上午9时，大量日本水兵和80多名军官抵达闸北八字桥的日本公墓。他们的到来引起了居民的极大骚动。经调查这批大量日本水兵出现在该地的原因，发现10月23日是祭奠已故日本海军陆战队员的日子。日本海军陆战队员于上午11时30分撤离。

仪式期间，在北站公安分局局长梁福佐（Liang Fu Tsoh，音译）及许多其他高级警官的控制下，八字桥和六松园（Rokuson Garden，音译）附近的两个分驻所警察在日本公墓周边采取了预防措施。

10月23日《东南晚报》：-

日军卡车撞倒人力车

10月22日上午7时，一辆人力车（租界执照号13028，华界执照号3028）在四川北路与雷恩路（Range Road，音译）转角处，被日本海军陆战队编号为6号和7号的两辆军用卡车撞倒。人力车轮胎受损。

卡车司机下车后掌掴车夫，并以其他方式殴打他。

《民报》及本地其他报纸（南京电通稿）：-

工厂视察

实业部已完成对上海工厂视察协议草案修订文本的审查。已通知上海市政府，并指示其基于实业部和外交部的意见，恢复与租界当局的谈判。

Date 23 / 10 / 36

October 23, 1936. Morning Translation.
Shun Pao and other local newspapers:-

THE HAINING ROAD MURDER CASE

At about 8 p.m. September 23, a First Class
Japanese Seaman named Taminato was fatally shot near Lane 15
at the corner of Haining Road and Woosung Road. Subsequently
members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party arrested a
congee hawker named Chang Yung Woo (張榮和), native of
Taichow, and discovered a Mauser pistol in a sand box by
which he was standing. The prisoner is being charged
by the Police under Article 165 of the Chinese Criminal Code
for concealing evidence.
At the hearing of the case before Judge Tsong
Ching in the Shanghai First Special District Court on
October 9, Chang Ss Tsoh (張師竹), Assistant Municipal
Advocate, requested the Court to make an inspection of the
scene of the crime and to examine the bullet marks on the
wall near the spot.
Judge Tsong has decided that an inspection is
not necessary as the prisoner is being charged with concealing
evidence only and not with the murder of the marine.
furthermore, a clear understanding of the case can be
acquired by a study of the detailed drawings supplied by
the Police together with the photographs taken at the scene
of the crime.
The case will come up for further hearing
before Judge Tsong at 2 p.m. to-day.

1936年10月23日。晨间译件。
《申报》及本地其他报纸：-

海宁路谋杀案

9月23日晚8时许，一名名为田凑（Taminato，音译）的一等日本水兵在海宁路与吴淞路转角处15弄附近被枪击身亡。随后，日本海军陆战队成员逮捕了一名名为张荣和（Chang Yung Woo）的台州籍粥贩，并在他站立的沙箱中发现了一把毛瑟手枪。警方依据《中华民国刑法》第165条以隐匿证据罪起诉该囚犯。
在10月9日上海第一特区地方法院钟清法官审理该案时，助理市检察官张师竹（Chang Ss Tsoh）请求法庭勘察现场，并检查附近墙上的弹痕。
钟法官决定无需勘察，因为囚犯仅被控隐匿证据，而非谋杀海军陆战队员。此外，通过研究警方提供的详细图纸以及在现场拍摄的照片，可以清楚地了解案情。
该案将于今日下午2时在钟法官面前继续审理。

S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 2538.
23 / 10 / 36）

October 23, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao of October 22 :-

ILLEGAL FUNCTIONING BY JAPANESE MARINES IN CHINESE CONTROLLED
TERRITORY : STRONG PROTEST LODGED BY SHANGHAI CITY GOVERNMENT

As members of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party Headquarters have frequently conducted activities in
Chapei, thereby giving rise to misunderstanding and excitement
among the people, the Shanghai City Government has lodged a
very strong protest with the local Japanese Consulate-General,
demanding that the Japanese authorities pay particular
attention to this matter with a view to avoiding further
misunderstanding.

Up to the present, two cases of activities
by Japanese marines in Chapei have been reported, of which the
one that took place on Soong Kung Yuan Road, Chapei, at about
9.45 a.m. October 21 was the more serious of the two and
neither the Chinese nor the Japanese authorities have released
any official statement regarding this affair.

The following are the circumstances surrounding
the Soong Kung Yuan Road incident :-

A brief report regarding this case was
published by newspapers on October 21. Now according to
further information secured by a reporter of this paper, it
appears that on October 21 two Japanese plain-clothes military
officers were noticed loitering along Soong Kung Yuan Road and
Yung Shing Road, Chapei. They were making notes in their
note books. Upon seeing this, the inhabitants became
suspicious and asked them whether they were officials from
the Bureau of Public Safety and why they were not in uniform.
The two Japanese officers made no reply, but when pressed by
the people, they replied in Japanese. As the people did not
understand what the Japanese said and as these two Japanese
had been frequently seen making observation for reasons
unknown, the people surrounded them and insisted on escorting
them to the Bureau of Public Safety, but the two Japanese
officers refused to go. The matter came to the notice of
a Chapei policeman on point duty who immediately proceeded
to the scene and did his utmost to safeguard the two Japanese
officers. He escorted them to the North Railway Station
Branch Bureau of Public Safety followed by a large number
of people.

After he had interrogated the Japanese,
Liang Fu Tsoh, Officer-in-Charge of the Branch Bureau of
Public Safety, intended to send them to the Japanese Consulate
in a motor car under an escort of police officers, but the
two Japanese declined this courtesy. Finally, they were
allowed to leave. Policemen were detailed to escort them
to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters.

Japanese Officials Conduct Enquiries At Scene Of Trouble.

At about 4 p.m. October 21, officials of
both the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters and the
Japanese Consulate conducted an investigation at the scene
of the trouble. Both Liang Fu Tsoh, Officer-in-Charge of the
North Railway Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety, and the
two Japanese military officers in question were present.
Strict precautionary measures were adopted by the Yung Shing
Road Police Station with a view to preventing untoward
incidents. The investigation lasted about 1½ hours.

（批：A-7538）

1936年10月23日）

1936年10月23日。晨间译件。

10月22日《华美晚报》：

日本海军陆战队在华方管辖区域内非法活动：上海市政府提出强烈抗议

鉴于日本海军陆战队总部成员频繁在闸北开展活动，从而在民众中引起误解和骚动，上海市政府已向当地日本总领事馆提出非常强烈的抗议，要求日本当局特别注意此事，以避免进一步的误解。

截至目前，已报告两起日本海军陆战队员在闸北活动的案件，其中10月21日上午9时45分左右发生在闸北宋公园路的一起较为严重，中日双方当局均未就此事件发布任何官方声明。

以下是宋公园路事件的相关情况：

各报于10月21日刊登了关于此案的简短报道。现据本报记者获得的进一步消息，10月21日，有人注意到两名便衣日本军官在闸北宋公园路和永兴路一带徘徊。他们正在笔记本上做记录。居民见此情景心生怀疑，询问他们是否是公安局的官员，以及为何不穿制服。这两名日本军官未作回答，但在民众的逼问下，他们用日语作了回答。由于民众听不懂日语，且此前经常看到这两名日本人出于不明原因进行观察，民众便围住他们，坚持要护送他们去公安局，但这两名日本军官拒绝前往。此事被一名在闸北执勤的警察获悉，他立即赶赴现场，并尽力保护这两名日本军官。他在大批民众的跟随下，将他们护送至北站公安分局。

北站公安分局负责人梁福祚在讯问日本人后，打算派警车并在警察护卫下将他们送往日本领事馆，但这两名日本人拒绝了这一礼遇。最终，允许他们离开。警方指派人员将他们护送至日本海军陆战队总部。

日本官员在事发地点进行调查。

10月21日下午4时许，日本海军陆战队总部和日本领事馆的官员在事发地点进行了调查。北站公安分局负责人梁福祚及涉事的两名日本军官均在场。永兴路巡捕房采取了严格的预防措施，以防发生意外事件。调查持续了约一个半小时。

（批注：A-7538）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 7535
Date ...... / ...... / ......

October 23, 1936. Morning Translation.

It is not known what will be the outcome of this affair as both the Chinese and Japanese authorities have not given out any statement. A reporter of this paper has secured information that the Shanghai City Government has sent a reply to the protest lodged by the Japanese in connection with the incident which occurred at the Wusih Guild on October 16. The reply states that the two Japanese military officers, after looking here and there, walked directly into the Wusih Guild. A small squad of Peace Preservation Corps members stationed in the Guild for the purpose of maintaining peace and order noticed the two Japanese officers who were in plain clothes and who looked like Chinese. As the Japanese were acting in a suspicious manner, the members of the Peace Preservation Corps searched them. The two Japanese never said a word, therefore it was not known that they were Japanese until a small book containing notes about important roads and junctions in Chapei was found on the person of one of them. However, they still failed to mentioned that they were officers of the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters. They refused to disclose their identity even to Liang Fu Tsoh, Officer-in-Charge of the North Railway Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety. When it was discovered that they were Japanese officers, the members of the Peace Preservation Corps ceased their interrogation. The Japanese were then escorted by Liang Fu Tsoh, Officer-in-Charge of the North Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety, to Paoshan at the boundary of the International Settlement where the two Japanese officers were left to proceed on their way. The Shanghai City Government, in its reply, states that the action of the Peace Preservation Corps was reasonable and proper. The City Government also brought to the notice of the Japanese Consulate the gravity of such affairs and urged that every means be adopted to avoid a repetition of such incidents with a view to avoiding misunderstanding. This reply of the City Government was given on October 18, two days after the incident.

After the occurrence of the incident on Soong Kung Yuan Road on October 21, Liang Fu Tsoh, Officer in charge of the North Station Branch of the Public Safety Bureau, had an interview with the Chief of Staff of the Japanese Naval Landing Party. On the afternoon of October 22 Liang went to the City Government to make a report. The Japanese have submitted to the City Government the result of their enquiries into the case, without any comment.

At 10.50 a.m. October 22, Japanese marines held drills in the Hongkew Park. Reports of firearms were heard. Later they were joined by about thirty more marines who came in trucks from Yangtsepoo via North Szechuen Road. The practice lasted one hour after which the marines returned to Headquarters.

The Japanese Brewery behind the Rokuson Garden has been re-occupied by marines. Patrols are being sent out to Dong Chi Road, Ching Yuen Road, Kiangwan Road and other places every day.

There were originally more than 200 Japanese marines at the Kung Dah Cotton Mill, Yangtsepoo. At midnight October 21 a further batch of about 100 marines

10月21日宋公园路事件发生后，公安局北站分局负责人梁福祚会见了日本海军陆战队参谋长。10月22日下午，梁前往市政府汇报。日本方面已向市政府提交了对此案调查结果，未加任何评论。

10月22日上午10时50分，日本海军陆战队员在虹口公园进行演习。听到枪声。随后，又有约三十名陆战队员乘卡车从杨树浦经四川北路加入。演习持续了一小时，之后陆战队员返回总部。

fully armed was sent to the mill in two military trucks.
Five Japanese marines riding in truck No.
8 went to the Civic Centre at 5.30 p.m. October 21. They
moved about for a considerable time and then drove away.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

City Government Issues Proclamation

The Shanghai City Government on October 22
issued the following proclamation :-
"Recently cases of misunderstanding and
conflict between the people and foreign residents have
occurred in Chinese controlled territory because of
language difficulties. At the present time when the
country is being confronted with many difficulties, an
imprudent act is liable to give rise to trouble. For the
sake of peace and order, the people are hereby warned
strictly to observe law and order and not to create trouble.
Offenders will be severely punished.
(Sealed) Wu Teh Chen,
Mayor."

Arrest of Chinese Traitors at Paoshan and Sungkiang

Yesterday the Bureau of Public Safety of
Paoshan arrested a suspicious-looking Chinese named Woo
Tsong Tsang (吳仲章) at a place in Paoshan. He was
found in possession of a strange badge and two pieces of
paper containing the names of several districts together
with the distances from one another. He was strongly
suspected of being a spy and was referred to the Paoshan
Hsien Government to be dealt with.

Whilst conducting a search of passengers
at the Railway Station at Sungkiang on October 20, Loh Yi
(陸倚), a detective of the Public Safety Bureau, and
Huang Yuan Chi (黃允祺), a Police Sergeant attached
to the Second Police Station of the Bureau, noticed a
young man dressed in blue jacket and trousers. Upon being
questioned, the man became confused. A search of his
person resulted in the finding of a piece of Kong Shi
cash, three dice and several articles bearing certain marks.
The young man was taken to the Police
Station and handed over to the Hsien Public Safety Bureau
on October 21.
At a preliminary trial held by Superintendent
Ghui (), the arrested man admitted that he was in
Sungkiang to secure certain information at the instigation
of certain nationals.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

市政府发布告示

上海市政府于10月22日发布如下告示：
“近期，华方管辖区域内因语言障碍，民众与外侨之间屡生误解与冲突。当前国家面临诸多困难，轻率之举易惹麻烦。为维持和平与秩序，特此严正警告民众务必遵守法纪，不得滋事。违者将严惩不贷。
（盖章）吴铁城，
市长。”

在宝山和松江逮捕中国汉奸

昨日，宝山公安局在宝山一地逮捕了一名形迹可疑的华人，名为吴仲章（Woo Tsong Tsang）。在他身上发现一枚奇特的徽章和两张写有几个地区名称及其相互距离的纸条。他因涉嫌为间谍，被移交宝山县政府处理。

10月20日，公安局侦探陆倚（Loh Yi）和该局第二巡捕房警长黄允祺（Huang Yuan Chi）在松江火车站搜查乘客时，注意到一名身穿蓝色夹克和长裤的青年。受到盘问时，该男子神色慌张。对其搜身后，发现一枚孔氏钱币、三颗骰子以及几件带有特定标记的物品。
该青年被带往巡捕房，并于10月21日移交县公安局。
在督察Ghui（原文不清）主持的初步审讯中，被捕者承认他是受某些国民指使，来松江获取某些情报的。

Date 23 / 10 / 36

October 23, 1936.

MAINICHI, NIPPO AND NICHI-NICHI

JAPANESE CONNECTED WITH SPECIAL LANDING PARTY
ASSAULTED BY CHINESE IN CHAPEI

The increase in the number of
plain clothes members of the Chinese Peace Preservation
Corps in Chapei has given rise to trouble every day.
On October 21 persons connected with the Japanese
Special Naval Landing Party were assaulted in Chapei
by several Chinese believed to be members of the Peace
Preservation Corps. The Chinese authorities gave
inaccurate information to the Chinese newspapers in
order to evade their responsibility. A detailed
investigation into the incident brought to light the
following facts:-

At about 9.25 a.m. October 21
as two Japanese in European clothing, who are connected
with the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party were
walking from east to west near a place about 50 metres
west of the intersection of Yung Shing and Sung Kung Yuan
Roads they were suddenly attacked from behind by a party
of two Chinese and a second party of three Chinese. The
attackers snatched away the walking sticks from the
Japanese and assaulted them. The object of the
attack was not robbery. The assailants are believed to
be members of the Chinese Peace Preservation Corps. One
of the Japanese sustained a broken front tooth. These
two men were injured in every part of their body; their
clothing was torn to pieces. At this stage a party of
16 men of the Peace Preservation Corps, including an
officer and two sergeants, arrived on the scene. A
crowd of 200 Chinese loafers had in the meantime collected
at the place. Although the two victims produced their
visiting cards, the Chinese officers and the loafers
turned them away and attempted to take the Japanese to
the Peace Preservation Corps. A patrol of the Bureau
of Public Safety arrived and took them to the West Jukong
Road Branch Police Station where they asked Mr. Yang Chun
Poo, officer in charge of the Station, to allow them to
communicate with Mr. Liang, officer in charge of the
North Railway Station Branch of the Bureau of Public
Safety by telephone but their request was rejected. The
victims were then taken to the Yung Shing Road Branch
Station where they waited about 15 minutes for an
interpreter. Later, the Japanese, in company with the
interpreter, went to the North Railway Branch Bureau
and requested that an investigation be made, but the
request was ignored.

Protest lodged with City Government

It is reported that the Japanese
Special Naval Landing Party will take effective measures
should this violent attitude of the Chinese be continued.
At 3 p.m. October 22 Acting
Consul-General Terasaki called on Secretary Yu of the
Shanghai City Government and lodged a strong protest.

1936年10月23日。

《每日新闻》、《日本新闻》和《日日新闻》

与特别陆战队有关的日本人在闸北遭中国人袭击

闸北中国保安团便衣成员数量的增加每天都引发麻烦。
10月21日，与日本特别海军陆战队有关的人员在闸北遭到几名据信是保安团成员的中国人袭击。中国当局向中国报纸提供了不实信息，以推卸责任。对此事件的详细调查揭示了以下事实：

10月21日上午9时25分左右，两名身穿欧式服装、与日本特别海军陆战队有关的日本人，在永兴路与宋公园路交叉口以西约50米处由东向西行走时，突然遭到后方两组中国人的袭击，第一组两人，第二组三人。袭击者夺走了日本人的手杖并殴打他们。袭击的目的并非抢劫。袭击者据信是中国保安团成员。其中一名日本人门牙折断。这两人全身多处受伤；衣服被撕成碎片。此时，包括一名警官和两名警长在内的16名保安团成员到达现场。与此同时，200名中国闲杂人等聚集在该地。尽管两名受害者出示了名片，但中国警官和闲杂人等将其喝退，并试图将日本人带往保安团。公安局巡逻队赶到，将他们带到西掘港路分巡捕房，他们请求分巡捕房负责人杨春圃先生允许他们通过电话与公安局北站分局负责人梁先生联系，但请求被拒绝。随后受害者被带到永兴路分巡捕房，在那里等待翻译约15分钟。后来，日本人在翻译的陪同下前往北站分局，要求进行调查，但该请求被忽视。

向市政府提出抗议

据报道，如果中国人的这种暴力态度继续下去，日本特别海军陆战队将采取有效措施。
10月22日下午3时，代理总领事寺崎拜访了上海市政府秘书俞先生，并提出强烈抗议。

October 22, 1936. Morning Translation.

Lih Pao :-

THE HAINING ROAD MURDER CASE.

Chang Yung Woo(張荣和), the suspect arrested in connection with the murder of a Japanese marine named Taminato on Haining Road, has been in custody for about a month. The Police have conducted a close investigation into the case and have summoned 28 Chinese and Japanese witnesses to give evidence all of whom, however, have testified that the accused was not the man who fired the shots. As there is no evidence to substantiate a charge of murder against the accused, the Police are prosecuting him on a charge of destroying evidence.

At a previous hearing of the case before Judge Tsong Ching(鍾清) in the Shanghai First Special District Court, the accused stated that he concealed the pistol with the intention of later giving information to the Police so as to secure a reward. The Police disbelieved his statement and requested a remand for further investigation.

It is learned that the case will come up for hearing to-morrow afternoon.

Judge Tsong will make an inspection of the scene of the murder this afternoon. Notice to this effect was sent to the Police last night.

Sin Wan Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking :-

THE SINO-JAPANESE NEGOTIATIONS.

At 3 p.m. October 21, Mr. Kawagoe, the Japanese Ambassador to China, called on General Chang Chun, Minister of Foreign Affairs, to continue the negotiations. The interview ended at 5.20 p.m. As the views of both sides were still too far apart, further parleys will be held.

Mr. Suma Returning To Japan For Instructions.

After returning from the conference with General Chang Chun, Mr. Kawagoe held a conference with Mr. Suma, Counsellor to the Embassy, and other Embassy officials and made a report on his conference with General Chang Chun.

It is reported that Mr. Suma left Nanking for Shanghai by train last night and will leave for Japan by the s.s. Nagasaki Maru to-day (October 22) to make a report to the Foreign Office on the negotiations between General Chang Chun and Mr. Kawagoe and to request for instructions.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

In an interview with newspaper reporters yesterday on board the s.s. Pottsdam, Mr. Sun Fo, President of the Legislative Yuan, who is leaving for Canton, said that he had no information about the fourth conference between General Chang Chun and Mr. Kawagoe. He added that a solution of the present situation lies in North China.

1936年10月22日。晨间译件。

《立报》：

海宁路谋杀案。

因涉嫌在海宁路谋杀一名名为田凑（Taminato，音译）的日本海军陆战队员而被捕的嫌疑人张荣和（Chang Yung Woo），已被羁押约一个月。警方对此案进行了严密调查，并传唤了28名中日证人作证，然而所有证人均证言称被告并非开枪者。由于没有证据支持对被告提出谋杀指控，警方正以销毁证据罪对其提起诉讼。

在上海第一特区地方法院钟清法官此前对该案的审讯中，被告陈述其藏匿手枪是意图日后向警方提供线索以获取赏金。警方不信其言，要求还押候审以便进一步调查。

据悉，该案将于明天下午开庭审理。

钟法官将于今天下午视察谋杀案现场。昨晚已向警方发出相关通知。

《新闻报》刊登如下来自南京的电讯：

中日谈判。

10月21日下午3时，日本驻华大使川越茂拜访外交部长张群将军，继续举行谈判。会谈于下午5时20分结束。由于双方观点仍相去甚远，将进一步举行磋商。

须磨弥吉郎返日请示。

川越茂在与张群将军会谈归来后，与使馆参赞须磨弥吉郎及其他使馆官员举行会议，汇报了其与张群将军的会谈情况。

据报道，须磨弥吉郎昨晚乘火车离开南京前往上海，并将于今日（10月22日）乘坐“长崎丸”轮（s.s. Nagasaki Maru）启程赴日，就张群将军与川越茂之间的谈判情况向外务省报告并请求指示。

《新闻报》及本地其他报纸：

立法院院长孙科昨日在即将启程前往广州的“波茨坦”轮（s.s. Pottsdam）上接受报记者采访时称，他对张群将军与川越茂之间的第四次会谈并无消息。他补充说，解决当前局势的关键在于华北。

"ANOTHER SINO-JAPANESE INCIDENT IN SHANGHAI"
"Two Japanese Military Officers in Clash with People"

"Hwa Mei Wan Pao" published on October 21
the following article under the above headings:-
Another Sino-Japanese incident took place
in Chapei at about 9.45 a.m. to-day (October 21). It
resembled the one that took place on October 16 when two
Japanese plain-clothes officers were found loitering
before the Wusih Guild on Chung Shing Road in Chapei. Both
the Chinese and the Japanese authorities are making discreet
enquiries into the affair. No official report has been
released by the authorities.
According to enquiries made by a reporter
of this paper, the incident took place on Soong Kung Yuen
Road, Chapei. Two Japanese military officers in plain
clothes were noticed loitering at that place for such a
long time that it gave rise to a misunderstanding among
the residents. The two Japanese officers were subsequently
sent away under an escort of Chinese policemen.
On October 20, these two Japanese officers
were noticed at that place conducting an inspection of
the district in the vicinity of the Cheng Kee Soap
Manufacturing Factory on Yung Shing Road. They were
concentrating their attention to the telephone service.
Their presence aroused the suspicions of the residents,
but fortunately nothing happened. When they appeared
again on Soong Kung Yuen Road on October 21, a misunder-
standing arose between them and the residents. Fortunately,
due to protection accorded by the Chinese police, nothing
untoward happened. It is said that the two Japanese
officers were armed with pistols.
According to further information, these
two Japanese officers are members of the local Japanese
Naval Landing Party Headquarters. As they were taking down
the numbers of houses along Soong Kung Yuen Road on the
morning of October 21, the inhabitants became suspicious
because such work is usually carried out by policemen;
moreover the two Japanese officers were in plain clothes.
Consequently, they were questioned, but they gave replies
in Japanese. This aroused the suspicion of the
inhabitants. Upon learning of the affair, policemen
immediately proceeded to the place and asked the two
Japanese to accompany them to the Bureau of Public Safety
or the Japanese Consulate. The request was rejected by
the two Japanese officers who were later allowed to leave.

Following the withdrawal of the Japanese
marine posts from the various strategic points and

greatly improved. However, the situation in Chapei is

marines.
At about 9 a.m. yesterday morning a group
of more than 10 Japanese marines were seen holding drills
in the vicinity of Yue Yuen (岳園) along the Woosung-
Shanghai Railway on Kiangwan Road. The drill lasted
for more than one hour. The Japanese military

“上海又一起中日事件”
“两名日本军官与民众发生冲突”

《华美晚报》于10月21日以以上标题刊登如下文章：
今晨（10月21日）约9时45分，闸北又发生一起中日事件。此事类似于10月16日发生的事件，当时发现两名便衣日本军官在闸北中兴路无锡公会门前徘徊。中日当局均在谨慎调查此事。当局尚未发布官方报告。
据本报记者查询，事件发生在闸北宋公园路。两名便衣日本军官在该处徘徊良久，引起居民误解。随后，这两名日本军官在中国警察的护送下被送走。
10月20日，有人注意到这两名日本军官在该处检查永兴路成记肥皂厂附近区域。他们重点关注电话服务设施。他们的出现引起了居民的怀疑，但幸未发生事故。当他们在10月21日再次出现在宋公园路时，与居民之间产生了误会。幸得中国警察保护，未发生不幸事件。据说这两名日本军官携带手枪。
据进一步消息，这两名日本军官系当地日本海军陆战队总部成员。10月21日上午，当他们在宋公园路记录门牌号码时，居民产生怀疑，因为此类工作通常由警察执行；此外，这两名日本军官身着便衣。因此，居民对他们进行质问，但他们用日语回答。这引起了居民的怀疑。警方获悉此事后立即赶赴现场，要求两名日本人随同前往公安局或日本领事馆。该要求被两名日本军官拒绝，随后获准离开。

随着日本海军陆战队哨位从虹口区各战略要点和十字路口撤出，局势已大为改善。然而，由于日本海军陆战队的活动，闸北局势仍然动荡不安。

At 9.45 a.m. to-day (October 21), a Japanese
military truck with 13 marines left the Japanese Landing
Party Headquarters. It proceeded along North Szechuen
Road to Nanking Road then turned west.
A group of about more than 100 Japanese marines
held drills in Hongkew Park at 3 p.m. October 21.

运输卡车在华元卡（Hwa Yuen Ka，音译）与江湾路日本海军陆战队总部之间繁忙往来。
今晨（10月21日）9时45分，一辆载有13名海军陆战队员的日本军用卡车离开日本海军陆战队总部。该车沿北四川路行驶至南京路，然后向西转弯。

October 21, 1936. Morning Translation.

Shanghai Evening News dated October 20 :-

THE LOCAL SITUATION

The Japanese marines posted at the Japanese Brewery behind the Rokusan Garden were withdrawn at 8 a.m. October 19, but were replaced at noon the same day. When a reporter of the Ta Kung News Agency went there, he saw the marines busily engaged at various duties. Work on the observation tower was undertaken by four marines. Pedestrians in the vicinity were not allowed to approach the place. It seems that the Japanese intend to continue the occupation of the brewery.

The Japanese marines on guard duty at various points in Hongkew were withdrawn on the morning of October 20. Parties of marines, however, were still patrolling Dixwell, Chi Mei, North Szechuen, Chang Tsun, and other roads. Transportation of military supplies was particularly busy between the Landing Party Headquarters on Kiangwan Road and Yangtszepoo.

China Times and other local newspapers :-

The reason why the Japanese marines were withdrawn from the Japanese Brewery on the morning of October 19 was due to the fact that one of the marines suddenly died of some disease which threatened to infect the others. The marines returned to the place in the afternoon after it had been disinfected. There are about 100 marines there.

About 30 to 40 Japanese marines held a drill at 10.45 a.m. October 20 in the Doi Garden on Dong Chi Road (同濟路).

The Chinese Saturday Post, Issue No. 662, published the following comment on October 17 :-

Arming of Chapei Residents Advocated

Since the January 28 incident, the word "exodus" has become a common expression among residents in Shanghai. The recent exodus took place because the enemy, taking advantage of the Haining Road incident, began to post sentries in Chinese controlled territory, construct barracks, instal barbed wire entanglements and send out marine patrols, the sight of which caused such a panic among the residents in Chapei and Hongkew districts that they began to remove into the Settlements.

In view of the tragic experiences which befell residents in Chapei and Hongkew during the hostilities in 1932, this exodus deserves public sympathy, yet one day the writer of this article noticed on Paoshan Road many household removing trucks being held up by policemen. This was not reasonable of the Chinese policemen. In our opinion, the first step in the movement to avert national ruin is to arm Chapei residents to enable them to defend the territory against unexpected attacks if they are to be prevented from removing into the Settlements in times of emergency..

1936年10月21日。晨间译件。

10月20日《上海晚邮报》：

本地局势

10月19日上午8时，部署在六三花园后方日本啤酒厂的日本海军陆战队员被撤走，但同日中午又被替换回来。当大公通讯社记者前往该处时，看到海军陆战队员正忙于各项勤务。四名海军陆战队员从事瞭望塔的施工工作。附近行人不得靠近该处。看来日本人打算继续占领该啤酒厂。

10月20日上午，驻守虹口各要点的日本海军陆战队员被撤走。然而，多股海军陆战队仍在狄思威路、集美路、北四川路、长治路等道路巡逻。军需物资运输在江湾路海军陆战队总部与杨树浦之间尤为繁忙。

《字林西报》及本地其他报纸：

10月19日上午日本海军陆战队员从日本啤酒厂撤出的原因，是因为其中一名陆战队员突然死于某种疾病，该病有传染给其他人的危险。消毒后，海军陆战队员于下午返回该处。那里约有100名海军陆战队员。

10月20日上午10时45分，约30至40名日本海军陆战队员在同济路杜伊花园（Doi Garden，音译）进行操练。

10月17日出版的《中国评论周报》第662期发表如下评论：

主张武装闸北居民

自一·二八事变以来，“逃难”一词已成为上海居民中的常用语。最近的逃难是因为敌人利用海宁路事件，开始在中国管辖领土内设置哨兵、修建营房、安装铁丝网并派出海军陆战队巡逻，这些景象导致闸北和虹口区居民极度恐慌，纷纷搬入租界。

鉴于1932年战事期间闸北和虹口居民的悲惨遭遇，此次逃难值得公众同情，然而本文作者有一天注意到宝山路上许多搬家卡车被警察拦下。中国警察这样做是不合理的。我们认为，避免国家灭亡运动的第一步是武装闸北居民，使他们能够在紧急情况下防止搬入租界时，有能力保卫领土免受意外攻击。
