SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 7538.
Date 17. 10. 1936

3.

October 17, 1936. Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated Oct.16:

THE LOCAL SITUATION

An inspection made by a reporter of this paper this morning shows that about 120 Japanese marines are stationed in the Toyoda Cotton Mill, Chung San Road.

Yesterday afternoon a large number of Japanese military trucks were noticed proceeding in a northerly direction via Avenue Edward VII on their way to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters.

This morning a military truck fully laden with Japanese marines was seen on Nanking Road going in an easterly direction.

The situation in Chapel has been quiet during the past few days. The Hongkew Park seems to have recently become a headquarters of the Japanese marines. The marines gather there every morning and the rifle and gun firing lasts several hours. This is no different from the big manoeuvres now being held by Japanese soldiers in North China.

The marine posts along North Szechuen Road have been increased. At noon to-day a marine was posted on the north side of the Foo Min Hospital and four others were stationed near the Isis Theatre. Additional posts could also be seen in Range Road.

According to a reporter of the Ta Kung News Agency, a group of some 10 Japanese armed marines were noticed installing military telephones in the vicinity of Kiangwan and Wonglo Roads. Another group of six Japanese marines boarded a motor truck and left in the direction of the Tien Tong An Railway Station where they crossed Paoshan Road to Dong Chi Road, Kiangwan Road and Hwa Yuan Ka to inspect the military telephones installed there. A small number of Japanese marines are patrolling Eu Yang Road and Sz Tah Road.

At 11 a.m. to-day about 200 Japanese marines carrying loaded rifles left the Landing Party Headquarters. in groups of four's and marched along North Szechuen Road, Haining Road, Woosung Road and Boone Road to Broadway Road and Yangtszepoo. As they marched they were given the names of streets by the officers.

According to information from the Sin Sin News Agency, 600 Japanese marines, with machine guns, heavy guns and tanks, held a sham fight in Yangtszepoo. They returned to Headquarters at nightfall.

Information secured by the Central News Agency reveals that the Japanese marines and the leaders of Japanese residents in Shanghai have started to form an investigation group to secure full information about every Japanese resident in Shanghai.

1936年10月17日。晨间译稿。

《华美晚报》10月16日讯：

本地局势

本报记者今晨视察发现，约120名日本海军陆战队士兵驻扎在中山路的丰田纱厂内。

昨日下午，有人注意到大量日军卡车沿爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）向北行驶，前往日本海军陆战队总部。

今晨，在南京路上看到一辆满载日本海军陆战队士兵的军用卡车向东行驶。

过去几天，闸北（Chapei）局势平静。虹口公园似乎最近已成为日本海军陆战队的总部。陆战队士兵每天早晨在此聚集，步枪和火炮射击持续数小时。这与目前日军在华北举行的大规模演习并无二致。

北四川路沿线的陆战队岗哨已增加。今日中午，一名陆战队士兵被部署在福民医院北侧，另有四名士兵驻守在伊西斯大戏院（Isis Theatre）附近。在兰路（Range Road）也可看到新增的岗哨。

据大公通讯社记者报道，有人注意到一群约10名武装日本陆战队士兵在江湾路和黄陆路（Wonglo Roads，音译）附近安装军用电话。另一组六名日本陆战队士兵登上一辆摩托卡车，向天通庵火车站方向驶去，在那里他们穿过宝山路到达东熙路、江湾路和华元卡（Hwa Yuan Ka，音译），检查那里安装的军用电话。少量日本陆战队士兵正在欧阳路和施达路（Sz Tah Road，音译）巡逻。

今天上午11时，约200名携带实弹步枪的日本陆战队士兵离开陆战队总部。他们四人一组，沿着北四川路、海宁路、吴淞路和百老汇路（Boone Road）行进至百老汇路（Broadway Road）和杨树浦。行进过程中，军官向他们报出街道名称。

根据申申通讯社的消息，600名配备机枪、重炮和坦克的日本陆战队士兵在杨树浦举行了一次假战斗演习。他们在黄昏时分返回总部。

中央通讯社获得的消息显示，日本陆战队和上海日本居民领袖已开始组建一个调查小组，以获取关于每位在上海的日本居民的完整信息。

No. D 2538
Date 16/10/36
October 16, 1936. Morning Translation.

China Evening News published the following brief comment on
October 15 :-

THE RICSHA PULLERS MUTUAL AID ASSOCIATION.

We have always been opposed to the collection
of contributions from ricsha coolies by the Ricsha Pullers
Mutual Aid Association. If the S.M.C. and the owners are
sincerely solicitous for the welfare of the coolies, they
should generously contribute to a fund instead of levying
contributions from the coolies.
According to a report published in the news-
papers, the S.M.C. has resolved to reorganize the Pullers
Mutual Aid Association and has also adopted the recommendation
of the Ricsha Special Committee that contributions to the
Pullers Mutual Aid Association should no longer be obtained
from the coolies through the owners but by increasing the
ricsha licence fee the proceeds of which the Council may,
at its discretion, earmark as a contribution to the Pullers
Mutual Aid Association.
If this plan is adopted, the Pullers Mutual
Aid Association contributions will ostensibly no longer be
collected from the coolies, but when the Council increases
the ricsha licence fee, the owners will try to make up this
loss by increasing the hire charges and ultimately it will
again be the coolies who will have to bear the burden. The
Council should devise some remedy for this.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE LOCAL SITUATION : JAPANESE MARINES STAGE ANOTHER SHAM
FIGHT.

Between 9 a.m. and 10.30 a.m. yesterday, about
100 Japanese marines held two sham fights on Kiangwan Road, an
extra-Settlement road. They assembled at the Hongkew Park and
moved southward along the Woosung-Shanghai Railway Line to
Wang Loh Road and Tien Tung An Station to make an attack on
the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters. An officer
in the observation tower of the Landing Party Headquarters
directed the operations with flag signals. The attacks
lasted half an hour each.
At 10.50 a.m. five Japanese marines of the
Engineering Corps put up telephone wires at the intersections
of Scott Road and Sz Dah Road and of Dixwell Road and Darroch
Road.
The work of erecting an observation tower at
the Japanese marine post at No.504, at the corner of Chi Mei
Road and Dixwell Road, was completed yesterday. A Japanese
marine was posted on duty in the tower.
In general, the situation is quiet, but more
Japanese patrols are operating on Kiangwan Road, Eu Yang Road,
Chi Mei Road, etc. Japanese marines were again posted for
duty yesterday on Dong Chi Road and Ching Yuin Road. Six
Japanese marines stood on guard at the Kashing Road Bridge.
At 10.15 a.m. yesterday a truck carrying about
30 Japanese marines proceeded along Avenue Edward VII in a
westerly direction. At 3 p.m. two trucks each carrying about
30 Japanese marines proceeded along Nanking Road on their way
to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters on Kiangwan
Road.

日期 1936年10月16日
1936年10月16日。晨间译稿。

《中国晚报》于10月15日发表了以下简短评论：

人力车夫互助会。

我们一直反对人力车夫互助会向人力车苦力收取捐款。如果工部局和车主真诚关心苦力的福利，他们应该慷慨地向基金捐款，而不是向苦力征收捐款。
据报纸报道，工部局已决定改组人力车夫互助会，并采纳了人力车特别委员会的建议，即不再通过车主从苦力那里获取对人力车夫互助会的捐款，而是通过增加人力车执照费，工部局可自行决定将所得款项指定为人力车夫互助会的捐款。
如果采用此计划，表面上将不再从苦力那里收集人力车夫互助会的捐款，但当工部局增加人力车执照费时，车主将试图通过增加租车费用来弥补这一损失，最终负担仍将落在苦力身上。工部局应为此制定一些补救措施。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

本地局势：日本海军陆战队再次举行假战斗演习。

昨天上午9时至10时30分之间，约100名日本海军陆战队士兵在界外道路江湾路上举行了两次假战斗演习。他们在虹口公园集结，沿吴淞-上海铁路线向南移动至王洛路（Wang Loh Road，音译）和天通庵站，对日本海军陆战队总部发动攻击。陆战队总部瞭望塔上的一名军官用旗语指挥行动。每次攻击持续半小时。
上午10时50分，五名日本工兵部队陆战队士兵在斯科特路（Scott Road）与施达路（Sz Dah Road，音译）的交叉口，以及狄克威尔路（Dixwell Road）与达罗克路（Darroch Road）的交叉口架设电话线。
位于吉美路（Chi Mei Road，音译）和狄克威尔路拐角处504号的日本陆战队岗哨搭建瞭望塔的工作于昨日完成。一名日本陆战队士兵在塔上执勤。
总体而言，局势平静，但江湾路、欧阳路、吉美路等地有更多的日本巡逻队在活动。昨天，日本陆战队士兵再次在东熙路和清源路（Ching Yuin Road，音译）执勤。六名日本陆战队士兵在嘉善路桥站岗。
昨天上午10时15分，一辆载有约30名日本陆战队士兵的卡车沿爱多亚路向西行驶。下午3时，两辆各载有约30名日本陆战队士兵的卡车沿南京路行驶，前往江湾路的日本海军陆战队总部。

D.C. (CRIME) / 2538.

October 15, 1936.    Morning Translation Branch

Lih Pao :-

THE LOCAL SITUATION : JAPANESE MARINES STAGE SHAM FIGHT.

At 9.30 a.m. yesterday, about 100 Japanese marines assembled at the intersection of North Szechmen Road and Dixwell Road and for about half an hour they made a mock attack on the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters on Kiangwan Road.

At 2 p.m. about 100 Japanese marines staged a sham fight in the vicinity of the Hongkew Park which lasted about an hour.

At 8.30 a.m. eight Japanese marines patrolled Changchun Road in Chinese controlled territory.

A detachment of Japanese marines is at present stationed in the Tung Wen College, Zikawei. At 10.30 a.m. yesterday, a number of Japanese petty officers, accompanied by marines on motor cycles and in military trucks, left the college and stopped at the corner of Columbia Road and Loh Ka Road. Here they made an inspection lasting about half an hour after which they returned to the college via Avenue Haig.

Shun Pao :-

At 3.50 p.m. yesterday Japanese marines in four trucks and on five motor cycles proceeded along Avenue Edward VII from west to east on their way to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters on Kiangwan Road.

The situation in Chapei yesterday was quiet. No Japanese marines were on patrol on Kiangwan Road, while the Japanese posts along Dong Chi Road have been withdrawn.

Lih Pao publishes the following brief comment :-

THE BOMB AFFAIR IN SWATOW.

Shootings of Japanese have occurred at several places, whilst at others bombs have been found in Japanese shops. With the exception of the Nakayama case, all the other incidents are still unsolved.

The discovery of a bomb in the Koshi Yoko, a Japanese firm in Swatow, has now been solved. It has been established that the bomb had been placed in the shop by the proprietor of the firm.

It seems that the proprietor had incurred a heavy business loss and had placed the bomb in his shop with the intention of doing harm to others. Fortunately, no untoward incident occurred, otherwise it is likely that the case would have become another "international affair".

I wonder whether some of the other unfortunate affairs are not of the same character as that of the Koshi Yoko case.

特别支部档案室。
刑事犯罪科 / 2538。
签发于 1936年10月15日。
（翻译科）

1936年10月15日。    晨间翻译科

《立报》：

本地局势：日本海军陆战队举行假战斗演习。

昨天上午9时30分，约100名日本海军陆战队士兵在北四川门路（North Szechmen Road，原文如此，应为北四川路）和狄克威尔路的交叉口集结，并对江湾路的日本海军陆战队总部进行了约半小时的模拟攻击。

下午2时，约100名日本海军陆战队士兵在虹口公园附近举行了一场假战斗演习，持续约一小时。

上午8时30分，八名日本陆战队士兵在中国管辖区域的长春路巡逻。

目前有一支日本陆战队分队驻扎在徐家汇的文华学院（Tung Wen College）。昨天上午10时30分，数名日本士官在骑摩托车和乘坐军用卡车的陆战队士兵陪同下离开学院，停在哥伦比亚路和罗迦路（Loh Ka Road，音译）的拐角处。他们在此进行了约半小时的检查，随后经海格路返回学院。

《申报》：

昨天下午3时50分，四辆卡车和五辆摩托车上的日本陆战队士兵沿爱多亚路从西向东行驶，前往江湾路的日本海军陆战队总部。

昨天闸北局势平静。江湾路上没有日本陆战队巡逻，东熙路沿线的日本岗哨已撤除。

《立报》发表以下简短评论：

汕头炸弹事件。

多处发生枪击日本人事件，另有一些日本商店发现炸弹。除中山案外，其他事件均未侦破。

汕头日本商行高志洋行（Koshi Yoko，音译）发现炸弹一案现已侦破。经查实，炸弹是该商行店主放置的。

看来该店主遭受了严重的商业损失，并将炸弹放置在自己的商店中，意图伤害他人。幸运的是，未发生不幸事件，否则该案很可能成为另一起“国际事件”。

我想知道其他一些不幸事件是否与高志洋行案性质相同。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, October 14, 1936
7538
15 10 36

Japanese Said
Seeking Control

Hongkew Power Urged.
Chinese Declare;
Exodus Analysed.

Following on the heels of the "demands" presented to the S.M.C. that Japanese men be appointed to the key positions in the Hongkew and Dkywell Road police stations, another movement has been launched to put Japan- ese on the S.M.C. Fire Brigade in these two areas, the reports declare.

Firemen "Ignorant"

The Japanese claim, in a pro- posal made to the S.M.C., that the Chinese firemen on the Bri- gade are "ignorant" of the con- struction of Japanese houses in the Hongkew district and there- fore not competent in times of emergency, it is said.

Chinese evening newspapers seeking to push their sales, news- boys eager to dispose of their copies and the low flying of commercial planes over Shanghai are responsible for the wholesale exodus from Chapei earlier in the month, according to these reports.

News Confusing

It is stated that while the sen- tries posted by the Japanese Naval Landing Party were the chief reason for the "war scare," the evening papers with glaring headlines and "hot news" con- tributed to the general confusion. Everyone, according to the report, was anxious to get a copy of the evening paper, and when they read anything suggestive of war they immediately packed up and left for the Settlement and the French Concession. The news- boys did their share by shouting false reports, which landed several of them behind the bars in the Settlement jails.

During the week, owing to strong winds, the British Com- pany's planes were forced to fly low when approaching their air- port and Chinese residents, who still live in that area, were terror-stricken after hearing the sound of the planes. It is declared, further, that the Japanese were reporting false episodes of that locality and so they immediately started their evacuation to the foreign areas for safety.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH / 14 OCT. 1936 / SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

（批：Jil / 2BR / sch）

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年10月14日，星期三
7538
1936年10月15日

据称日本人
寻求控制权

敦促加强虹口警力。
华人宣称；
分析撤离原因。

继向工部局提出“要求”，任命日本人担任虹口和狄克威尔路警察分局的关键职位之后，据报道，又发起了一场运动，旨在让日本人进入这两个区域的工部局消防队。

消防员“无知”

据说，日本人在向工部局提出的提案中声称，消防队中的中国消防员对虹口区日本房屋的构造“无知”，因此在紧急情况下无法胜任。

据报道，旨在推动销量的中文晚报、急于处理报纸的报童，以及在上海上空低空飞行的商用飞机，是导致本月早些时候闸北大举撤离的原因。

消息令人困惑

据称，虽然日本海军陆战队设置的哨兵是造成“战争恐慌”的主要原因，但刊登醒目头条和“热点新闻”的晚报加剧了普遍的混乱。据报道，每个人都急于得到一份晚报，当他们读到任何暗示战争的内容时，便立即收拾行李前往租界和法租界。报童也推波助澜，高喊虚假报道，导致其中几人被关进租界监狱。

本周，由于强风，英国航空公司的飞机在接近机场时被迫低空飞行，仍居住在该地区的中国居民听到飞机声后惊恐万分。此外，据称日本人报道了该地区发生的虚假事件，因此他们立即开始疏散到外国区域以求安全。

（印：特别支部 / 1936年10月14日 / 上海公共租界工部局警务处）

（批：Jil / 2BR / sch）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 7538
Date 14 / 10 / 36

October 14, 1936.    Morning Translation

MAINICHI

CHINESE SENDS THREATENING LETTER TO JAPANESE

On October 12 a Japanese woman
named Uki Tsukasaki residing at No. 3 Kiangwan Road,
Chapei, informed the Japanese Consular Police that she
had received a letter written in Chinese threatening
that 500 persons will attack her shop and bombs will be
thrown.

CHAPEI REFUGEES RETURNING TO OLD HOMES

Acting on information that
a number of secret organizations were planning to effect
the release by force of the accused in the Nakayama case
after the hearing of the case on October 1, the Japanese
Landing Party adopted precautionary measures against
untoward incidents. Misunderstanding the action of
the Japanese Landing Party, the Chinese residents in
Chapei started to remove into the Foreign Settlements
and the exodus continued up to October 5.
The Japanese Landing Party then
issued a proclamation in Chinese informing the Chinese
people that these measures were taken as a matter of
precaution and advised them to carry on their business
peacefully. The interview between Chiang Kai Shek
and Ambassador Kawagoe took place on October 8 and the
result was reported to be favourable. Consequently,
the people who had removed into the Foreign Settlements
started to return to their old homes on October 9.

NIPPO

TWO VICTIMS IN THE HAINING ROAD SHOOTING
INCIDENT LEAVE FOR JAPAN

First Class sailor Yoshitane
Yawata and Second Class sailor Yoshimi Deriba, who were
wounded in the Haining Road shooting incident on the
evening of September 23, were released from the Japanese
Naval Hospital on October 13. They will leave for
Japan on the Special Service ship "Yoshima" on October
14.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别支部档案室。
编号 D 7538
日期 1936年10月14日

1936年10月14日。    晨间译稿

《每日新闻》

中国人向日本人发送恐吓信

10月12日，居住在闸北江湾路3号的一名名叫 Uki Tsukasaki（音译）的日本妇女向日本领事警察报告称，她收到了一封用中文写的信，威胁说有500人将袭击她的商店并投掷炸弹。

闸北难民返回家园

鉴于有消息称，一些秘密组织计划在10月1日审理中山案后，武力释放被告，日本陆战队采取了预防措施以防不测事件。中国居民误解了日本陆战队的行动，开始搬入外国租界，撤离行动一直持续到10月5日。
随后，日本陆战队发布中文公告，告知中国人民这些措施是出于预防目的，并建议他们安心经营业务。蒋介石与川越大使的会晤于10月8日举行，据报道结果有利。因此，搬入外国租界的人们于10月9日开始返回家园。

《日日报》

海宁路枪击事件中的两名受害者启程前往日本

在9月23日晚上海宁路枪击事件中受伤的一等水兵 Yoshitane Yawata（音译）和二等水兵 Yoshimi Deriba（音译），于10月13日从日本海军医院出院。他们将于10月14日乘坐特种勤务船“吉岛丸”（Yoshima，音译）前往日本。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 2538.
RECD. COMMISSIONER 10/ 36
Date
(CRIME BRANCH)

October 14, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao of October 13 :-

THE LOCAL SITUATION.

Ostensibly, the Japanese authorities are adopting a calm attitude towards the local situation, but in reality they are still actively accelerating their preparations. The strength of the local Japanese landing forces has been increased. At 2.30 a.m. October 13, a Japanese destroyer arrived here with 300 marines. As a matter of fact, since the Hongkew Incident, a large quantity of military supplies and a large number of marines have been despatched to Shanghai from Tokyo.

Although the situation in Chapel has remained unchanged, yet Japanese marine patrols are being sent out every one or two hours, much to the excitement of the people.

Armoured cars, tanks and other cars mounted with machine guns are still being stationed in front of the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters ready for emergencies, while military trucks laden with marines patrol North Szechuen Road, Range Road and Dixwell Road.

According to the Sin Sin News Agency, the marine posts at Jukong Road and Dixwell Road intersections on North Szechuen Road were withdrawn yesterday morning. However, Japanese marines are still stationed on Range Road and Woosung Road corner and at the Kashing Road Bridge. There are still more than 100 marines posted in the Japanese Brewery behind the Rokusan Garden.

The marine post at the Yung Feng Building on North Szechuen Road is still functioning, while the construction of an observation post and the erection of anti-aircraft guns are under way on the roof of the Branch Station of the Japanese Landing Forces at No. 504 Dixwell Road. Japanese marines are still being stationed in the premises of the Japanese Primary School, No. 221 Eu Yang Road, while marine posts were likewise on duty in the vicinity of Lane 226 Dixwell Road. More than 30 Japanese marines were seen yesterday morning holding drills in the Hongkew Park.

Lih Pao :

Fruit Debris Falls On A Japanese Marine : Case Concluded.

Lee Feng Fah(陳分發), a coolie employed by the Shing Lee(勝利) Bakery, 171 Yue Ching Faung(越靖坊), North Szechuen Road, was released at 10.30 p.m. October 12 after having been detained for 15 days by North Szechuen Road Police Station of the Bureau of Public Safety for having carelessly thrown out from a window some fruit debris which fell on a Japanese marine on the night of September 27.

The Haining Road Incident : Cinema Picture Taken.

Yesterday a motion picture was taken of the reconstruction by the Japanese marines in Shanghai of the fatal shooting of a Japanese marine named Taminato on Haining Road.

1936年10月14日。晨间译件。

10月13日《华美晚报》：

本地局势。

表面上，日本当局对本地局势采取冷静态度，但实际上他们仍在积极加速备战。驻沪日本海军陆战队兵力已增加。10月13日凌晨2时30分，一艘日本驱逐舰抵达此处，载有300名海军陆战队员。事实上，自虹口事件以来，大量军需物资和大批海军陆战队员已从东京派往上海。

尽管闸北局势保持不变，但日本海军陆战队巡逻队每隔一两个小时便出动一次，引起民众极大恐慌。

装甲车、坦克及其他装有机关枪的车辆仍停在日本海军陆战队总部前，以备紧急之需，而满载海军陆战队员的军用卡车则在北四川路、靶子路和狄思威路巡逻。

据辛辛新闻社报道，北四川路与掘孔路及狄思威路交叉口的海军陆战队哨所已于昨晨撤除。然而，日本海军陆战队员仍驻扎在靶子路与吴淞路转角处以及嘉兴路桥。六三花园背后的日本啤酒厂内仍有100多名海军陆战队员驻守。

北四川路永丰大楼的海军陆战队哨所仍在运作，而在狄思威路504号日本登陆部队分遣队站址的屋顶上，正在修建观察哨并架设高射炮。欧阳路221号日本小学 premises 内仍有日本海军陆战队员驻扎，狄思威路226弄附近也设有海军陆战队哨位。昨晨有人看见30多名日本海军陆战队员在虹口公园进行演习。

《立报》：

水果残渣掉落砸中一名日本海军陆战队员：案件结案。

李分发（音译），系北四川路越靖坊171号胜利面包店雇用的苦力，因在9月27日晚不慎从窗户扔出一些水果残渣，砸中一名日本海军陆战队员，被公安局北四川路警察局拘留15天后，于10月12日晚10时30分获释。

海宁路事件：拍摄电影画面。

昨日，日本海军陆战队在上海重演了名为田凑（Taminato）的日本海军陆战队员在海宁路被枪杀致死的情景，并拍摄了电影。

October 12, 1936. Morning Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers dated October 10.

THE HAINING ROAD INCIDENT : TRIAL OF SUSPECT

In connection with the incident which took place on the night of September 23 at the corner of Woosung and Haining Roads, in which one Japanese named Taminato was fatally shot and two others named Yawata and Dariba were wounded, three suspects named Chang Yung Ho (張榮和), a congee hawker, Ma Yung Zai (馬永才) and Ma Yung Nyi (馬永年) were arrested by the Japanese Landing Party. The arrested persons were later handed over to the Hongkew Police Station and were arraigned before the Shanghai First Special District Court. Ma Yung Zai and Ma Yung Nyi were released owing to lack of evidence, but Chang Yung Ho, the congee hawker, was detained in custody.

The case against Chang Yung Ho again came up for hearing at the Shanghai First Special District Court at 2 p.m. October 9 before Judge Tsong Ching (鍾清). Procurator Soong Kung San (宋根山) was in attendance. Municipal Advocates Paul Y. Ru (汝德彝) and Chang Sze Tsoh (張師竹) represented the Police. More than ten members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters were present in Court.

In the course of a statement, one of the two Municipal Advocates said: "The accused has admitted to the Police that as soon as he heard the shots on the day of the fatal shooting, he immediately proceeded to the scene from west to east. When he had reached a spot about seven feet from Lane No. 15, his foot kicked against an article on the ground. Picking it up, he found it to be a pistol. He at once threw the weapon into the sand box but was arrested. According to his statement, he had concealed the pistol in the sand box in the hope of securing some reward when he later reported the find to the Police. For this reason, the Police is now prosecuting him under Article 165 of the Criminal Code for destruction of evidence. There are many witnesses in this case; eleven of them did not actually see the shooting. As regards those witnesses who have already made statements to the Police, they can be exempted from interrogation. As regards the witnesses to whom reference will be made to-day, they actually saw the shooting. Their names are Yoshio Kuroda, Tsuneshige Nakayama, Hisamitsu Wakabayashi, Jiro Tanabe, Sadao Yoshida, and a Chinese witness named Chang Liang Pao (張良宝). As regards the remaining witnesses, they are not so important and therefore they can be interrogated later. Medical certificates regarding the two wounded marines and the one who was killed have been issued by Magatake Yoshida and Ogawa, military doctors of the Japanese Landing Party. Photographs of these three Japanese marines are also available, and photographs of the scene of the incident have also been taken on which marks of the shots on the walls at the place of the shooting can be seen. If it is necessary to conduct an inspection of the place, the Court is requested to fix a date for this purpose. 10月10日《民报》及本地其他报纸。

海宁路事件：嫌疑人受审

关于9月23日晚发生在吴淞路与海宁路转角处的事件，一名叫田凑（Taminato）的日本人被枪杀身亡，另外两名叫八幡（Yawata）和达里巴（Dariba）的人受伤，三名嫌疑人——粥贩张荣和、马永才和马永年——被日本海军陆战队逮捕。被捕者随后被移交至虹口警察局，并在上海第一特区地方法院出庭受审。马永才和马永年因证据不足获释，但粥贩张荣和被羁押候审。

针对张荣和的案件于10月9日下午2时在上海第一特区地方法院再次开庭审理，由钟清法官主持。检察官宋根山出庭。公设辩护人汝德彝和张师竹代表警方。日本海军陆战队总部十余名成员出席法庭。

在陈述过程中，两名公设辩护人之一称：“被告向警方承认，在发生致命枪击案当天，他一听到枪声，便立即从西向东赶往现场。当他到达距离15弄约七英尺的地方时，脚踢到了地上的一个物体。捡起一看，发现是一把手枪。他随即将武器扔进沙箱，但随即被捕。据他陈述，他将手枪藏在沙箱里，希望日后向警方报告拾获情况以获取赏金。因此，警方现依据《刑法》第165条以毁灭证据罪对他提起公诉。本案有许多证人；其中十一人并未亲眼目睹枪击过程。至于已向警方作证的证人，可免于讯问。至于今日提及的证人，他们实际目睹了枪击过程。他们的名字是黑田芳雄（Yoshio Kuroda）、中山常茂（Tsuneshige Nakayama）、若林久光（Hisamitsu Wakabayashi）、田边二郎（Jiro Tanabe）、吉田贞夫（Sadao Yoshida），以及一名叫张良宝的中国证人。至于其余证人，他们并不那么重要，因此可以稍后讯问。关于两名受伤和一名死亡的海军陆战队员的医学证明已由日本陆战队军医吉田（Magatake Yoshida）和小川（Ogawa）出具。这三名日本海军陆战队员的照片也已备妥，现场照片也已拍摄，从中可以看到枪击地点墙壁上的弹痕。如果有必要进行现场勘查，请法庭确定日期。”

The pistol that was found at Yue Ching Faung alleyway (餘慶坊) has no connection with this case as a result of an examination made and will therefore not be produced. The nine empty cartridges and the round of spent ammunition that were found at the place of the shooting have been certified by Police experts as having been discharged from the pistol that was picked up from the sand box, and a report to this effect has been made by the experts. It is now produced for the Court's perusal with various other documents."

The first witness whose name is Yoshio Kuroda, a Japanese, said: "On that day, I was out on certain affairs. I first noticed behind me a man about 5 feet 4 or 5 inches in height, dressed in a brown suit of foreign clothing. Later, the man overtook me and walked in front of me. Shortly afterwards, I heard three reports of pistol shots and noticed the man turning to the left into North Haining Road. When he reached the front of a Japanese Church, he hired a ricsha and disappeared towards North Szechuen Road. Afterwards I lost sight of him."

The next witness was a Chinese named Chang Liang Pao, who said: "I am at present working as a boy with a Korean family at House No. 48 North Haining Road. On that night, I saw two men at the scene of the incident: one dressed in a yellow suit of foreign clothing, while the other was clad in a suit of foreign clothing of deep grey. They were walking in front of four Japanese marines. Later, the two men stopped near an electric pole beside the Shanghai Bank, a Japanese concern, while the four Japanese marines passed them. Immediately afterwards, the man who was clad in a yellow suit of foreign clothing drew a pistol and fired two shots. Upon seeing this, I at once ran to my master from lane No. 15 and reported the matter to Macolan, a special police, who resides in Room No. 65 upstairs. Taking his pistol, Macolan immediately ran downstairs to give chase. I know nothing of what followed."

The third witness, a Japanese named Hisamitsu Wakabayashi, said: "On that night I noticed a man dressed in foreign clothing running into Lane No. 15 immediately after he had fired the shots." The witness also stated that the man in question was dressed in a green suit of foreign clothing. As this evidence was contradictory to what had been given by the first two witnesses, the Court instructed the three witnesses to point out an example of the exact colour amongst the clothing worn by the people in Court.

This having been done, another witness, a Japanese named Jiro Tanabe, was called. He said that there were two persons concerned in this case: one was dressed in a grey suit of foreign clothing, while the other was clad in a black short coat.

Sadao Yoshida, the 5th witness, likewise stated that he saw a man dressed in foreign clothing

第一位证人名叫黑田芳雄（Yoshio Kuroda），日本人，他说：“那天我外出办事。我首先注意到身后有一个身高约5英尺4或5英寸的男子，身穿一套棕色西装。后来，该男子超过我走到我前面。不久，我听到三声手枪响，并注意到该男子向左转入北海宁路。当他走到一座日本教堂前时，雇了一辆人力车，向北四川路方向消失。之后我便看不见他了。”

下一位证人是一名中国人，名叫张良宝，他说：“我目前在北海宁路48号一户韩国家庭中做佣童。当晚，我在现场看到两个人：一个身穿黄色西装，另一个身穿深灰色西装。他们走在四名日本海军陆战队员前面。后来，这两人在一家日本商号上海银行旁边的电线杆附近停下，而四名日本海军陆战队员从他们身边走过。紧接着，身穿黄色西装的男子掏出手枪开了两枪。见此情景，我立即从15弄跑回主人家，向住在楼上65室的特别警察麦科兰（Macolan）报告此事。麦科兰拿起手枪，立即跑下楼去追赶。随后的事情我就不知道了。”

第三位证人名叫若林久光（Hisamitsu Wakabayashi），日本人，他说：“当晚我注意到一名身穿西装的男子在开枪后立即跑进15弄。”该证人还称，涉事男子身穿绿色西装。由于这一证词与前两位证人的证词相矛盾，法庭指示这三名证人在法庭人员所穿衣物的颜色中指出确切的颜色示例。

完成此项程序后，传唤了另一位名叫田边二郎（Jiro Tanabe）的日本证人。他说本案涉及两人：一人身穿灰色西装，另一人身穿黑色短外套。

第五位证人吉田贞夫（Sadao Yoshida）同样表示，他看到一名身穿西装的男子

escaping into Lane No. 15 immediately after the shooting.

The Court then summoned Chang Yung Ho,

said: "After I heard the pistol shots, I immediately

suspected of being one of the assassins. Therefore, I
concealed the pistol in the sand box with the intention
of reporting the find to the Police later. However, I
was arrested by the Japanese just as I had concealed

At first, the prisoner stated that he
did this with the intention of securing a reward, but
later he denied having had such an intention.
He was handed for examination the
pistol produced by the Police and was asked whether it
was the one that he had picked up at the place and later
concealed in the sand box. To this, the accused said:
"Yes, it is somewhat similar."
The prisoner had previously stated
that when he heard the pistol shots, he thought that
a fellow-provincial named Yue Zang Tai (俞長泰), a
cooked rice stall keeper, was being wounded, so he rushed
to the place to find out.
The Court then questioned Yue Zang
Tai. In reply to questions, Yue Zang Tai said: "I used
to place my cooked rice stall at a spot about 4 or 5
feet away from the sand box. As I happened to be away
from my stall to purchase hot water at the time of the
shooting, I know nothing about the murder."
Yue Li Sz (俞李氏), wife of the
cooked rice stall keeper, said: "I did not notice what
took place at that time. When Chang Yung Ho came, he
asked me what was the trouble and I told him that I
did not know. Shortly afterwards I saw him arrested
by some person. Just at that moment, some one bumped
into me, but I do not know who the man was."
Judge Tsong remanded the case till
the afternoon of October 23. He stated that a date
would be fixed for an inspection of the scene of the
shooting.

有人撞了我一下，但我不知道那人是谁。”
钟法官将案件延期至10月23日下午。

1936年10月12日。晨间译件。

枪击发生后立即逃入15号弄堂。
田边次郎（Jiro Tanabe）和吉田贞夫（Sadao Yoshida）已明确陈述，
刺客是中国人，鉴于东方人的肤色 somewhat alike（ somewhat alike 意为“有些相似”，此处依语境译为“颇为相近”），且刺客当时身着西式服装，法庭随即询问他们是以何种方式认定刺客为中国人的。

对此，田边和吉田称，他们在识别中国人方面拥有特殊经验。
法庭随后传唤被告张永和（Chang Yung Ho）进行讯问。

在回答提问时，囚犯说：“听到枪声后，我立即赶往事发现场。途中，我踢到了一把手枪。我当时非常惊恐和激动，如果我立刻拿着手枪去警察局报告拾获情况，我担心自己会被怀疑是刺客之一。因此，我将手枪藏在沙箱里，打算稍后向警方报告拾获情况。然而，就在我将手枪藏入沙箱时，我被日本人逮捕了。”

起初，该囚犯声称他这样做是为了获取赏金，但后来他否认有此意图。

警方出示了那把手枪供其查验，并问他这是否就是他在现场捡起并随后藏在沙箱里的那一把。对此，被告说：“是的，有点相似。”

该囚犯此前曾陈述，当他听到枪声时，他以为是一位名叫俞长泰的同乡、一位熟饭摊贩受了伤，所以他赶到现场去查看。

法庭随后讯问了俞长泰。在回答提问时，俞长泰说：“我通常将我的熟饭摊设在距离沙箱约4或5英尺的地方。由于枪击发生时我恰好离开摊位去买热水，我对这起谋杀案一无所知。”

熟饭摊贩之妻俞李氏（Yue Li Sz）说：“我当时没有注意到发生了什么。当张永和来时，他问我出了什么事，我告诉他我不知道。不久后，我看见他被某人逮捕。就在那时，有人撞了我一下，但我不知道那人是谁。”

曾法官（Judge Tseng）将案件延期至10月23日下午审理。他表示，将确定一个日期对枪击现场进行勘验。

October 9, 1936. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE LOCAL SITUATION : STERN WARNING TO RUMOUR-MONGERS.

General Yang Hu, Commissioner of the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Headquarters, issues the following notification to-day, October 9 :-
"In Shanghai are to be found people of various nationalities; every grade of society is represented. Undesirables and reactionaries frequently take advantage of local conditions to spread rumours and seditious reports to the menace of the peace and order of the locality. This Headquarters is responsible for the maintenance of peace and order in Woosung and Shanghai. Whoever is found, after the promulgation of this notification, spreading rumours affecting the order of the district will be subject to immediate arrest and be severely dealt with. Apart from instructing the military and police authorities to keep a sharp look-out for such elements, this notification is hereby published for general information. The people should remain calm and attend to their respective businesses peacefully and pay no heed to sensational reports."

Protest Against Presence Of Japanese Marines In Chapel.

During the past few days, Japanese marines have been despatched by the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters to patrol Tien Tung Road, Soo Chin Kong Road, Feng Siu Miao, Ho Ka Mou Jao and various other districts in Chinese controlled territory under the pretext of affording protection to Japanese residents. As these districts are within the jurisdiction of the Shanghai City Government and as this action on the part of the Japanese marines constitutes a violation of our administrative rights, it is learned that the Shanghai City Government has lodged a further protest with the local Japanese Consul-General and has demanded that the Japanese Naval Authorities be notified to cease dispatching marines for patrol in Chinese controlled territory.

China Evening News of October 8 published the following comment:-

"China's Tether Is Near Its End"

It has always been the policy of the "London Times", the organ of the British Conservative Party, to support Japan so as to preserve Britain's vast interests in the Far East. Yesterday this paper suddenly changed its tone and strongly criticised Japan's aggressive activities in China. This is a matter truly worthy of attention.
The "Times" says :-
"Japan can expect little sympathy and nothing more concrete than sympathy until her much-vaunted altruism in Asia is shown to be something better than perfunctory disguise. ----- The murder of half a dozen Japanese on Chinese territory is, indeed, regrettable, but it is impossible to forget that, five years ago, the Japanese Army was engaged in killing Chinese citizens on Chinese territory as

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER S.S.M.P. (CRIME BRANCH)）

1936年10月9日。晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

本地局势：严厉警告造谣者。

吴淞上海警备司令部司令杨虎将军于今日，10月9日，发布如下通告：-
“上海汇聚各国人士，社会各阶层皆有代表。不良分子及反动派常利用本地局势散布谣言及煽动性报道，危害地方治安与秩序。本司令部负责维持吴淞及上海的治安与秩序。自本通告颁布之日起，凡被发现散布影响地区秩序之谣言者，将立即予以逮捕并严加惩处。除指令军警当局对此类分子严加监视外，特发布此通告以广周知。民众应保持冷静，安居乐业，勿听信耸人听闻之报道。”

抗议日本海军陆战队出现在教堂。

过去数日，日本海军陆战队总部以保护日本居民为借口，派遣日本海军陆战队巡逻天通庵路（Tien Tung Road）、苏家宅路（Soo Chin Kong Road）、丰寿庙（Feng Siu Miao）、何家木桥（Ho Ka Mou Jao）及中国管辖区域内的其他多个地区。鉴于这些地区属于上海市政府管辖范围，且日本海军陆战队的这一行动构成了对我国行政权的侵犯，据悉上海市政府已向当地日本总领事提出进一步抗议，并要求通知日本海军当局停止派遣海军陆战队在中国管辖区域内巡逻。

10月8日的《China Evening News》（英文报名，暂保留或译为《中国晚报》）发表如下评论：-

“中国的忍耐已近极限”

作为英国保守党机关报的《伦敦泰晤士报》，其一贯政策是支持日本，以维护英国在远东的巨大利益。昨日该报突然改变语调，强烈批评日本在华的侵略活动。这确实是一件值得注意的事情。
《泰晤士报》称：-
“在日本将其在亚洲大肆吹嘘的利他主义证明为不仅仅是敷衍的伪装之前，她很难指望得到同情，更不用说比同情更具体的支持了。----- 在中国领土上谋杀六名日本人，确实令人遗憾，但人们无法忘记，五年前，日本军队曾在中国领土上尽可能快地杀害中国公民，

（印：苏州河以南警务处副处长（刑事科））

fast as it conveniently could. The casualty lists in Manchuria have not yet been closed, though most of the indigenous dead may be classed as bandits.
------ If Japan persists in being overbearing and exorbitant, China's leaders will revolt at being frog-marched farther. Once passive resistance becomes an armed forlorn hope - a contingency not inordinately remote - Japan must accept the consequences."
This declaration of the "London Times" represents the opinion of the majority of British people; it is a reaction to Japan's boundless ambition which is endangering British interests in Central and South China. Should Japan adopt a more conciliatory attitude, Britain will become sympathetic to Japan. For this reason, we do not attach much importance to the criticism of the "Times" of "Japan's much-vaunted altruism and perfunctory disguise", but the other passages of the article we have quoted merit serious attention.
During the past five years, countless Chinese people in the North-Eastern Provinces have been killed as "bandits". Now when only six Japanese have been murdered in Chinese territory, Japan adopts a "particular line of attack". There is no doubt that the British people are thinking that the negotiations now in progress will be entirely irrelevant to the original agenda.
China's leaders are carrying out the negotiations with the greatest forbearance. The people of China will never accept any demand which will lead to loss of even an inch of territory or a fraction of their sovereign rights. As the "Times" says, "Japan has got somewhere near the end of China's tether."

Lih Pao :-

Arrest of Spies

At about 2 p.m. October 7, the Peace Preservation Corps at Ta Zang (大場) arrested in front of its Headquarters two persons named Yang (楊) and Kwoh (郭), who are believed to be traitors to secure information. It is said that they are stable boys of the Kiangwan Race Course. They are now being detained at the Ta Zang Headquarters of the Peace Preservation Corps.
Shortly after 10 a.m. yesterday when a certain member of the Peace Preservation Corps at Kaochongmiao (高昌廟) was returning to duty, he noticed a man, dressed in ragged clothing, loitering about and making enquiries about the strength of the Peace Preservation Corps. As the man's behaviour was suspicious, the officer searched the man and found a pencil and a sheet of paper on which the names and directions of the various streets at Kaochongmiao had been marked down. The man was taken to the Headquarters of the Corps.
The following letter of correction from the Secretariat of the Kiangsu Provincial Government appears in to-day's "Shun Pao":-
"The report published in your paper on Oct. 7 to the effect that emergency measures had been adopted in various Hsiens in the vicinity of Shanghai is untrue. Please make a correction."

只要方便便大肆杀戮。满洲的伤亡名单尚未终结，尽管大多数当地死者可能被归类为匪徒。
------ 如果日本继续恃强凌弱、贪得无厌，中国领导人将反抗被进一步牵着鼻子走。一旦被动抵抗变成武装的孤注一掷——这种可能性并非遥不可及——日本必须承担后果。”
《伦敦泰晤士报》的这一声明代表了大多数英国人的观点；这是对日本危及英国在华中和华南利益的无限野心的反应。如果日本采取更为缓和的态度，英国将对日本表示同情。因此，我们并不十分重视《泰晤士报》对“日本大肆吹嘘的利他主义和敷衍伪装”的批评，但我们引用的文章其他段落值得认真关注。
在过去五年中，东北各省无数中国人被作为“匪徒”杀害。现在，当仅有六名日本人在中国领土上被谋杀时，日本却采取了“特别的攻击路线”。毫无疑问，英国人认为正在进行的谈判将与最初的议程完全无关。
中国领导人正以最大的克制进行谈判。中国人民绝不会接受任何导致丧失哪怕一寸领土或丝毫主权的的要求。正如《泰晤士报》所说，“日本已接近中国忍耐的极限。”

《立报》：-

逮捕间谍

10月7日下午2时许，大场保安团在其总部前逮捕了两名姓杨和姓郭的人，据信他们是刺探情报的汉奸。据说他们是江湾赛马场的马夫。他们目前被拘留在大场保安团总部。
昨天上午10点后不久，高昌庙保安团的一名成员在返岗途中，注意到一名衣衫褴褛的男子在附近徘徊，并打听保安团的兵力情况。由于该男子行为可疑，警官对其进行了搜身，发现了一支铅笔和一张纸，纸上标记了高昌庙各条街道的名称和方向。该男子被带往保安团总部。
今日《申报》刊登了江苏省政府秘书处发出的如下更正函：-
“贵报10月7日刊载的关于上海周边各县已采取紧急措施的报道不实。请予更正。”

Correction

The following letter of correction from the Secretariat of the Kiangsu Provincial Government appears in to-day's "Shun Pao":-
"The report published in your paper on October 7 to the effect that emergency measures had been adopted in various Hsiens in the vicinity of Shanghai is untrue. Please make a correction."

Min Pao:

The Nakayama Case: Appeal to be Filed

In connection with the murder of the Japanese marine named Hideo Nakayama, Yang Vung Tao and Yih Hai Sung alias Siao Kwangtung have been sentenced to death by the Shanghai First Special District Court, while Tseu Shou Yong, the third accused, has been acquitted. During the period of appeal, Yang Vung Tao and Yih Hai Sung have been removed to the Ward Road Gaol for detention. Yang Tong Sz, the wife of the accused Yang Vung Tao, has already instructed Tong Wei Chuin and other lawyers to file an appeal with the Kiangsu 2nd Branch High Court. Unaware of this fact, Yang Vung Tao the other day informed the Governor of Gaols that he would file an appeal and requested him to draw up the grounds of appeal on his behalf.
At 2 p.m. yesterday, Tong Wei Chuin and Kuo Chi Ming, lawyers for the defence of Yang Vung Tao, called on him at the gaol in order to obtain from him his grounds of appeal. They were given a verbal account of the grounds of appeal by Yang Vung Tao in the presence of a warder. It is learned that the two lawyers will file an appeal. Yang Vung Tao informed his lawyers that he was being well treated in Gaol.

Lih Pao:

Trial of Suspect in Haining Road Murder

On the evening of September 23 a Japanese marine named Taminato was murdered and two others wounded on Haining Road. Ma Yung Zai (马永才), Ma Yung Nien (马永年) and Chang Yung Woo (张永和) were arrested the same evening at the scene of the crime. As the evidence against Ma Yung Zai and Ma Yung Nien was insufficient, they have been released.
As regards the man Chang Yung Woo, 25 Japanese witnesses have come forward to give their statements to the Police; he is therefore being accused as the actual murderer. These witnesses have declared that the pistol which was found in the No.16 sand box at the back entrance of the Shanghai Bank, a Japanese concern, had been thrown there by Chang Yung Woo.
The case against Chang Yung Woo will be heard at 2 p.m. to-day. The 25 Japanese witnesses will give evidence, while one Zang Tai (常泰) and his wife will testify for the defence.

《民报》：

中山案：将提起上诉

关于日本海军陆战队士兵中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）被谋杀一案，上海第一特区地方法院判处杨云涛（Yang Vung Tao）和叶海松（Yih Hai Sung，别名小广东 Siao Kwangtung）死刑，第三被告周守庸（Tseu Shou Yong）无罪释放。在上诉期间，杨云涛和叶海松已被移送提篮桥监狱羁押。被告杨云涛之妻杨童氏（Yang Tong Sz）已委托董维钧（Tong Wei Chuin）等律师向江苏高等法院第二分院提起上诉。杨云涛不知此事，日前告知监狱长他将提起上诉，并请监狱长代为起草上诉理由书。
昨日下午2时，杨云涛的辩护律师董维钧和郭志明（Kuo Chi Ming）前往监狱会见他，以获取其上诉理由。杨云涛在狱警在场的情况下口头陈述了上诉理由。据悉，两位律师将提交上诉状。杨云涛告知其律师，他在监狱中受到良好待遇。

《立报》：

海宁路谋杀案嫌疑人受审

9月23日晚，一名名为田凑（Taminato，音译）的日本海军陆战队士兵在海宁路被谋杀，另有两人受伤。马永才、马永年和张永和于当晚在现场被捕。由于针对马永才和马永年的证据不足，他们已被释放。
关于张永和一人，已有25名日本证人向警方提供证词；因此他被指控为实际凶手。这些证人宣称，在上海银行（一家日资企业）后门入口处的16号沙箱中发现的手枪，是张永和扔在那里的。
针对张永和的案件将于今天下午2时开庭审理。25名日本证人将出庭作证，而一名叫常泰（Zang Tai）的人及其妻子将为辩方作证。

October 9, 1936.

NICHI NICHI

MORE POWER FOR JAPANESE POLICE OFFICERS DESIRED.

At noon yesterday the Foreign Affairs Negotiations Committee of the Japanese Residents Corporation held a meeting to consider Municipal Police affairs.

The S.M.P. has Deputy Commissioners, Assistant Commissioners and Superintendents who assist Commissioner Gerrard in administering Police affairs. There is, however, a big difference in the authority held by the British officers and that held by the Japanese officers for the authority of the latter is limited to control of the Japanese Branch only. Thus in times of emergency the Japanese officers will not be able to issue orders to European or Chinese officers. For this reason, the Japanese officers should be given the same power as that held by the British officers.

The meeting decided that the Committee should study further the matter.

The meeting also suggested that the number of Japanese detectives be increased and that more detectives be detailed to localities where the Japanese population is very dense and that police boxes be erected at places where many Japanese reside so as to prevent a recurrence of incidents.

The meeting further declared that Japanese should be attached to the Fire Stations in areas where many Japanese reside.

MAINICHI, NIPPO AND NICHI NICHI

CHINESE SENDS THREATENING LETTER TO JAPANESE.

On the evening of October 6 a Japanese midwife named Nao Hayashita, age 39, residing in Lane 82, House 9, Hannen Road, received by post the following anonymous letter in Chinese :-
"You, Nao Hayashita, are a Japanese devil. We cannot forget your action against us. No mercy will be shown to you. I openly warn you that we will not tolerate your dirty action. No reason will be given to you regarding the danger to your life. We shall make you a second Kayau case."

1936年10月9日。

《日日新闻》

要求赋予日本警官更大权力。

昨日中午，在沪日侨民会外事交涉委员会召开会议，审议工部局警务事宜。

上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）设有副总监、助理总监及督察长，协助总监吉拉德（Gerrard）管理警务。然而，英籍警官与日籍警官所持权限存在巨大差异，后者的权限仅限于管辖日本分部。因此，在紧急情况下，日籍警官无法向欧籍或华籍警官发布命令。鉴于此，应赋予日籍警官与英籍警官同等的权力。

会议决定，委员会应进一步研究此事。

会议还建议增加日籍侦探的人数，并向日侨人口非常密集的地区增派更多侦探，且在日侨聚居地设立警察岗亭，以防止事件再次发生。

会议进一步声明，在日侨聚居地区的消防站应配备日籍人员。

《每日新闻》、《日本新闻》及《日日新闻》

华人向日侨寄送恐吓信。

10月6日晚，居住在汉璧礼路82弄9号、39岁的日本助产士林下直（Nao Hayashita，音译）收到一封中文匿名信，内容如下：
“你，林下直，是个日本鬼子。我们无法忘记你对我们的所作所为。绝不会对你手下留情。我公开警告你，我们不会容忍你的肮脏行径。关于你生命的危险，我们不会给你任何理由。我们将让你成为第二个‘加藤案’（Kayau case，原文如此）。”

October 8, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

The Social Daily News (社会日报) published the following comment on October 7 :-

THE QUESTION OF SAFETY IN THE SETTLEMENT

The other day there appeared in the Readers' Forum of the "Lih Pao" a letter stating that the International Settlement of Shanghai, which had always been regarded by a certain section of the Chinese people as a place of safety, has, during the past few years, become a place of insecurity, especially in view of the fact that the Chinese residents in the Settlement are frequently subjected to unreasonable oppression and arrest. The authorities of the International Settlement, the letter further states, cannot evade their responsibility for this state of affairs.

In reply to these remarks, the editor of the "Lih Pao" wrote: "Mr. Fessenden, Secretary-General of the S.M.C., has already made a reply to such complaints by saying that the authorities of the International Settlement have no right to open negotiations and have therefore decided to submit a report to the Consular Body. What will be the result of such a report to the Consular Body? We dare predict that it will have no result at all. The action of the authorities in permitting a certain nation to make use of the International Settlement as a base during the January 28 incident proves this. For this reason, it will be only a dream if Chinese think that the authorities of the International Settlement would devise ways and means to deal with such affairs."

This comment is vague and incomplete. The Foreign Settlements are regarded as a place of safety by a section of the servile high class Chinese only. According to the Treaties, a Settlement is a place allotted for the residence of foreigners, wherein the inhabitants are all subject to the jurisdiction of the Chinese Government. This rule was clearly specified in the Yangkingpang Regulations. For instance, in December 1848, when the American flag was hoisted above the premises of the American Consulate in the Settlement, the British Consul sent a despatch to the then Taotai of Shanghai stating that the Settlement was not American territory and therefore no American flag should be allowed to be hoisted. From this, we can see that the British people have no doubt about the status of the Settlement. At the close of the Tsing Dynasty, the then Chairman of the S.M.C. advocated that Shanghai be converted into a free port, but the proposal was turned down by the then British Minister to China, who, in his reply to the British Consul, said: "Although foreigners have the right of administration in the Settlements which are located in China, yet the territory wherein such Settlements are located still belongs to China and cannot be monopolized by the westerners. It is, therefore, impossible to convert Shanghai into a free port, especially in view of the fact that the Chinese Government has not relinquished its right of jurisdiction over the Chinese, nor has the British Government the right to demand of the Chinese Government protection for the Chinese people residing in the Settlement."

《社会日报》于10月7日发表如下评论：

租界的安全问题

日前，《立报》读者论坛刊登了一封信，指出上海公共租界一向被部分中国人视为安全之地，但在过去几年中，已变得不再安全，特别是考虑到租界内的中国居民经常遭受不合理的压迫和逮捕。该信进一步指出，公共租界当局对此种状况难辞其咎。

针对这些言论，《立报》编辑写道：“工部局秘书长费森登（Fessenden）先生已对此类投诉作出答复，称公共租界当局无权就此开启谈判，因此决定向领事团提交报告。向领事团提交此类报告会有什么结果？我们敢预言，这将毫无结果。当局在一·二八事变期间允许某国利用公共租界作为基地的行为，证明了这一点。因此，如果中国人认为公共租界当局会想方设法处理此类事务，那不过是痴人说梦。”

此评论含糊且不完整。只有部分奴性十足的中国上层阶级才将外国租界视为安全之地。根据条约，租界是划供外国人居住的地方，其中的居民均受中国政府管辖。这一规则在《洋泾浜章程》中有明确规定。例如，1848年12月，当美国国旗在租界内的美国领事馆 premises 升起时，英国领事向当时的上海道台发送照会，指出租界并非美国领土，因此不应允许悬挂美国国旗。由此可见，英国人对租界的地位毫无疑问。清朝末年，时任工部局总董主张将上海改为自由港，但该提议被当时的英国驻华公使驳回，他在回复英国领事时表示：“虽然外国人在位于中国的租界内拥有行政管理权，但租界所在的领土仍属于中国，不能被西方人垄断。因此，不可能将上海改为自由港，特别是考虑到中国政府并未放弃对华人的管辖权，且英国政府也无权要求中国政府保护居住在租界内的中国人。”

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. REGISTRY.
No. D. 7538
October 8, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

All this clearly indicates the status of
the International Settlement. The privilege enjoyed by
the S.M.C. in levying taxes upon Chinese is not based on
treaties but on a practice which was encouraged in the
past by a small section of high class Chinese who, in
their anxiety to seek shelter, regarded the Settlement
as a place of safety during times of civil war. But a
privilege which has been so easily secured can likewise
be easily lost. Take, for instance, the unreasonable
oppression and arrest of Chinese by the nationals of
a certain country. It is true, as Mr. Fessenden has
stated, that the S.M.C. has no right to open negotiations
over such affairs.
We predict that in the event of Sino-Japanese
relations taking a turn for the worse, thereby placing
the S.M.C. in a more difficult and embarrassing position
in the exercise of its administration, the Settlement
will revert to its original status, that is to say, the
S.M.C. will have to exercise its administration strictly
in accordance with the provisions of the Yangkingpang
Regulations and the Chinese people will not be allowed
to reside in the International Settlement.
We emphasize that it is the Shanghai City
Government and not the S.M.C. that is responsible for the
safety of Shanghai residents. We should not rely upon
the S.M.C. for protection.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-
THE DOUBLE TENTH ANNIVERSARY.
October 10 being the 25th Anniversary of the
Republic of China, the local Tangpu will convene at 10 a.m.
on that day a meeting of representatives of various local
public bodies at the People's Education Institute, Wen Miao
Road, Nantao, to celebrate the occasion. Newspaper offices,
banks, the Customs, the Post Office, the Courts, the large
factories and business firms will observe the day as a
holiday. The national flag will be hoisted throughout
the district.
In view of the present tense situation and
the prevalence of rumours, the police authorities of Chinese
controlled territory and Foreign Settlements will adopt
precautionary measures on that day.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-
MOVE TO PREVENT INCREASE IN RICE PRICES.
With a view to putting a stop to the rapid
increase in the price of rice, the local Social Bureau at
10 a.m. yesterday summoned rice dealers to a meeting presided
over by Fan Kung Chai, Commissioner of the Bureau.
The following decisions were reached :-
(1) That the Social Bureau instruct the various Rice Dealers
Associations to prohibit any increase in the price of
rice.
(2) That the Shanghai City Government be petitioned to place
a ban on the exportation of rice.
(3) That the Social Bureau detail officers to conduct an
investigation into the amount of rice in stock in
Shanghai.

1936年10月8日。下午译文。

所有这些清楚地表明了
公共租界的地位。工
部局向华人征税的特权并非基于
条约，而是基于一种惯例，这种惯例在过去受到
一小部分中国上层阶级的鼓励，他们
出于寻求庇护的迫切心理，在内战时期将
租界视为安全之地。但是，如此轻易获得的
特权同样容易丧失。以某国国民对
华人的不合理压迫和逮捕为例。费森登
先生所言属实，即工
部局无权就此类事务开启谈判。
我们预测，一旦中日
关系恶化，从而使
工部局在行使行政管理时处于更加困难和尴尬的境地，租界
将恢复其原始状态，也就是说，
工部局将必须严格按照《洋泾浜章程》的规定
行使行政管理权，且不允许
中国人在公共租界内居住。
我们要强调，对上海居民的安全负责的是
上海市政府，而非工
部局。我们不应依赖
工部局提供保护。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：
双十节纪念。
10月10日是中华民国成立25周年纪念日，当地党部将于当日上午10时在南市文庙路民众教育馆召开各地方公共团体代表会议，以庆祝这一时刻。报社、银行、海关、邮局、法院、大型工厂和商号将放假一天。全区将悬挂国旗。
鉴于当前局势紧张及谣言盛行，华界及外国租界的警察当局将在当天采取预防措施。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：
防止米价上涨的措施。
为了制止米价快速上涨，当地社会局于昨日上午10时召集米商开会，由该局局长范公柴（Fan Kung Chai，音译）主持。
达成以下决定：
(1) 社会局指令各米业公会禁止提高米价。
(2) 请愿上海市政府禁止大米出口。
(3) 社会局派遣官员调查上海的库存大米数量。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 7538.
Date 8. / 10. / 36

October 8, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

NIPPO

JAPANESE WANT S.M.C. TO ENGAGE MORE JAPANESE

As the lives and property of Japanese residents have been seriously menaced by recent incidents, the Japanese Residents Corporation on October 3 sent a letter to the Japanese Consulate-General requesting him to move the S.M.C. to expand the Detective Department of the S.M.P. and to appoint Japanese officers to take charge of Hongkew Station, Dixwell Road Station and Yangtszepoo Station.
To-day the Foreign Affairs Negotiations Committee of the Japanese Residents Corporation will hold a meeting to consider the engagement of more Japanese to important positions in the various departments of the S.M.C. as the Japanese have the largest population in Shanghai and better treatment of Japanese by the S.M.C. as Japanese employees are receiving less favourable treatment than the European staff.

NICHI-NICHI

ACTIVITIES OF ANTI-JAPANESE DRAMATIC GROUPS

The Zuh Nyi Small Dramatic Group and the Mo Ni("Ants") Dramatic Group have been suppressed by the authorities.
The Mo Ni("Ants") Dramatic Group has been dissolved by its members who have now formed a Comedy Club with a view to uniting the front of dramatic circles against Japan.

《日本新闻》

日本人要求工部局雇佣更多日本人

由于近期事件严重威胁到在沪日侨的生命和财产，在沪日侨民会于10月3日向日本总领事馆致函，请求其促使工部局扩充工部局警务处的侦探部，并任命日籍警官负责虹口巡捕房、狄思威路巡捕房和杨树浦巡捕房。
今日，在沪日侨民会外事交涉委员会将举行会议，审议在工部局各部门的重要职位上雇佣更多日本人事宜，因为日本人在上海人口最多，且工部局应给予日本人更好的待遇，因为日籍雇员受到的待遇不如欧籍职员优厚。

《日日新闻》

反日戏剧团体的活动

“阻逆”小型戏剧团和“莫尼”（“蚂蚁”）戏剧团已被当局取缔。
“莫尼”（“蚂蚁”）戏剧团已被其成员解散，他们现在组建了一个喜剧俱乐部，旨在团结戏剧界阵线以对抗日本。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 10, 1936.
SHAI MINIF: 16988
S. D. 7538
12 / 10 36

Sham Fight
Is Staged
In Chapei
Japanese Do Not Reply
To Mayor's Protest
Exodus Continues

The exodus into the International Settlement from Chapei and Hongkew continued throughout the day yesterday and not only did the residents of the outside area leave their homes, but many residing on the Settlement side of the boundaries also decided to move to safer localities. Chinese news agencies reported that all well-to-do people residing in districts about Shanghai, had already moved into the Settlement, notably those from Tansang.

Apparently further tension was added to the nervousness prevailing among the Chapei, Kiangwan and Hongkew residents when the Japanese marines held a street fighting practice within Chinese territory in Kiangwan near the Rokusun Gardens yesterday morning.

Regret was expressed by the local Chinese authorities over the move, as it was said that it greatly hampered their efforts to quieten the situation and bring things back to normal. The Chinese authorities were surprised at the Japanese action in view of the protest made by Mayor Wu Te-chen on Thursday over the presence of Japanese bluejackets in Chapei several days ago, to which no reply was received yesterday.

Three Manoeuvres

Manoeuvres were held in three separate areas by the Japanese bluejackets yesterday morning, one in Chapei and two in the Settlement.

In Chapei the manoeuvres were staged between the Yu Yuan Garden and the Rokusun Gardens. Marines were seen lying down and then running to attack an "objective."

The practices in the Settlement were held along Pingliang Road and in the Hongkew Park.

Towards night the exodus had diminished considerably and due to the reassuring statements from Nanking it is expected that it will remain all quite over the week-end.

（批：SI / See photos / No FILE / 82 / Chun）

《字林西报》，1936年10月10日，星期六。
SHAI MINIF: 16988
S. D. 7538
36年10月12日

在闸北
上演假战斗
日本人对
市长的抗议
未作答复
外逃仍在继续

昨天一整天，从闸北和虹口涌入公共租界的外逃潮持续不断，不仅界外地区的居民离开家园，许多居住在租界边界一侧的居民也决定迁往更安全的地区。中国新闻机构报道，居住在上海周边地区的富裕人士已全部搬入租界，尤其是来自谭家桥（Tansang，音译）的人士。

显然，昨天上午日本海军陆战队在江湾六三花园附近的中国领土内进行巷战演习，加剧了闸北、江湾和虹口居民中普遍存在的紧张情绪。

中国地方当局对这一举动表示遗憾，据说这极大地阻碍了他们平息局势并使一切恢复正常的工作。鉴于吴铁城市长周四就几天前日本水兵出现在闸北一事提出抗议，而截至昨日未收到任何答复，中国当局对日本的行动感到惊讶。

三次演习

昨天上午，日本水兵在三个不同区域举行了演习，一次在闸北，两次在租界内。

在闸北，演习在豫园和六三花园之间进行。有人看到海军陆战队士兵卧倒，然后奔跑攻击一个“目标”。

租界内的演习沿平凉路和虹口公园进行。

临近夜晚，外逃潮已大幅减少，得益于南京方面令人安心的声明，预计整个周末情况将保持平静。

（批注：SI / 见照片 / 无档案 / 82 / Chun）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 10, 1936 16990

JAPANESE MARINES
IGNORE PROTEST

Additional Sentries Posted
in Chapei

Despite another protest by the
Shanghai City Government against
the stationing of Japanese sentries in
Chinese territory, increased activities
of Japanese marines were reported in
the vicinity of Hokusan Garden,
Chapei, yesterday morning. There
was, however, a marked decrease of
evacuation from Chapei and Hong-
kew. Two parties of Japanese
marines, all armed with rifles, cross-
ed the railway track near the Hong-
kew Park at about 9.30 a.m. into
Hwa Yuan Street, Chapei. The num-
ber of Japanese stationed at several
street crossings in Chapei remained
the same as before.

In support of the Shanghai City
Government's order for the suppres-
sion of wild rumours, the Shanghai
and Woosung Garrison Commander's
Headquarters issued a notice yester-
day warning the public.

Looting Planned

The plans of a loafer gang to take
advantage of the situation to loot
Chapei were revealed in the First
Special District Court, yesterday,
when Loh Zee-fa was charged with
murdering Kao Lee-sung, the head of
a rival gang, and two others were
charged with being involved in the
fatal fight. They were remanded for
further inquiries.

According to the prosecution, the
murdered gang leader was invited by
a rival to amalgamate forces to rob
Chapei residents. The former re-
jected the suggestion, whereupon he
was asked to attend a meeting in
Ward Road on Thursday night. About
11 p.m., members of the rival gangs,
with their leaders, met in Ward Road,
near Chemulpo Road, and a quarrel
ensued, whereupon the man who had
rejected the proposal for amalgama-
tion was attacked by over ten per-
sons, all of whom were armed with
knives and other instruments. When
police from Yulin Road Station ar-
rived on the scene, the man had been
fatally injured, and he died while
being conveyed to hospital. Two of
the three men arrested by the police
had received slight injuries.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年10月10日，星期六 16990

日本海军陆战队
无视抗议

闸北增派哨兵

尽管上海市政府再次抗议日军哨兵驻扎在中国领土上，但据报昨日上午在闸北霍山花园附近，日本海军陆战队的活动有所增加。然而，从闸北和虹口撤离的人数显著减少。上午9时30分左右，两队全副武装步枪的日本海军陆战队队员穿过虹口公园附近的铁路轨道，进入闸北华园路。驻扎在闸北几个十字路口的日军人数与之前相同。

为支持上海市政府关于取缔谣言的命令，上海及吴淞警备司令部昨日发布公告，警告公众。

预谋抢劫

第一特区法院昨日揭露了一伙游手好闲之徒企图趁乱抢劫闸北的计划。罗子发（Loh Zee-fa，音译）被控谋杀敌对帮派头目高李松（Kao Lee-sung，音译），另有两人被控参与这场致命斗殴。他们被还押候审，以待进一步调查。

据检方称，被杀的帮派头目曾被对手邀请合并势力以抢劫闸北居民。前者拒绝了该建议，随后被要求于周四晚在华德路参加一次会议。晚上11点左右，敌对帮派的成员及其头目在华德路靠近济物浦路（Chemulpo Road）处会面，随即发生争吵，拒绝合并提议的人遭到十余人袭击，这些人均持有刀具和其他器械。当榆林路警察局的警察到达现场时，该男子已受致命伤，并在送往医院途中死亡。警方逮捕的三名男子中有两人受了轻伤。

16994
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, October 10, 1936 2538
12 / 10 36

Chapei Exodus
Trickling Out

But Chinese Evacuating
District; Uneasiness
Still Prevails

The exodus of Chinese residents from Chapei Hongkew and Yangtze-poo areas is much reduced today, owing to renewed confidence among the local populace as result of the interview between Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek and the Japanese Ambassador Shigeru Kawagoe.

Although there are a few still moving into the Settlement, the number has no comparison with the high mark Wednesday and Thursday. The chief contributing factors prompting the decrease are the reassuring reports from Nanking, and those who could afford to move had left the area already, thus leaving a very small per cent of the populace to evacuate today, and some of them do not care to move until they see the worst.

Still Uneasy

Those who are moving today were impressed by the uneasiness among these remaining in Chapei yesterday morning when Japanese bluejackets held maneuvers in the vicinity of the Rokusan Garden, Chapei, and mock street fights were staged in the Yangtzepoo area and near Hongkew Park.

Complete confidence is not likely to be restored for some time, and the evacuated refugees will not move back until the Japanese withdraw their sentries from Chinese territory.

The police forces of the three municipalities were taking special precautions today to check any possible untoward incidents and demonstrations. Up to noon no incidents and demonstrations were reported.

Japanese Calmer

Marking a return to normalcy in Shanghai's "Little Tokyo" the fifth annual fall concert of geishas was staged at the new Towa Theatre, Chapei Road yesterday. The function was originally scheduled for September 28 but was postponed because of the killing three days earlier of a Japanese sailor on Haining Road. The performance will be repeated today.

The annual fall festival of the Shanghai Jinja Shinto shrine on Kiangwan Road, will be held for three days beginning October 1 under a decision reached by the laymen's committee of the institution on Friday.

16994
《上海晚报与水星报》，1936年10月10日，星期六 2538
12 / 10 36

闸北外流
逐渐减少

但华人正在撤离该区；不安情绪依然盛行

由于蒋介石总司令与日本大使川越茂会晤后，当地民众信心恢复，今日从闸北、虹口和杨浦区撤离的中国居民大幅减少。

虽然仍有少数人搬入租界，但其数量无法与周三和周四的高峰期相比。促成减少的主要因素是来自南京的令人安心的报告，以及有能力搬迁的人已经离开了该地区，因此今天只有极少比例的民众需要撤离，其中一些人表示在看到最坏情况发生之前不愿搬迁。

仍然不安

今日搬迁的人对昨日早晨留在闸北的人中间弥漫的不安情绪印象深刻，当时日本水兵在闸北六三花园附近举行演习，并在杨浦区和虹口公园附近上演了模拟街头战斗。

完全的信心在一段时间内不太可能恢复，已撤离的难民在日本将其哨兵撤出中国领土之前不会返回。

三界市政当局警力今日采取特别预防措施，以遏制任何可能的意外事件和示威活动。截至中午，未报告发生任何事件或示威活动。

日本人较为平静

标志着上海“小东京”回归常态，第五届艺伎秋季音乐会昨日在闸北路新东和戏院举行。该活动原定于9月28日举行，但因三天前一名日本水兵在海宁路被杀而推迟。演出将于今日重演。

根据该机构俗人委员会周五作出的决定，位于江湾路的上海神社神道教的年度秋季祭典将从10月1日起举行三天。

虹口生活
再度活跃

东和戏院举行艺伎音乐会

标志着虹口回归常态，第五届艺伎秋季音乐会昨日在乍浦路新东和戏院举行。该活动原定于9月26日举行，但因三天前一名日本水兵在海宁路被杀而推迟。演出将于今日重演。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 10, 1936. E. RE.
D. 7538
12 10 36

Hawker Hid Pistol With An
Idea Of Getting Reward

Congee Seller Held In Connection With Murder Of
Japanese Marine On September 23 last;
Charged With Concealing Evidence

Tsang Yoong-ho, congee seller, held in connection with the killing of First Class Seaman Taminato, of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, on Haining Road, on the night of September 23, confessed to the police and again in open court yesterday afternoon that he had picked up the large Mauser pistol thrown away by the murderer and hid it in the sand box in an alleyway, of Haining Road, with the sole idea of later handing it over to the authorities and collecting a reward.
When brought before Judge Tsoong in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon Tsang was charged with concealing evidence under Article 167 of the Chinese Criminal Code. He told his story to the judge with a great many gestures, while moving all over the dock. His 60-year-old father stood at the back of the court and held his hands together, while looking up to the ceiling, as if praying for his son.
A number of eye-witnesses of the shooting testified yesterday, but discrepancies were noted in their testimony, one man stating that the killer wore a dark brown suit, another alleging that the murderer was dressed in a grey suit and the third testifying that the murderer wore a green suit. All, however, agreed that the man, who fired the shots that killed Seaman Taminato and wounded the other two sailors, wore foreign clothes and a felt hat. After hearing all the evidence Judge Tsoong remanded Tsang for trial until October 23.
Followed Sailors
All the witnesses, however, seemed to agree that the killer followed the sailors, fired at them from behind or the side of a telephone pole and then ran down the alleyway on the north side of Haining Road.
Two of the Japanese witnesses were asked by the judge why they thought that the killer was a Chinese. One of the witnesses contended that he gathered this from the man's feature. "Aren't the features of all Oriental races similar?" asked the judge. "I could distinguish this man's features," was the reply. Another witness contended that he thought the killer to be a Chinese by his appearance.
A discrepancy also arose between the witnesses as to the number of shots that had been fired, a Chinese boy, who stood just behind the killer, stated that only two had been fired, a Japanese, whom the alleged murderer passed, stated that three shots were fired. One Japanese witness, who saw the shooting from a window of a restaurant, stated that he saw a small boy, the Chinese witness, standing behind the murderer.
It was brought out at the hearing that two Japanese had 'phoned the Japanese Naval Landing Party headquarters immediately after the shooting.

小贩藏匿手枪
意在获取赏金

卖粥者因涉及去年9月23日日本海军陆战队士兵被杀案被捕；
被控隐匿证据

曾永浩（Tsang Yoong-ho，音译），一名卖粥者，因涉及9月23日晚海宁路日本海军陆战队一等水兵田凑（Taminato，音译）被杀案，向警方供认，并于昨日下午在公开法庭上再次承认，他捡起了凶手丢弃的大号毛瑟手枪，并将其藏在海宁路一条小巷的沙箱里，唯一的想法是日后将其交给当局并领取赏金。
昨日下午，曾在第一特区法院出庭受审时，曾某被控违反《中华民国刑法》第167条隐匿证据。他在被告席上四处移动，配合大量手势向法官讲述了自己的故事。他60岁的父亲站在法庭后方，双手合十，仰望天花板，仿佛在为儿子祈祷。
多名枪击案目击者昨日作证，但他们的证词存在差异，一人称凶手身穿深棕色西装，另一人称凶手身穿灰色西装，第三人作证称凶手身穿绿色西装。然而，所有人都同意，开枪打死水兵田凑并打伤另外两名水手的那个人穿着西式服装并戴着毡帽。听完所有证据后，宗法官（Judge Tsoong，音译）将曾某还押候审，直至10月23日开庭审理。
跟踪水兵
然而，所有证人似乎都同意，凶手跟踪水兵，从电线杆后面或侧面开枪，然后沿海宁路北侧的小巷逃跑。
法官询问两名日本证人为何认为凶手是中国人。其中一名证人声称他是从该人的面部特征得出的结论。“难道所有东方种族的面部特征不都相似吗？”法官问道。“我能分辨出这个人的特征，”对方回答。另一名证人声称，他是通过外貌判断凶手是中国人。
证人在开枪次数上也存在差异，站在凶手正后方的一名中国男孩称只开了两枪，而被 alleged 凶手经过的一名日本人称开了三枪。一名从餐厅窗户目睹枪击案的日本证人称，他看到一个小男孩，即那名中国证人，站在凶手身后。
听证会上指出，枪击发生后，两名日本人立即致电日本海军陆战队总部。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 10, 1936 16971
HONGKEW MURDER
SUSPECT
Alleged Concealment of Gun
Which Killed Sailor
WITNESSES OF SHOOTING
GIVE EVIDENCE
Chang Yoong-hwo, a food hawker, arrested on the night of September 23, immediately after the shooting of A. Taminato, a Japanese sailor, in Haining Road, was charged with concealing evidence when he appeared before the First Special District Court, yesterday.
Mr. T. T. Tsang, Assistant Municipal Advocate, told the Court that, during the period of remand, the accused had made another statement to the effect that, on the night of the shooting, he went to Haining Road to see a friend and found a Mauser pistol on the ground. He kicked the weapon and then picked it up and concealed it in a sand-box. He told the police that he did not report his finding immediately, because he was afraid, when he did so, that he would be suspected of being the assailant. He intended to report after concealing the weapon in the sand-box.
Owing to the fact that many persons had handled the Mauser pistol since it was discovered, the fingerprints on the weapon were incomplete and the police could not tell whether they were the accused's. However, one thing was certain, namely, that the bullet taken from the sailor's body was fired from the pistol, Mr. Tsang said.
A Japanese named Kuroda stated that, on September 23, about 8 p.m., he went to Haining Road to meet a friend and a man was walking behind him. When witness passed by a shop, the man behind him overtook him and immediately produced a gun and fired three shots. Witness described this man as one with a broad chest, wearing a foreign-style suit of dark brown colour. After the shooting, witness hid in a lane and heard someone pass by him. Then he saw this man hire a rickshaw outside a Japanese church.
A 17-year-old Chinese, Tsang Liang-pao, employed by a Korean in North Haining Road, said that, on the night in question, he was in Haining Road and saw four Japanese sailors come along with two men in front of them. Near an electric pole, the two men stopped, allowing the sailors to pass by. Then one of the men, in a brown suit, produced a pistol, fired two shots at the sailors and ran away.
Another witness, Wakabashi, said he heard two shots, after which he saw a man run into an alleyway. Witness telephoned a Japanese newspaper and then returned to the scene of shooting, where he saw the accused arrested. The assailant was in a dark green suit.
J. Tanabe, a Japanese office clerk, said he also saw the shooting and the assailant was in dark grey clothing. Witness was in a restaurant. The assailant was a Chinese, who ran into an alleyway after the shooting.
The Judge: "How do you know the assailant was a Chinese?"
Tanabe: "His appearance was Chinese."
The Judge: "The people of the East are all more or less the same in appearance, and how can you tell which is a Chinese?"
Tanabe: "I can distinguish them."
The Judge adjourned the hearing till September 23.

《字林西报》，1936年10月10日，星期六 16971
虹口谋杀案
嫌疑人
涉嫌藏匿杀害水兵的手枪
枪击目击者
提供证词
食品小贩张永火（Chang Yoong-hwo，音译）于9月23日晚日本水兵A. 田凑（A. Taminato，音译）在海宁路被枪杀后立即被捕，昨日在第一特区法院出庭时被控隐匿证据。
助理市检察官唐先生（Mr. T. T. Tsang，音译）告诉法庭，在还押期间，被告作了另一份陈述，称枪击当晚他去海宁路看望朋友，并在地上发现了一把毛瑟手枪。他踢了一下武器，然后捡起并藏在沙箱里。他告诉警察，他没有立即报告这一发现，是因为担心这样做会被怀疑是袭击者。他打算在将武器藏在沙箱后再行报告。
由于自发现以来多人接触过这把毛瑟手枪，武器上的指纹不完整，警方无法确定是否为被告所留。然而，有一件事是确定的，即从水兵体内取出的子弹是由该手枪发射的，唐先生说。
一名名叫黑田（Kuroda）的日本人陈述称，9月23日晚8点左右，他去海宁路见朋友，有一名男子走在他身后。当证人经过一家商店时，身后的男子超过了他，立即掏出手枪开了三枪。证人描述此人身材宽胸，身穿深棕色西式西装。枪击后，证人躲进一条弄堂，听到有人从他身边经过。随后他看到此人在一座日本教堂外雇了一辆人力车。
一名17岁的中国人张良宝（Tsang Liang-pao，音译），受雇于海宁北路的一名朝鲜人，他说，案发当晚他在海宁路，看到四名日本水兵走来，前面有两个人。在一根电线杆附近，那两个人停下来，让水兵们通过。随后，其中一名穿棕色西装的男子掏出手枪，向水兵开了两枪后逃跑。
另一名证人若桥（Wakabashi，音译）说，他听到两声枪响，随后看到一名男子跑进一条小巷。证人给一家日本报社打了电话，然后返回枪击现场，在那里看到被告被捕。袭击者身穿深绿色西装。
日本职员田边（J. Tanabe，音译）说，他也看到了枪击过程，袭击者身穿深灰色衣服。证人在一家餐馆内。袭击者是中国人，枪击后跑进了一条小巷。
法官：“你怎么知道袭击者是中国人？”
田边：“他的外貌是中国人。”
法官：“东方人的外貌都大同小异，你怎么分辨哪一个是中国人？”
田边：“我能分辨出来。”
法官宣布休庭，直至9月23日。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 10, 1936

5 Tell Court
Of Shooting
In Hongkew

All Agree On Major
Details In Killing
Of Japanese

HAWKER PICKED
UP DEATH GUN

Man Hid Mauser In
Sand Box, Hoping
To Get Reward

Details of the investigation into
the shooting of Warrant Officer
Asamitsu Taminato, Japanese Naval
Landing Party, on the night of
September 23, were revealed at an
open hearing before the First Spe-
cial District Court yesterday.
Briefly, the facts are these:
Tseng Yoong-ho, age 21, food
hawker, now being held by the
police, had nothing to do with the
actual shooting but did pick up the
Mauser pistol from which the shots
were fired and hid it in a sandbox
at the entrance to Lane 15, North
Haining Road. He has been charg-
ed with concealing a weapon which
he knew to have been used in the
commission of a crime.
Only one man did the shooting.
He is believed to have been Chinese
and was about five feet, four inches
tall, of stocky build, and who wore
foreign-style clothes and a felt hat.
Five eye-witnesses to the shoot-
ing, four Japanese and one Chinese
boy of 17, have been located by the
police and were brought into court
to give testimony yesterday after-
noon.

Witnesses Disagree
Although the five declare that
they saw the man shoot three Jap-
anese bluejackets in the back on
North Haining Road about 8.15 p.m.,
September 23, not one of them could
agree on the color of the suit and
hat that the man wore. One of
them said it was dark brown, ano-
ther dark gray and another de-
clared that it was dark green.
The Japanese witnesses all declar-
ed that the man was Chinese but
could not state how they knew this
to be true. They explained it by
saying that were able to tell the
difference between Chinese and
other people of Asia, even at some
distance.
The proceedings yesterday were
conducted before Judge Tsoong The
session started at 2.30 p.m. and
lasted for two hours, and was then
adjourned until October 23.
Assistant Municipal Advocate T.
T. Tseng opened the session by
stating that Tseng, the food hawker,
had changed his statement since
he last appeared before the court
and had confessed to finding the
pistol.
The hawker told the police that
on the night the shooting occurred,
he went from his home on Sing Kya
Road to North Haining Road to see
a friend. He heard the shooting
and while passing Lane 15, North
Haining Road, saw a Mauser pistol
on the ground. He declared that
he picked it up and hid it in the
sandbox.

Immediately after he had hidden
the gun, he was grabbed by Mr.
Takashi Horiye, who happened to
witness the action. The latter
turned the hawker over to the Jap-
anese naval authorities who had ar-
rived on the scene by that time.
Afraid Of Being Involved
Tseng declared that the reason he
did not notify the authorities imme-
diately was because he was afraid
he might become involved in the
case, but added that as soon as the
commotion in the neighborhood
quieted down a bit, he intended to
inform the police.
Questioned by the court, Tseng
retracted the statement he had
made to the police and added that
he hadn't realized he was doing
anything wrong. He had acted in
haste, he said, and was now very
sorry that he had touched the gun.
He declared, however, that he was
not an eye-witness to the shooting.
The first eye-witness to the shoot-
ing called to the stand was Mr. M.
Kuroda, clerk. He stated that on
the night of the slaying, he had
left his home in another section of
Hongkew to visit a friend on North
Haining Road. In fact, every wit-
ness called but one including the
hawker declared he had gone to
North Haining Road on the fatal
night to visit a friend.
Konuda, dressed in a light grayish
brown suit, declared that he entered
a Japanese restaurant district,
stayed there for a short time and
then left the place. Shortly after
his departure, he turned about and
noticed that a Chinese, wearing a
dark brown suit and a felt hat was
following him, he said.
He said the man continued to
follow him for quite a distance but
that he soon passed him. Ahead
of him, Koruda declared, were four
Japanese bluejackets walking along
the street. The man in the brown
suit, he said, suddenly stopped,
pulled a Mauser pistol from inside
his coat and commenced shooting at
the bluejackets.

Informed Japanese
The witness continued that the
man fired three shots and then
fled down Lane 15. He said he hid
behind a door until the shooting
was over, and then dashed over to
the Japanese Naval Landing Party's
sub-station on Chapoo Road where
he informed the officers in charge
of the affray. He said the man who
did the shooting was about five
feet, four inches tall and he was
certain that the suit he wore was
brown. From his position behind
the door, he continued, he could not
see whether the man had anyone
waiting for him or not.
The second eye-witness called was
Tseng Liang-pao, age 17. The boy
was short of stature and looked
about 12. He gave a vivid descrip-
tion of what he saw, however. He
declared that he left his home on
Kashing Road earlier in the even-
ing and walked to North Haining
Road to see a friend. Just as he
arrived near Lane 15, he saw a man
dressed in a brown suit step and
open fire on some Japanese blue-
jackets walking ahead. He said he
only heard two shots but wasn't
sure that there were not more since
he became badly frightened and
for a moment stood paralysed in
his tracks.
After the shooting, he declared
that the man ran down the lane
and disappeared. A Japanese blue-
jacket fell down and his companions
ran away. Only one man did the
shooting, he said, but he added that
he saw the man in the brown suit
stop near an electric light pole and
talk to another man.

Saw Shooting
The third witness was Mr. Hisaake
Wakabayashi, Japanese residing in
Hongkew, who was dining with a
friend in a restaurant near the
scene of the shooting and on the
same street. He said he heard a
shot, rushed to the window and
looked out. He added that he saw
a Chinese in a foreign-style suit
shooting Japanese bluejackets in the
back. He added that he faced back
of the killer and not far away stood
a small Chinese in a black jacket
and Chinese-style trousers. This
second man seemed much surprised,
he said, and then added that the
Chinese boy who had testified look-
ed very much like him. Asked how
the killer was dressed, he stated
that he wore a dark green suit of
foreign cut.
Wakabayashi continued that he
immediately dashed out into the
street and ran toward the scene of
the shooting. The killer, he added,
darted up the alley and disappear-
ed. He said that, as the slayer
ran, he thought he saw him throw
something away.
The court requested the witness to
look about the room and see if he
could find a suit on anyone present
that was like the suit he saw on the
killer. He declared that he could
see no such suit in the court room.
The Chinese witness was called
back to the stand and asked to see
if he could find a similar suit worn by
anyone in the court. He selected
the suit worn by Koruda, the first
witness, as being like it. Koruda
was asked to see if he could locate
a suit similar to one the killer wore.
He selected a dark brown suit worn
by a spectator.

Testimony Varies
Two other Japanese witnesses were
called. Both testified that they had
witnessed the shooting and one de-
clared that the suit the killer wore
was dark gray and declared that the
suit worn by a certain newspaper
reporter was very much like it. The
last of the witnesses called said the
man wore a light brown suit and
found a similar one in the court-
room.
As matters stand, the court and
the police are not very clear on the
color of the suit. They do know
that one man did the shooting and
according to the police, the bullets
that were taken from the dead
Japanese bluejacket and his two
wounded comrades were fired from
the Mauser taken from the sandbox.
The session yesterday was well
attended. Most of the spectators
were Japanese naval officers and
other Japanese officials. The
hawker's aged father, heart-broken
that his only surviving son of a
family of nine boys should be in
the hands of the law, was a deeply
interested listener to everything that
was said.
