《字林西报》，1936年10月10日，星期六

虹口枪击案
五人在法庭作证

关于日本人被杀案的主要细节
各方说法一致

小贩拾获作案手枪

男子将毛瑟枪藏于沙箱，希图获取赏金

昨日，在第一特区法院举行的公开听证会上，披露了9月23日晚日本海军陆战队准尉田凑朝光（Asamitsu Taminato）遭枪击一案的调查细节。简而言之，事实如下：

现被警方羁押的21岁食品小贩曾永浩（Tseng Yoong-ho，音译）并未实际参与枪击，但他捡起了发射子弹的毛瑟手枪，并将其藏在北海宁路15弄入口处的沙箱内。他被指控隐瞒其明知已用于犯罪的武器。

开枪者仅有一人。据信此人为中国人，身高约5英尺4英寸，体格粗壮，身穿西式服装，头戴毡帽。警方已找到五名枪击案目击者，包括四名日本人和一名17岁的中国少年，并于昨日下午将他们传唤至法庭作证。

证人证词不一

尽管五人均声称在9月23日晚8点15分左右，在北海宁路目睹一名男子从背后向三名日本水兵开枪，但对于该男子所穿西装和帽子的颜色，无人能达成一致。一人称是深棕色，另一人称是深灰色，还有一人坚称是深绿色。

日本证人均宣称该男子是中国人，但无法说明如何确知此事。他们解释说，即使距离较远，他们也能分辨出中国人与其他亚洲人的区别。

昨日的庭审由钟法官（Judge Tsoong，音译）主持。庭审于下午2点30分开始，持续两小时，随后休庭至10月23日。

助理市检察官T. T. Tseng（音译）在开庭时指出，食品小贩曾某自上次出庭以来已改变供词，并承认捡到了手枪。

该小贩告诉警方，枪击发生当晚，他从辛家路（Sing Kya Road，音译）的家中前往北海宁路探望朋友。他听到了枪声，在经过北海宁路15弄时，看到地上有一把毛瑟手枪。他声称自己捡起手枪并将其藏在沙箱里。

就在他藏好枪后，恰好目睹这一举动的堀江隆志先生（Mr. Takashi Horiye，音译）抓住了他。后者将该小贩移交给当时已抵达现场的日本海军当局。

害怕受牵连

曾某声称，他没有立即通知当局的原因是他害怕被卷入此案，但他补充说，一旦附近的骚动稍加平息，他本打算向警方报告。

经法庭讯问，曾某撤回了此前向警方所作的陈述，并补充说他并未意识到自己做错了什么。他说自己当时行动仓促，现在非常后悔碰了那把枪。然而，他声明自己并非枪击案的目击者。

第一位被传唤作证的枪击案目击者是职员黑田M先生（Mr. M. Kuroda，音译）。他陈述说，凶杀案发生当晚，他离开虹口另一区域的住所，前往北海宁路拜访朋友。事实上，除一人外，包括该小贩在内的所有被传唤证人均声称，他们在案发当晚前往北海宁路是为了探望朋友。

黑田身穿浅灰褐色西装，他声称自己进入了一家日式餐馆区，停留片刻后离开。他说，离开后不久，他转身注意到一名身穿深棕色西装、头戴毡帽的中国人正尾随他。

他说那人继续尾随了他相当长的一段距离，但他很快超过了那人。黑田声称，在他前方有四名日本水兵沿街行走。他说，那名穿棕色西装的男子突然停下，从外套内掏出一把毛瑟手枪，开始向水兵射击。

通知日本人

该证人继续说道，那人开了三枪，然后沿15弄逃窜。他说自己躲在一扇门后，直到枪击结束，然后冲向乍浦路日本海军陆战队分局，向负责处理此事的官员报告。他说开枪者身高约5英尺4英寸，他确信其所穿西装为棕色。他接着说，由于他躲在门后，无法看清是否有人在等候该男子。

第二位被传唤的目击者是17岁的曾良宝（Tseng Liang-pao，音译）。这名少年身材矮小，看起来约12岁。然而，他对所见情形作了生动的描述。他声称当晚早些时候离开嘉善路（Kashing Road，音译）的家，步行至北海宁路探望朋友。就在他到达15弄附近时，他看到一名身穿棕色西装的男子迈步向前，向走在前面的几名日本水兵开火。他说他只听到两声枪响，但不确定是否还有更多枪声，因为他吓得要命，一时僵在原地动弹不得。

他说，枪击过后，那人跑进弄堂并消失了。一名日本水兵倒下，其同伴四散奔逃。他说开枪者只有一人，但他补充说，他看到那名穿棕色西装的男子在一根电线杆旁停下，与另一名男子交谈。

目睹枪击

第三位证人是居住在虹口的日本人若林久明先生（Mr. Hisaake Wakabayashi，音译），事发时他正与一位朋友在案发现场附近同一条街的一家餐馆用餐。他说他听到一声枪响，冲到窗前向外张望。他补充说，他看到一名身穿西式服装的中国人从背后向日本水兵射击。他还说，他正对着凶手背部，不远处站着一名身穿黑色夹克和中式长裤的小个子中国人。他说这第二名男子显得非常惊讶，并补充说，此前作证的中国少年与他非常相像。当被问及凶手衣着时，他表示凶手身穿一套深绿色的西式剪裁西装。

若林继续说道，他立即冲上街道，跑向枪击现场。他补充说，凶手窜入小巷并消失。他说，在凶手逃跑时，他觉得自己看到凶手扔掉了什么东西。

法庭请该证人在房间内环顾四周，看看能否在现场任何人身上找到与他在凶手身上看到的相似的西装。他声称在法庭内未见到此类西装。

中国证人被再次传唤作证，并被要求查看法庭内是否有人穿着类似的西装。他选中了第一位证人黑田所穿的西装，认为与之相似。黑田也被要求寻找与凶手所穿相似的西装。他选中了一名旁观者所穿的深棕色西装。

证词各异

另有两名日本证人被传唤。两人均作证目睹了枪击过程，其中一人宣称凶手所穿西装为深灰色，并称某位报社记者所穿西装与之非常相似。最后一名被传唤的证人称该男子身穿浅棕色西装，并在法庭内找到了一套相似的西装。

目前的情况是，法庭和警方对西装的颜色尚不清楚。他们确实知道开枪者仅有一人，且据警方称，从死亡的日本水兵及其两名受伤同伴体内取出的子弹，正是从沙箱中缴获的那把毛瑟手枪所发射。

昨日的庭审座无虚席。大多数旁观者为日本海军军官及其他日本官员。该小贩年迈的父亲因九个儿子中唯一幸存的儿子落入法网而心碎不已，他对庭上所说的一切听得极为专注。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, October 9, 1936 16968

7538
12 / 10 36

Chapei, Kiangwan
Exodus Continues

Nervousness Decreases
Slightly But Many
Chinese Leaving

With reassuring statements coming from Nanking from both Chinese and Japanese sources following the important conference between General Chiang Kai-shek, president of the Executive Yuan, and Mr. Shigeru Kawagoe, Japanese ambassador to China, the heavy exodus of Chinese from Chapei and Kiangwan areas is expected to be diminished shortly.

Some nervousness and "war-scare," however, still exist in Chapei and Kiangwan area as result of the continued activity of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party in the areas adjoining the International Settlement. Drills by a large force of Japanese bluejackets this morning near the Rokusan Garden and similar activities by armed forces caused fresh nervousness. Near Rokusen Garden, the Japanese bluejackets practiced trench warfare with grim seriousness.

Big Exodus In Night
The largest exodus from Chapei area occurred late last night when wild rumors were in circulation that the Nanking negotiations had broken down and that the Japanese bluejackets here were to repeat the affair of 1932. In order to avoid police intervention, many moved in the small hours of this morning.

Because of the general nervousness among the students, many of the schools in Kiangwan ordered two or three days' holidays on occasion of the Double Tenth, the Chinese National Day, tomorrow. Many of the schools were closed Thursday and others from today until next Monday. In some of the schools, the faculty members became so nervous that during the classes, they told the students how to reach safer spots in the downtown area in case of hostilities.

Officers Alert
Chinese authorities are still on the alert to check the circulation of wild rumors and to break up the gangs organized to fabricate alarmist stories to enrich themselves through the nervousness and evacuation. The Garrison Commander's Headquarters for Shanghai and Woosung Areas has just issued an order threatening invocation of martial law against those responsible for fabricating alarmist rumors.

Despite the actions, the situation in Chapei, as summed up by a Chinese vernacular paper is "nine out of 10 houses empty."

The City Government of Greater Shanghai, seeking to remove the fundamental cause of the state of mind among the Chapei populace, has lodged a second protest with the Japanese Consulate-General against the activities of the Japanese bluejackets in Chapei. Their presence in Chapei is declared as an infringement upon Chinese territorial and sovereign rights.

Transport Profits
That "it's an ill wind that blows nobody good" has proved to be a fitful adage once again in Shanghai. While residents of Hongkew and Chapei are nervous in apprehension of more trouble some are taking advantage of the situation to reap rich profits.

Despite the fact that many Chinese business firms in north Shanghai are being hit by the recent war scare, the transportation companies—the ricksha hongs, taxi companies, and truck companies—are reaping profits unprecedented since the 1932 Sino-Japanese debacle out of the present grave situation in Hongkew.

Fleets Help
The general exodus from Chapei and Hongkew districts is still in full swing, and the transportation companies are raking in dollars by the loads with every outbreak of wild rumors. With the arrival of U.S. and the British naval vessels the taxi companies, too, are doing an unusually brisk business.

According to Mr. V. J. Song, vice-manager of the G. E. Marden Company, Ltd., which is one of the largest transportation companies in Shanghai, the business of the company has increased two-fold since the renewed tension in Hongkew. Shortage of trucks, removing vans, and buses was evident in garages in Shanghai this morning.

Information was also obtained that with the arrival of the U.S. and British ships in port the daily income of taxi companies has jumped to a new high during the last few days.

War Risk Rates Rise
The uncertainty of the local situation makes things difficult for many insurance firms, and to comply with such a heavy demand of war risk policies, a rapid increase in rate is resulting. Rates have been doubled for the Central District and parts of the Western area. As much as 17.5 per mille is now asked for property north of Soochow Creek and in Chapei, as against a normal 2.50.

Several insurance companies have refused to insure against war risk any personal effects north of the Creek, accepting war risk only on property for six months, and then on condition that fire insurance is also carried. Several underwriters have agreed to insure property in Kiangwan, Chapei and the Civic Centre district at a low rate of $10 per mille for three months and $15 per mille for six months.

Seek Wider Powers
Studies into the advisability of securing wider powers for the high Japanese officers of the Shanghai Municipal Police have been launched by the Foreign Relations Committee of the Japanese Residents' Corporation following a meeting to discuss the aftermath of the slaying of a Japanese marine and the wounding of two others on Haining Road on Sept. 23.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年10月9日，星期五 16968

7538
12 / 10 36

闸北、江湾
撤离仍在继续

紧张情绪略有缓解
但许多华人仍在离开

随着行政院长蒋介石将军与中国日本大使川越茂先生举行重要会议后，来自南京的中日双方均发表了令人安心的声明，预计闸北和江湾地区华人大量外逃的现象将很快减少。

然而，由于日本特别海军陆战队在毗邻公共租界的地区持续活动，闸北和江湾地区仍存在一些紧张情绪和“战争恐慌”。今天上午，大批日本水兵在六三花园附近进行演习，武装部队的类似活动也引发了新的紧张情绪。在六三花园附近，日本水兵神情严峻地演练战壕战。

夜间大规模外逃
昨晚，闸北地区出现了最大规模的外逃，当时流言四起，称南京谈判破裂，驻此地的日本水兵将重演1932年的事件。为避免警方干预，许多人在今日凌晨时分搬离。

由于学生普遍感到紧张，江湾的许多学校借明日（双十节，即中国国庆日）之机放假两三天。许多学校于周四停课，其他学校则从今天起停课至下周一。在一些学校中，教职员变得非常紧张，甚至在课堂上告诉学生，一旦发生敌对行动，如何前往市中心更安全的地方。

当局保持警惕
中国当局仍保持警惕，以遏制疯狂谣言的传播，并捣毁那些利用紧张情绪和撤离潮制造恐慌故事以牟利的团伙。淞沪警备司令部刚刚发布命令，威胁对制造恐慌谣言的责任人实施戒严。

尽管采取了这些行动，但据一份中文白话报纸总结，闸北的局势仍是“十室九空”。

大上海市政府为消除闸北民众心态的根本原因，已就日本水兵在闸北的活动向日本总领事馆提出第二次抗议。声明指出，他们在闸北的存在是对中国领土主权权利的侵犯。

运输业获利
谚语“塞翁失马，焉知非福”在上海再次得到印证。虽然虹口和闸北的居民因担心更多麻烦而感到紧张，但有些人正利用这一局势攫取丰厚利润。

尽管上海北区的许多华商企业受到近期战争恐慌的打击，但运输公司——人力车行、出租车公司和卡车公司——正从虹口目前的严峻局势中获取自1932年中日冲突以来前所未有的利润。

车队助力
闸北和虹口地区的大规模外逃仍在全面进行，每次谣言爆发，运输公司都大赚美元。随着美国和英国军舰的到来，出租车公司的生意也异常兴隆。

据上海最大的运输公司之一马登有限公司（G. E. Marden Company, Ltd.）副经理宋维俊（V. J. Song，音译）先生称，自虹口紧张局势重新加剧以来，该公司的业务增加了一倍。今天上午，上海各车库明显缺乏卡车、搬家货车和公交车。

另有消息获悉，随着美英船只抵达港口，过去几天出租车公司的日收入跃升至新高。

战争险费率上升
当地局势的不确定性使许多保险公司陷入困境，为满足对战争险保单的巨大需求，费率迅速上涨。中区及西区部分地区的费率已翻倍。目前，苏州河以北及闸北地区的财产保险费率高达千分之17.5，而正常费率为千分之2.50。

几家保险公司拒绝为河北岸的任何个人财物承保战争险，仅接受为期六个月的财产战争险，且条件是必须同时投保火险。几位承保人同意以千分之10的较低费率承保江湾、闸北和大上海中心区（Civic Centre district）的财产三个月，或按千分之15的费率承保六个月。

寻求更大权力
继9月23日海宁路发生一名日本海军陆战队员被杀、两名受伤事件的后续讨论会议之后，日本居留民团外交委员会已开始研究赋予上海公共租界工部局警务处高级日本警官更大权力的可行性。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 10, 1936
16985
7538
12 10 36

POLICE CHANGES IN
SHANGHAI ASKED
Japanese Seeking New
Powers For Officers
In Local Force

Studies of the advisability of securing wider powers for the high Japanese officers of the Shanghai Municipal Police were launched on Thursday by the Foreign Relations Committee on the Japanese Residents' Corporation, following a meeting to discuss the aftermath of the slaying of a Japanese marine and the wounding of two others on Haining Road on September 23.

According to the Japanese press, the committee holds that there is no reason why the high Japanese S.M.P. officers are not given the authority to direct the operations of officers of various nationalities in the same manner as the high British officers are.

This lack of authority, the committee believes, considerably hampers the activities of these Japanese officers, who have absolute command only over lower Japanese officers and constables.

The need for an increase in the number of plain clothes detectives, the question of establishing permanent police posts and a proposal for placing Japanese at fire stations in districts thickly populated by Japanese were also tabled at the meeting.—Domei.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年10月10日，星期六
16985
7538
12 10 36

要求改变上海
警务人员权限
日本人寻求赋予
本地警力中的日籍
警官新权力

继9月23日海宁路发生一名日本海军陆战队员被杀、两名受伤事件的后续讨论会议之后，日本居留民团外交委员会于周四开始研究赋予上海公共租界工部局警务处高级日本警官更大权力的可行性。

据日本媒体报道，该委员会认为，没有理由不赋予工部局警务处的高级日本警官与高级英国警官相同的权力，以指挥各国籍警官的行动。

该委员会认为，这种权力的缺失严重阻碍了这些日本警官的活动，他们目前仅对下级日本警官和巡捕拥有绝对指挥权。

会议上还提出了增加便衣侦探人数、设立永久警察岗哨以及在日侨聚居区的消防站安置日本人的提议。——同盟社

Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, October 9, 1936
D. 7538
10 10 36

Hawker Faces
Changed Charge

Vendor Tells Attempt
To Hide Japanese
Death Gun

Because he picked up and tried
to hide the gun which he saw the
suspected murderer of Siaman
[illegible] of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party throw to the
ground as he fled from the scene
of the shooting on September 23,
Chang Yung-ho, 21-year-old con-
gee vendor, this afternoon was
being brought before the First
District Court and charged under
article 167 of the Chinese Criminal
Code with concealing an offender
and attempting to conceal evidence.
Mr. Paul Y. Ru, assistant muni-
cipal advocate, is conducting the
prosecution of Chang.

The congee vendor broke down
recently and confessed to detectives
of the Hongkew Station that on
the night when Taminato was
killed and two of his companions
injured, he saw a man fleeing
from the scene throw a gun to the
ground. Thinking that there
would be a reward out for the
recovery of the death gun, Chang
picked it up and attempted to
conceal in a sandbox at the south
end of lane 15, north Haining
Road. He was discovered in the
act of putting the gun in the box
by a Japanese tailor, Mr. Tadashi
Horiye, who seized him and called
for help.

According to the story given to
police, the man that Chang saw
run away was a Chinese. Chang,
however, has not been able to
furnish any adequate description
of the man who is thought to have
fired the shots that wounded the
Japanese Naval Party members.

The maximum penalty which
Chang can be given under article
167 is two years. The article
reads:

Whoever forges, alters, de-
stroys or conceals evidence in
a criminal case in which an-
other is implicated, or makes
use of such forged documents
or altered evidence, shall be
punished with imprisonment
for not more than two years,
or detention or a fine of not
more than five hundred yuan.

16966
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年10月9日，星期五
D. 7538
10 10 36

小贩面临
变更指控

摊主讲述试图藏匿
致日本人死亡之枪支

21岁的粥摊小贩张永和（Chang Yung-ho，音译）因捡起并试图藏匿他在9月23日枪击案现场看到的一名嫌疑人扔在地上的枪支，该嫌疑人系日本海军陆战队暹罗人[原文不清]（Siaman [illegible]）的谋杀嫌疑犯，并于作案后逃离现场。今天下午，张永和被带至第一特区法院，并根据《中华民国刑法》第167条被控窝藏罪犯和试图隐匿证据。市助理检察官鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru，音译）先生负责对张提起公诉。

这名粥摊小贩最近崩溃，并向虹口捕房的侦探供认，在田港（Taminato，音译）被杀、两名同伴受伤的当晚，他看到一名男子从现场逃跑时将一支枪扔在地上。张永和以为找回致死枪支会有赏金，便捡起枪支，试图将其藏匿在北海宁路15弄南端的一个沙箱里。日本裁缝堀江正（Tadashi Horiye，音译）先生发现了他正在将枪放入箱内的行为，随即将其抓住并呼救。

根据向警方陈述的故事，张永和看到的逃跑男子是一名中国人。然而，张永和未能提供被认为开枪打伤日本海军陆战队成员的那名男子的任何充分描述。

根据第167条，张永和可能受到的最高刑罚是两年监禁。该条款规定：

凡伪造、变造、毁灭或隐匿他人涉及之刑事案件的证据，或使用此类伪造文件或变造证据者，处二年以下有期徒刑、拘役或五百元以下罚金。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, OCTOBER 9. 1936
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. E. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 7538
Date 9 / 10 36

WAR RISK INSURANCE
RATES INCREASED

Underwriters Hesitate
To Insure Personal
Effects In Hongkew

BIG DEMAND LEADS
TO RATE RISE

The uncertainty of the local
situation has made itself felt in
local insurance circles, and result-
ed in a rise in war risk rates.
Rates have been doubled for the
Central districts and parts of the
Western area, but as much as 10/-
per mille is now asked for property
North of the Creek and in Chapei
as against a normal 2.50.

Several insurance companies
have refused to insure against war
risk any personal effects North of
the Creek, accepting war risk only
on property for six months, and
then on condition that fire insur-
ance is also carried.

It was pointed out by an
insurance man yesterday that it
was not exactly that the present
tense situation were governing the
rates of the underwriters, but the
demand, which has been very heavy
during the past week. Large
amounts have been underwritten
and many more inquiries were
being made from all parts of the
city.

The ordinary rate for war risk
insurance in Hongkew and Chapei
is 2.50 per mille. The rate for
the Central and Western districts

mille with personal effects being
underwritten, while the rate in the
northern and eastern districts of
the Settlement has been accepted

month, 5 per mille for three
months and 10 per mille for six
months. No policies have been
issued for longer periods.

It was pointed out that a num-
ber of factories and godowns took
out war risk about a month ago
for outside areas at low rates, but
that certain areas are now being
refused by underwriters.

Yesterday several underwriters
agreed to insure property in
Kiangwan, Chapei and the Civic
Centre district at a low rate of
$10 per mille for three months and
$15 per mille for six months.

《字林西报》，1936年10月9日，星期五
上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. E. 登记处
编号 S. B. D. 7538
日期 36年10月9日

战争险费率
上调

承保人犹豫
为虹口个人财物
承保

需求大增导致
费率上涨

当地局势的不确定性已波及本地保险界，并导致战争险费率上涨。中区及西区部分地区的费率已翻倍，但苏州河以北及闸北地区的财产保险费率目前高达千分之十（10/- per mille），而正常费率为千分之二点五零（2.50）。

几家保险公司已拒绝为苏州河以北的任何个人财物承保战争险，仅接受为期六个月的财产战争险，且条件是必须同时投保火险。

一位保险业内人士昨日指出，确切地说，决定承保人费率的并非当前的紧张局势，而是过去一周内非常旺盛的需求。大量业务已被承保，来自全市各地的咨询也日益增多。

虹口和闸北地区战争险的常规费率为千分之二点五零。中区和西区的费率现已翻倍至千分之五，并承保个人财物；而租界北部和东部地区的费率则被接受为：一个月千分之四，三个月千分之五，六个月千分之十。未签发更长期限的保单。

有人指出，约一个月前，一些工厂和仓库以低费率为其位于外围区域的资产投保了战争险，但目前某些区域已被承保人拒绝承保。

昨日，几位承保人同意以较低费率承保江湾、闸北和大上海中心区（Civic Centre district）的财产，费率为：三个月千分之十（$10 per mille），六个月千分之十五（$15 per mille）。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, OCTOBER 8, 1936

Gang Admits
Spreading Of
Idle Rumors

Eight Men Arrested By
Chapei Police After
Latest Exodus

Eight men, believed by police to be members of an organized gang engaged in spreading groundless rumors during the last few days which led to the exodus of Chapei residents, were arrested yesterday by officers of the Bureau of Public Safety.

These men admitted to the Chinese police that they have been asked by an unnamed group of people to circulate the alarmist reports, and to persuade the populace to move out of the Chinese areas.

From their statements, the police learned that their favorite way of spreading the fabricated reports was to use the telephone. One member of the gang, for instance, would call up a certain resident and tell an entirely unfounded story about Japanese occupation or scare tales of like nature.

Playing on the general fear on the part of the populace, members of the gang knew that such a mysterious phone call would be relayed by the recipient to his neighbors and friends, thus assuring that the rumor would spread in the way the authors of these reports desired.

Closely Organized

Indicating that the rumor mongers are closely organized, the officers had received various informations showing that all the telephone messages were worded in a similar manner.

The eight arrested men include Chu Yac-chang and Li Ching-chuen. Officers were last night conducting a search for the men who organized the gang.

Eager to sell his papers and to compete with other boys in his district on Honan Road, Chao An-san, a news boy, decided yesterday that he would make up a little "scoop" of his own.

To the crowd which was returning home from the downtown offices, he yelled:

"Read all about the declaration of war between China and Japan! Read all about the war."

His cry attracted the attention of a passing police officer, who bought a paper as did many other passers-by.

There was not a single line about the war in the evening paper Chao sold. He was brought to the Central Police station and was last night detained, pending investigation by officers.

Together with the professional alarmists, another racket had grown up with the mass evacuation of residents from Chapei. People who wanted to move in this area were approached by leafers who promised to obtain the necessary permits from the authorities. Many residents reported yesterday that they paid various sums of money, but the "permits" never appeared nor did the man who promised to get them.

In Chapei yesterday, the exodus, spurred by the wild reports, showed no signs of curtailment up to a late hour last night. Pacahan Road, the main thoroughfare of the area, was jammed by rickshas, moving vans, and carts loaded with household goods, making ordinary traffic on the street almost impossible.

Persuasion Useless

Despite the persuasion and explanation made by the officers of the Bureau of Public Safety, the residents continued their trek into the International Settlement and the French Concession throughout the day.

Information from official sources last night indicated that the ban on evacuation, lifted several days ago, may again be put into effect today in order to check the circulation of rumors and to prevent any disturbances.

Reinforcement in police was seen in many sections of Chapei yesterday. Officers explained this move as a necessary precautionary measure brought about by the movement of a large body of residents.

Meantime in Hongkew, the situation remains unchanged. The district, with only a few Japanese patrols on duty, was quiet. Only a small group of the people who joined the exodus came from that area.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》，1936年10月8日，星期四

帮派承认
散布无聊谣言

最新一波逃离潮后
闸北警方逮捕八人

八名男子昨日被公安局警官逮捕，警方认为他们是一个有组织帮派的成员，该帮派在过去几天里散布毫无根据的谣言，导致闸北居民外逃。

这些人向中国警察承认，他们受一群未具名的人士指使，散布引起恐慌的报告，并劝说民众搬离华人居住区。

从他们的供词中，警方获悉，他们散布捏造报告的最常用手段是使用电话。例如，帮派中的一名成员会致电某位居民，编造关于日军占领的完全无稽之谈，或类似性质的恐怖故事。

利用民众普遍的恐惧心理，帮派成员知道这种神秘的电话会被接听者转告给邻居和朋友，从而确保谣言按照造谣者希望的方式传播。

组织严密

表明造谣者组织严密的是，警官们收到了各种信息，显示所有电话留言措辞相似。

被捕的八人中包括朱亚章（Chu Yac-chang，音译）和李清泉（Li Ching-chuen，音译）。警官昨晚正在搜捕组织该帮派的人员。

赵安三（Chao An-san，音译）是一名报童，为了卖出报纸并与河南路所在街区的其他男孩竞争，他昨天决定自己编造一点“独家新闻”。

他对一群刚从市中心办公室下班回家的人群大喊：

“快看中日宣战的消息！快看战争消息。”

他的叫喊引起了一名路过警察的注意，该警察像许多路人一样买了一份报纸。

赵所卖的晚报上连一行关于战争的报道都没有。他被带到中央巡捕房，昨晚被拘留，等待警官调查。

随着闸北居民的大规模撤离，除了职业恐慌制造者外，另一种骗局也应运而生。想要搬离该地区的人会被发传单者接触，这些人承诺能从当局获得必要的通行证。许多居民昨日报告称，他们支付了不同数额的钱款，但“通行证”从未出现，承诺办理的人也无影无踪。

昨日在闸北，受疯狂报道刺激的外逃潮直到昨晚深夜仍未见减缓迹象。该地区的主要干道巴卡汉路（Pacahan Road，即今八字桥路/宝通路一带，原文可能指主要道路）挤满了人力车、搬家卡车和装载家什的手推车，使得街道上的正常交通几乎无法进行。

劝解无效

尽管公安局警官进行了劝解和解释，居民们仍整天持续向公共租界和法租界迁徙。

昨晚来自官方渠道的消息表明，几天前解除的撤离禁令可能今日再次生效，以遏制谣言传播并防止任何骚乱。

昨日在闸北许多地段可见警力增援。警官解释称，此举是因大量居民流动而采取的必要预防措施。

与此同时，虹口地区的局势保持不变。该区只有少数日本巡逻队在执勤，气氛平静。只有少数加入外逃潮的人来自该地区。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, OCTOBER 1, 1936
16950
MUNICIPAL
REGISTRY
D. 7538
8 10 36

Another
Scare In
Hongkew

Evacuation Resumed On
Rumour Of Martial
Law In District

The evacuation of Chapei and
Hongkew was resumed with in-
creased speed yesterday afternoon
when rumours that martial law
was about to be enforced by
Chinese authorities in the district
led to a general scare, heightened
by a new outburst of activity
throughout the day on the part of
the Japanese Naval Landing
Party.
Alarm spread when it became
known that martial law had actu-
ally been proclaimed in the dis-
tricts around Shanghai following
an order issued by the Kiangsu
Provincial Government, and with
the new activity by Japanese
forces in Hongkew, Chinese house-
holders immediately began to re-
move their possessions by every
available conveyance, a thin tric-
kle in the morning developing into
a panic rush during the after-
noon and fading away to only an
occasional, belated refugee in the
evening.
The erection of telephone wires
by Japanese troops during the
morning and later the transporta-
tion of barbed-wire barricades to
various points in the city added
to the uneasiness prevailing at
Hongkew, and when increased
patrols of Marines were noted in
many districts, the tension
spread.
"Preventative Measure"
According to Chinese news
agencies, martial law was pro-
claimed in outside districts as a
preventative measure on the part
of the Chinese during the present
negotiations between Chinese and
Japanese diplomats of the two
countries' relations.
The order proclaiming martial
law stated that "during the time
when the Government is trying to
readjust the Sino-Japanese situa-
tion, there might be reactionary
elements which would attempt to
create disturbances, and thus com-
plicate the present situation." The
order also called for co-operation
on the part of the people in the
reporting of all suspicious revolu-
tionary characters.
Another report stated that dur-
ing the day a number of men,
alleged to have been employed for
the purpose of spreading alarmist
rumours in Hongkew and Chapei,
were arrested by the Chinese
authorities and sent to Lunghwa
to stand court martial.

《字林西报》，1936年10月1日，星期四
16950
市政
登记处
D. 7538
36年10月8日

虹口再次
恐慌

因谣传该区将实施
戒严令，撤离行动恢复

昨日下午，随着谣传中国当局将在该地区实施戒严令，引发普遍恐慌，加之日本海军陆战队全天活动再度爆发，闸北和虹口的撤离行动以更快的速度恢复。

当得知江苏省政府发布命令，在上海周边地区实际宣布戒严后，恐慌蔓延开来；加上日军在虹口的新动向，中国住户立即开始通过各种可用交通工具搬运财物，早晨的零星人流在下午发展为恐慌性奔逃，到了晚上则消退为偶尔出现的迟滞难民。

日军上午架设电话线，随后将铁丝网路障运往市内各处，加剧了虹口普遍存在的不安情绪；当在许多地区发现海军陆战队巡逻增加时，紧张局势进一步扩散。

“预防措施”

据中国新闻社报道，在中日两国就双边关系进行外交谈判期间，中方宣布在外围地区实施戒严令是一项预防措施。

宣布戒严的命令指出，“在政府试图调整中日局势期间，可能会有反动分子企图制造骚乱，从而使当前局势复杂化。”该命令还呼吁民众合作，举报所有可疑的革命分子。

另一则报道称，白天有多名据称受雇在虹口和闸北散布恐慌谣言的男子被中国当局逮捕，并送往龙华接受军事法庭审判。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 7, 1936

Fresh Exodus
From Chapei
Being Checked

Idle Rumor Mongers
Blamed For Latest
Movement Outward

The spread of a host of unfounded rumors in Chapei and Kiangwan yesterday started another exodus of residents in those areas into the International Settlement and the French Concession.

Despite the explanation and the assurances given by the Bureau of Public Safety officers, the movement of residents into the Central and Western districts of the foreign-controlled areas continued to gain more followers throughout the day.

Officers of the bureau told reporters last night that they believe that some groups of people were deliberately spreading groundless reports with malicious intent.

Around 7 o'clock last night, residents of the Civic Center were much disturbed by the report that trouble had started or was going to start in Shanghai. Authors of this piece of information announced that the lights on the Wing On Company tower, which can be seen for miles around had been turned off to prepare for an impending air raid.

Say Hand Grenades Distributed

Another report, which police officers branded as "Just as ridiculous," claimed that hand grenades and other deadly weapons had been distributed among the men of the Greater Shanghai Peace Preservation Corps as a measure for taking care of emergency.

Other rumors of a similar nature gained quick currency among the gullible portion of the Chapei and Kiangwan area populace. But despite the present tendency of the residents to move, officers of the Bureau of Public Safety were confident last night that the exodus yesterday would not assume the proportion of the one several days ago.

Meantime, the Hongkew area had returned to a state which gave the outward semblance of normality. Concern, however, still gripped the greater portion of the residents in that area. A tour through the district at nightfall revealed that practically no Japanese sentry was around and business and traffic had returned to its customary animated pace.

After dark, however, the streets and the night-life resorts were deserted, showing that residents were unwilling to venture outside their houses. On Haining Road and at the corner of Chimei Road, the spots where the two recent murders of Japanese took place, Naval Landing Party men were on guard. Passing pedestrians and motorists were closely scrutinised.

Across the Shanghai-Woosung railway tracks, in Chapei, a small group of Japanese soldiers continued to keep watch near the vicinity of the Japanese cemetery at Paitsachiao.

（批：切）
（批：J）

36年10月7日
《大美晚报》，1936年10月7日，星期三

闸北新一轮
外逃潮正受遏制

无聊谣言制造者
被指为最新外流
运动之起因

昨日，闸北和江湾地区大量毫无根据的谣言传播，引发了这些地区居民向公共租界和法租界的又一轮外逃。

尽管公安局警官作出了解释和保证，但居民向外国控制区域的中区和西区迁移的运动在整个白天继续吸引更多人参与。

该局警官昨晚告诉记者，他们认为某些人群出于恶意故意散布毫无根据的报告。

昨晚7点左右，大上海中心区（Civic Center）的居民因有关上海已发生或即将发生事端的报告而深感不安。这条消息的发布者声称，方圆数英里可见的先施公司（注：此处原文为Wing On Company，即永安公司）塔楼灯光已熄灭，以为即将到来的空袭做准备。

称手榴弹已分发

另一则被警官斥为“同样荒谬”的报告声称，作为应对紧急情况的措施，手榴弹和其他致命武器已分发给大上海和平维持团（Greater Shanghai Peace Preservation Corps，即保安团）的成员。

其他类似性质的谣言在闸北和江湾地区轻信的民众中迅速流传。但尽管目前居民有迁移倾向，公安局警官昨晚确信，昨天的外逃规模不会达到几天前的程度。

与此同时，虹口地区已恢复到表面正常的状态。然而，该地区大部分居民仍感到担忧。黄昏时分对该区的巡视显示，周围实际上没有日本哨兵，商业和交通已恢复往常的活跃节奏。

然而，天黑后，街道和夜生活场所空无一人，显示居民不愿走出家门。在海宁路和赤峰路（Chimei Road，音译，疑为赤峰路或附近道路）拐角处，即最近两起日本人被杀案的发生地，有海军陆战队队员站岗。过往行人和司机受到严密盘查。

越过沪淞铁路轨道，在闸北，一小股日本士兵继续在八字桥（Paitsachiao，音译）日本公墓附近保持警戒。

（批：切）
（批：J）

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, October 5, 1936
1691/6

Japanese Raid
Chinese Police,
Hunt For Spies

Chapei Station Offers
No Resistance; Raid
Made On Villages

KUWAJIMA HOLDS
ATTENTION NOW

Hongkew More Normal,
Patrols Taken Off,
Trade As Usual

A branch station of the Bureau
of Public Safety of the City
Government of Greater Shanghai,
housed in the neighborhood of the
Japanese Rokusan Garden near
Tientungan, was raided by two
batches of officers and men from
the Japanese Special Naval Land-
ing Party at 8 o'clock last night,
it was learned today.

With a group of plainclothes
men throwing a cordon around
the station, about 20 officers and
men, arriving in two groups,
entered the Chinese police station
and searched every room. The
Japanese officers are said to have
explained that the search was for
spies who are said to be hiding
inside the building. The Chinese
officers offered no resistance to
the invasion and the subsequent
search.

Villages Visited

Causing much anxiety among
the populace, small groups of
Japanese bluejackets last night
visited the Chuanchnako and
Hochacha villages in Chapei.
They knocked at the doors and
aroused the villagers. After re-
maining in the village for a brief
time, they left.

More than 300 Japanese blue-
jackets, headed by their officers,
early this morning marched from
their barracks to the Hongkew
Park for drill. They took with
them machine guns and rifle
pieces.

"Spies" Hunted

Chinese authorities in and
around Shanghai are redoubling
their efforts to round up spies be-
lieved to have been hired by
Japanese to obtain information
on military movements. Five
Chinese Buddhist monks were ar-
rested in Tachang, a city west
of Shanghai, yesterday. Secret
identification marks were found
in their gowns, it is said. They
are being held at the magistrate's
office for questioning.

In Tachang, scene of a Sino-
Japanese battle in 1932, two, one
a monk and another a beggar,
were arrested last month. Con-
clusive evidence had been found
against them, it is said. The
suspects had been sent to the
Third District Peace Preservation
Headquarters for trial before a
military court.

Hongkew More Quiet

With the Hongkew and Chapei
districts fast resuming their
normal appearance after 11 days
of tension, interest today veered
to the arrival at 5:50 o'clock in
the afternoon of Mr. Kasue Ku-
wajima, director of the Bureau
of East Asiatic Affairs of the
Tokyo Foreign Office.

Bringing with him what is gen-
erally described by the Japanese
as "the last word" of the Tokyo
authorities regarding the present
Sino-Japanese negotiations for a
readjustment of the relations be-
tween the two countries, Mr.
Kuwajima, immediately after his
arrival, was to go into conference
with the highest local representa-
tive of the Japanese Army, Navy
and Foreign Affairs Ministries.
The high Gaimusho official will
entrain for Nanking at 11 o'clock
tonight.

To See Envoy

In the capital, where he is
scheduled to remain two to three
days, he will discuss at length the
present state of Sino-Japanese
relations with Ambassador Shigeru
Kawagoe and Mr. Yakichiro Suma,
consul-general in Nanking.

With uneasiness among the
Japanese residents dispelled to a
large extent, all Nipponese schools
today resumed normal all-day
schedules to the chagrin of pupils
who, for one week, enjoyed half
holidays. Special precautions were
taken by the S.M.P. and the
Japanese Consular Police to guard
the children against untoward
events.

Patrols Diminished

Japanese Naval Landing Party
sentry posts and patrols had been
markedly diminished. All men on
guard carried their arms in "at
ease" positions without fixed
bayonets.

Large quantities of unsigned
handbills, printed in red, urging
the Chinese people to stand
against Japan were scattered from
the roofs of the Sun Sun and
Wing On Department stores on
Nanking Road at about 5:20
o'clock yesterday afternoon, ac-
cording to Japanese reports. Of-
ficers were rushed to the two
establishments from the Louza
Police Station nearby but no ar-
rests were made, they said.

The text of the handbills de-
nounced the operations of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party in
Shanghai.

The revival of the police-post
system, abolished after the adop-
tion of the best patrol scheme by
the S.M.P. is being advocated
among Japanese, it is also reported.

The major obstacle was the
lack of sufficient appropriations.

6 10 36

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年10月5日，星期一
1691/6

日军突袭
中国警察，
搜捕间谍

闸北分局未加抵抗；
突袭村庄

今井（Kuwajima）此刻
备受瞩目

虹口趋于正常，
巡逻撤除，
贸易如常

据悉，昨晚8时，两批日本特别海军陆战队官兵突袭了位于天通庵附近、日本六三花园一带的大上海市政府公安局的一个分所。

一群便衣人员对该分局形成包围圈后，约20名官兵分两组进入中国警察局，搜查了每个房间。据称，日本军官解释说，搜查是为了寻找据信藏匿在楼内的间谍。中国警官对此次入侵及随后的搜查未作任何抵抗。

走访村庄

昨晚，小股日本水兵走访了闸北的川沙口（Chuanchnako，音译）和何家宅（Hochacha，音译）村，引起民众极大焦虑。他们敲门并唤醒村民。在村里短暂停留后，他们离去。

今天清晨，300多名日本水兵在军官率领下，从兵营行进至虹口公园进行操练。他们携带了机枪和步枪部件。

搜捕“间谍”

上海及周边地区的中国当局正加倍努力，围捕据信受雇于日本以获取军事调动情报的间谍。昨天，在上海西面的大场镇逮捕了五名中国佛教僧侣。据说在他们的长袍中发现了秘密识别标记。他们正被羁押在地方法院接受讯问。

在大场——1932年中日战斗的发生地——上个月逮捕了两名嫌疑人，其中一人是僧侣，另一人是乞丐。据说已发现针对他们的确凿证据。这些嫌疑人已被送往第三区保安总部，由军事法庭审判。

虹口较为平静

经过11天的紧张局势后，虹口和闸北地区迅速恢复正常面貌，今天的关注点转向东京外务省东亚局局长今井（Kasue Kuwajima）先生于下午5时50分的抵达。

今井先生带来了被日本人普遍描述为东京当局关于当前中日调整两国关系谈判的“最后意见”。他抵达后立即与日本陆军、海军和外务省的最高当地代表举行会议。这位外务省高级官员将于今晚11时乘火车前往南京。

会见公使

在首都，他计划停留两到三天，将与川越茂（Shigeru Kawagoe）大使和驻南京总领事须磨弥吉郎（Yakichiro Suma）先生详细讨论当前的中日关系状况。

随着日本侨民的不安情绪在很大程度上得到消除，所有日本学校今天恢复了全天的正常课程，这让享受了一周半假期的学生们感到懊恼。公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）和日本领事警察采取了特别预防措施，保护儿童免受意外事件伤害。

巡逻减少

日本海军陆战队的哨位和巡逻明显减少。所有执勤人员均以“稍息”姿势持枪，未上刺刀。

据日方报道，昨天下午5时20分左右，大量未署名的红色印刷传单从南京路的新新百货公司和永安百货公司的屋顶撒下，呼吁中国人民抵制日本。警官们从附近的老闸捕房迅速赶往这两处场所，但据称并未实施逮捕。

传单内容谴责了日本海军陆战队在上海的行动。

另据报道，在日本人中有人主张恢复警岗制度，该制度曾在工部局警务处采用最佳巡逻方案后被废除。

主要障碍是缺乏足够的拨款。

6 10 36

16917
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 6, 1936

MINOR INCIDENT
CAUSES RUMOUR
Mafoo And Veterinary
Surgeon In Dispute
At Kiangwan
NERVOUSNESS IN
CHAPEI AGAIN
Rumours last night of fighting
between Japanese and Chinese in
the Kiangwan district proved, on
enquiry, to have arisen from a
minor incident at Kiangwan race-
course where there was an alter-
cation during the afternoon be-
tween a Japanese veterinary sur-
geon and a mafoo.
It is understood that the "vet."
accused the mafoo of stealing
medicine and that the Chinese was
arrested by officers of the Peace
Preservation Corps after one or
two blows had actually been struck.
The mafoo, who was later ordered
to apologize and to pay the
Japanese veterinary surgeon the
cost of the missing medicine, was
released after investigations.
A tense atmosphere is said to
have revived in Chapei following
the raid carried out by Japanese
marines on a Chinese police
station on Sunday night, and the
continued activities of the Japan-
ese Naval Landing Party in the
region. According to Chinese re-
ports, a special lookout station has
been constructed on the roof of
the Japanese brewery near Roku-
san Gardens, where the strength
of the outpost is said to have been
largely increased.

《字林西报》，1936年10月6日，星期二

小事件
引发谣言

马夫与兽医
在江湾发生争执

闸北再次
出现紧张情绪

昨晚有关江湾地区中日之间发生战斗的谣言，经查询证实，源于江湾赛马场发生的一起小事件，当天下午一名日本兽医与一名马夫发生了争吵。

据了解，这名“兽医”指控马夫偷窃药品，在实际上发生了一两下击打后，该中国人被保安队警官逮捕。该马夫后来被责令道歉并向日本兽医赔偿丢失药品的费用，经调查后获释。

据称，继周日晚上日本海军陆战队突袭中国警察局以及日本海军陆战队在该地区持续活动之后，闸北的紧张气氛再次回升。据中方报道，在六三花园附近的日本啤酒厂屋顶上建立了一个专门的瞭望站，据说该前哨的力量已大幅增加。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 2538
October 6, 1936. Morning Translations 6/ 10 / 36

Hwa Mei Wan Pao and Shanghai Evening News of October 5 :-

JAPANESE MARINES SEARCH CHAPEI POLICE STATION.

The situation in the various districts in
Chapei and Hongkew was quiet yesterday. On the night of
October 4, a scene was created near the Japanese Rokusan
Garden as the result of a search conducted by Japanese
marines at the Tien Tung An Police Station of the Bureau
of Public Safety. No official report has been made by
the authorities regarding this affair. However, according
to an investigation made by a reporter of this paper, the
incident was due to a misunderstanding.
At about 8 p.m. October 4, a small group of
Japanese marines patrolled Dung Ohi Road and Kiangwan Road,
Chapei. Several country men upon seeing the marines near
the Japanese Rokusan Garden began to run away, some going
in the direction of the Police Station. This aroused the
suspicion of the Japanese marines who forced their way into
the Station. The Japanese marines did not understand
Chinese nor were any of the officers at the Police Station
able to speak Japanese. Subsequently, the Japanese patrols
proceeded to the Japanese Rokusan Garden where two of them
remained outside while the others went inside and notified
the branch station of the Japanese Landing Forces at Hwa
Yuan Ka by a military telephone. Shortly afterwards, a
Japanese military truck with more than 20 Japanese marines
in full military kit and armed with a machine gun was
despatched to the place. In company with the Japanese
marines previously mentioned, they surrounded the Police
Station. The situation became very delicate. The
Japanese entered the Police Station and searched the
premises. The police officers remained quiet and calm.
A Japanese resident acted as interpreter. The
misunderstanding was finally cleared up and the Japanese
marines withdrew. However, Japanese sentries and patrols
were posted along Hwa Yuan Ka and the Japanese Rokusan
Garden until about 7 a.m. October 5.

It is learned that more than 1,000 Japanese
soldiers landed on the night of October 3 at the Wei Tu
Wharf at the end of Yangtzepoo.
Four or five armed Japanese marines were
still posted at the corner of North Szechuen Road and
Jukong Road, Sze Dah Road and in front of the Japanese
Marine Posts. The situation at other places is the same
as before. However, the number of posts on Dixwell Road
seemed to have been increased and patrols were likewise
more numerous.
The strength of the Japanese marines in the
Japanese Brewery behind the Rokusan Garden was increased
by more than 50 marines. Precautionary measures are
still being adopted in the vicinity of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party Headquarters, its various branch stations
in the International Settlement and at various places at
Hwa Yuan Ka in Chapei.

10月5日的《华美晚报》和《上海晚报》：

日本海军陆战队搜查闸北警察局。

昨天，闸北和虹口各区的局势平静。10月4日晚，由于日本海军陆战队对公安局天通庵警察局进行搜查，在日本六三花园附近造成了一场风波。当局尚未就此事件发布官方报告。然而，根据本报记者的调查，该事件是由于误会引起的。

10月4日晚8时许，一小队日本海军陆战队在闸北的邓欧路（Dung Ohi Road，音译）和江湾路巡逻。几名乡下人在日本六三花园附近看到海军陆战队后开始逃跑，一些人朝警察局方向跑去。这引起了日本海军陆战队的怀疑，他们强行进入警局。日本海军陆战队不懂中文，警察局的警官也没有人能说日语。随后，日本巡逻队前往日本六三花园，其中两人留在外面，其他人进去并通过军用电话通知了华元卡（Hwa Yuan Ka，音译）的日本登陆部队分站。不久之后，一辆载有20多名全副武装、配备机枪的日本海军陆战队员的军用卡车被派往该地。他们与此前提到的日本海军陆战队一起包围了警察局。局势变得非常微妙。日本人进入警察局并搜查了场所。警察保持安静和冷静。一名日本居民担任翻译。误会最终得以澄清，日本海军陆战队撤离。然而，直到10月5日早上7点左右，日本哨兵和巡逻队一直部署在华元卡和日本六三花园沿线。

据悉，10月3日晚，1000多名日本士兵在杨树浦末端的威妥码头（Wei Tu Wharf，音译）登陆。

仍有四五名武装日本海军陆战队员驻扎在北四川路与鞠恭路（Jukong Road，音译）、四达路（Sze Dah Road，音译）的拐角处以及日本海军陆战队哨所前。其他地方的情况与以前相同。然而，狄思威路（Dixwell Road，音译）上的哨位数量似乎有所增加，巡逻队也更多了。

六三花园后面的日本啤酒厂内的日本海军陆战队兵力增加了50多人。在国际租界的日本海军陆战队总部、其各分站以及闸北华元卡的各个地方，仍在采取预防措施。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. REGISTRY.
No. D 7538.
October 6, 1936.    Morning Tradition.

According to information secured by a reporter
of the Ta Kung News Agency, the Japanese marines during the
past several days have been busy constructing an underground
path inside the Japanese Brewery behind the Rokusan Garden.
According to information secured from the
residents along Kiangwan Road, Chi Mei Road and Tung Chi
Road by a reporter of the Sin Sin News Agency, the Japanese
marines have been very active during the past few days.
Pedestrians passing by these districts were subjected to
strict search by the marines.

Lih Pao :-

The Arbitrary Arrests of Residents by Japanese
Marines

According to "Oz Pei"(波士貝), Secretary
to the British Consulate-General in Shanghai, the S.M.C.
has not yet referred to the Consular Body the question of
the reckless extension of patrols and the arbitrary arrest
of residents in the International Settlement by the Japanese
Landing Force. None of the Consuls have expressed views
on these matters.

The Sung Veh Sunday Periodical (生活星期刊) of October 4 :-

The Hongkew Incident.

At about 8.30 p.m. September 23 one Japanese
marine was killed and two others were wounded on Haining
Road. Shortly afterwards, a large number of Japanese
marines and tanks arrived at the spot and pedestrians were
not allowed to approach the scene of the crime; Chapoo,
Yalu, Woosung and Range Roads were completely under their
control. A rigorous search was conducted by the marines.
In connection with the incident, we desire to
bring the following facts to the notice of readers :-
(1) A congee hawker named Chang Yung Woo was
arrested because his appearance was suspicious for he was
wearing a worn-out foreign-style shirt. Two brothers named
Ma, who were returning home from their place of employment,
a printing shop, upon seeing what had happened on Haining
Road began to retrace their steps but were arrested. These
three suspects were handed over to the Police after
negotiations by the Settlement authorities.
(2) The Japanese posts were detailed to Chinese
controlled territory.
(3) This incident took place in the International
Settlement and in an area regularly patrolled by the Japanese
Police, yet the Japanese are holding the Chinese Government
responsible. Several days after the incident, the Japanese
newspapers in Shanghai published rumours that 30,000 plain-
clothes Peace Preservation Corps had arrived in Shanghai and
that Chinese military forces were being concentrated in the
vicinity of Soochow and Kashing. All these rumours were
refuted by the Chinese Government. On the other hand, large
reinforcements of the Japanese marines arrived in Shanghai.
We deeply regret the unfortunate incidents
befalling foreigners residing in China but the Chinese people
will never accept any more demands.

1936年10月6日。晨间译文。

据大公新闻社记者获得的消息，过去几天，日本海军陆战队一直在六三花园后面的日本啤酒厂内忙着修建一条地下通道。

据欣欣新闻社记者从江湾路、集美路（Chi Mei Road，音译）和同济路（Tung Chi Road，音译）沿线的居民处获得的消息，过去几天日本海军陆战队非常活跃。经过这些地区的行人受到海军陆战队的严格搜查。

《立报》：

日本海军陆战队任意逮捕居民

据上海英国总领事馆秘书“Oz Pei”（波士貝，音译）称，工部局尚未就日本登陆部队在国际租界内肆意扩大巡逻范围和任意逮捕居民的问题向领事团提出交涉。各位领事均未就此事项发表意见。

10月4日的《生活星期刊》：

虹口事件。

9月23日晚8时30分左右，一名日本海军陆战队员在海宁路被杀，另外两名受伤。不久之后，大批日本海军陆战队员和坦克到达现场，行人不得靠近犯罪现场；乍浦路、鸭绿江路（Yalu Road，音译）、吴淞路和兰路（Range Road，音译）完全处于他们的控制之下。海军陆战队进行了严密的搜查。

关于此事件，我们希望提请读者注意以下事实：
(1) 一名名叫张永武（Chang Yung Woo，音译）的粥贩因形迹可疑被捕，因为他穿着一件破旧的外国式衬衫。姓马的两兄弟从工作地点印刷厂回家，看到海宁路上发生的事情后开始折返，但也被逮捕。经租界当局交涉后，这三名嫌疑人被移交给警方。
(2) 日本哨所被部署到中国控制的领土。
(3) 此事件发生在国际租界内，且位于日本警察定期巡逻的区域，但日本方面却要求中国政府承担责任。事件发生几天后，上海的日本报纸散布谣言，称3万名便衣保安队已抵达上海，中国军队正在苏州和嘉兴附近集结。所有这些谣言均被中国政府驳斥。另一方面，大批日本海军陆战队增援部队抵达上海。

我们对居住在中国的外国人遭遇的不幸事件深表遗憾，但中国人民绝不会接受任何进一步的要求。

October 5, 1936.    Morning Translation.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY. No. D 7538. Date 5 / 10 / 36）

Lih Pao publishes in its Readers' Forum the following letter
to the editor by one Yen Liang (英良):

ATTITUDE OF S.M.C. CRITICIZED

The International Settlement of Shanghai has
always been regarded by a certain section of the Chinese people
as a place of safety but during the past few years it has
become a place of greater uneasiness, especially in view of
the fact that Chinese residents in the Settlement are
frequently subjected to unreasonable oppression and arrest.
Take, for instance, the unfortunate incident
that occurred recently on Haining Road. The S.M.C. had
been negligent in adopting precautionary measures prior to
the incident and had failed to adopt adequate measures to deal
with the incident afterwards; therefore, it cannot evade
its responsibility. As a matter of fact, the Settlement
Police should have stopped the marines of a certain nation
from removing the two marines who were wounded and the dead
body of the marine who was fatally shot; the Police should
have first made an examination and taken a photograph as
evidence and then assisted the marine authorities of that
nation to remove the deceased and the wounded marines to a
hospital. In this way, the Settlement Police could say
that they had carried out their duty. However, the Settlement
Police failed to do these things but allowed the marines of
that nation to remove the victims and afterwards they
even permitted the marines to conduct searches of dwelling
houses, to arrest innocent pedestrians, to obstruct traffic
and to convey arrested persons for detention at their Landing
Party Headquarters to be dealt with at their will.
All this shows that Chinese residing in the
International Settlement, though obliged to pay taxes, are
not being given proper protection. Under the circumstances,
it is therefore only natural for us to fear for our future
safety in the Settlement. I am of the opinion that such
a fear does exist in the minds of Chinese residents and of
foreign residents as well.
We wonder whether the S.M.C. will again follow
the attitude which it adopted five years ago when it permitted
the marines of a certain nation to use the Settlement as a
military base for aggression against China. If the S.M.C.
has no such intention, then we hope that the Council will
accord similar protection to all residents in the Settlement
irrespective of nationality and adopt rigorous measures
to put a stop to the free action of the marines.

Lih Pao publishes another letter in its Reader's Forum from one
Liao Kwang Hwa (廖光華) :-

Interference With Chinese Military Training

Our friendly neighbour has always alleged that
the Chinese students are the principal elements who are
anti-X; it has therefore always obstructed the military
training of Chinese students.
However, according to a telegram from Tsingtao,
dated September 21, several hundred students of middle schools
of the XX residents held military drills at Kanshan (    ).

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别分部档案室。编号 D 7538。日期 36/10/5）

《立报》在其“读者论坛”栏目刊登了一封由英良（Yen Liang）写给编辑的信：

批评工部局的态度

上海公共租界一向被部分中国人视为安全之地，但在过去几年中，这里已变得令人更加不安，尤其是鉴于租界内的中国居民经常遭受不合理的压迫和逮捕。以最近发生在海宁路的不幸事件为例。工部局在事发前未能采取预防措施，事后也未能采取适当措施处理该事件；因此，它无法推卸其责任。事实上，租界巡捕本应阻止某国海军陆战队移走两名受伤的海军陆战队员以及一名被枪击身亡的海军陆战队员的尸体；巡捕本应先进行检查并拍照取证，然后协助该国海军当局将死者和伤者送往医院。这样，租界巡捕便可称其已履行职责。然而，租界巡捕并未这样做，而是任由该国海军陆战队员移走受害者，随后甚至允许海军陆战队员搜查住宅、逮捕无辜行人、阻碍交通，并将被捕人员押送至其登陆队总部，任其随意处置。
所有这一切表明，居住在公共租界的中国人虽然必须纳税，却未得到适当的保护。在这种情况下，我们自然会对未来在租界的安全感到担忧。我认为，这种恐惧不仅存在于中国居民心中，也存在于外国居民心中。
我们想知道，工部局是否会再次采取五年前的态度，当时它允许某国海军陆战队利用租界作为侵略中国的军事基地。如果工部局没有此类意图，那么我们希望公董局能对租界内所有居民给予同等保护，不论其国籍如何，并采取严厉措施制止海军陆战队的自由行动。

《立报》在其“读者论坛”栏目还刊登了另一封来自廖光華（Liao Kwang Hwa）的信：

干涉中国学生军训

我们的友好邻邦一直声称中国学生是反X的主要分子；因此，它一直阻挠中国学生的军事训练。
然而，据9月21日发自青岛的电讯称，XX居民的几所中学的数百名学生在干山（Kanshan，原文不清）进行了军事演习。

5: 10.1.36
Chinese Saturday Post (禮拜六), a weekly periodical, published
the following article on Oct. 3:

THE HONGKEW INCIDENT

On the night of September 23 a terrible case
occurred in Shanghai. As it took place in Hongkew district
of the International Settlement (Woosung and Haining Roads
corner), it was therefore called the Hongkew Incident.
According to a statement made by an eye-witness,
it was at about 8 p.m. September 23 that pistol shots were
suddenly heard at the corner of Haining and Woosung Roads.
Before policemen could reach the spot, the place was already
swarming with Japanese marines; the assassins made good
their escape. Shortly afterwards, a commotion followed.
The Japanese marines began their activities and conducted
a search of the dwelling houses and the pedestrians in the
neighbourhood. No pedestrians, not even newspaper
reporters, were allowed to walk within 30 feet of the scene
of the crime. People heard that a Chinese hawker named
Chang Yung Woo (張榮和) and several other persons had been
taken by Japanese marines to the Landing Party Headquarters
on suspicion, for some unknown reason, of being the culprits.
The events that took place afterwards were more
terrible. A Japanese military truck dashing left and
right nearly collided with a No.7 Route tramcar. Emergency
measures were immediately proclaimed in the Hongkew district,
while armed Japanese marines stood on guard on the borders
of the International Settlement and Chinese controlled
territory in Chapel. The district seemed to have
fallen entirely into the hands of the Japanese. The
incident took place in the International Settlement, yet
the inhabitants of Chinese controlled territory became so
terror-stricken that they began to remove their homes.
Patriotic Chinese realize full well that such
acts of terrorism would simply afford the enemy a pretext
for aggression, less patriotic Chinese do not possess
sufficient courage to undertake such an enormous risk as
shooting a Japanese marine. As regards professional
murderers, they are not anxious for such kinds of terrorism.
As for the statement that so-called communists are trying
to create Sino-Japanese dissension, this is merely a nice
expression of the Japanese Foreign Minister Arita and
represents the erroneous view of XX Imperialists that Chinese
communists are not patriotic. Therefore, it is clear
that the incident had been deliberately created by XX,
although we are not in a position to prove that it had been
agreed upon by important officials with the deceased
beforehand. The present incident was not accidental.
The Chinese Government dealt with the Chengtu, Pakhoi,
Fengtai and Hankow Incidents on the principle of conciliation
and the enemy in each incident had attained its minimum
object. How would the enemy act to realize its four
maximum demands? To attain this, another pretext was
required; thus the so-called Hongkew Incident took place.
If the Chinese Government continues to deal with this
incident on the principle of conciliation, it is possible
that further incidents of this nature may be expected.

(印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER
5 OCT. 1936
CRIME BRANCH)

中文周刊《礼拜六》于10月3日发表了以下文章：

虹口事件

9月23日晚，上海发生了一起可怕的案件。由于该事件发生在公共租界虹口区（吴淞路与海宁路转角），因此被称为“虹口事件”。
据一位目击者陈述，9月23日晚8点左右，突然听到海宁路与吴淞路转角处传来手枪声。在警察到达现场之前，该地已挤满了日本海军陆战队员；刺客趁机逃脱。不久之后，随之发生了一阵骚动。日本海军陆战队员开始行动，对附近的住宅和行人进行搜索。任何行人，包括报纸记者，均不得在距离犯罪现场30英尺范围内行走。人们听说，一名名叫张荣和（Chang Yung Woo）的中国小贩及其他几人因被怀疑为凶手（原因不明）而被日本海军陆战队员带至登陆队总部。
随后发生的事件更为可怕。一辆日本军用卡车左右冲撞，险些撞上一辆7路电车。虹口区随即宣布实行紧急措施，武装的日本海军陆战队员在公共租界与闸北中国控制地区的边界上站岗放哨。该地区似乎完全落入日本人手中。事件发生在公共租界内，但中国控制区的居民却惊恐万状，开始搬迁家园。
爱国的中国人充分认识到，此类恐怖行径只会给敌人提供侵略的借口；不够爱国的中国人则缺乏足够的勇气去承担枪杀一名日本海军陆战队员的巨大风险。至于职业杀手，他们并不热衷于此类恐怖活动。至于所谓共产党人试图制造中日不和的说法，这仅仅是日本外相有田（Arita）的一种美化说辞，代表了XX帝国主义者认为中国共产党人不爱国的错误观点。因此，很明显，该事件是由XX蓄意制造的，尽管我们无法证明重要官员事先已与死者达成协定。当前的事件并非偶然。中国政府本着和解原则处理了成都、北海、丰台和汉口事件，敌人在每次事件中都达到了其最低目标。敌人将如何行动以实现其四项最高要求？为此，需要另一个借口；于是所谓的“虹口事件”便发生了。如果中国政府继续本着和解原则处理此事件，那么可能会预期发生更多此类事件。

（印：副总监
1936年10月5日
刑事科）

October 5, 1936. Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao :-

NORMAL CONDITIONS IN HONGKEW

The additional marine posts detailed by the
Japanese Naval Landing Party along North Szechuen Road were
withdrawn on the morning of October 3. However, four or
five Japanese marines are still on guard in the vicinity of
Jukong Road and Sz Dah Road.

A reporter of this paper made an inspection
yesterday morning and found definite signs of improvement
in the district. The number of Japanese marines on duty
in Jukong Road, Tien Tung An Railway Station and other
places have been reduced to two. The situation has now
returned to normalcy. The situation in Chapei is also
quiet.

1936年10月5日。上午译文。

《大公报》：

虹口局势恢复正常

日本海军登陆队沿北四川路增派的额外哨位于10月3日上午撤除。然而，仍有四五名日本海军陆战队员在掘港路（Jukong Road，音译）和施达路（Sz Dah Road，音译）附近站岗。

本报记者昨晨视察发现，该地区情况有明显改善。在掘港路、天通庵火车站（Tien Tung An Railway Station，音译）等地执勤的日本海军陆战队员人数已减至两人。目前局势已恢复正常。闸北局势也很平静。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, OCTOBER 4, 1936

TAMINATO MURDER
SEQUEL

Two Suspects Freed; Third
Remanded Till Oct. 9

Following the sentencing on Friday
afternoon of Yang Ven-tao and Yih
Hai-sen to pay the death penalty
for the shooting of H. Nakayama, a
Japanese sailor, the hearing was
opened in the First Special District
Court yesterday morning of the case
where three Kompo men, Tsang
Yoong-wo, a hawker, Mau Yung-sau,
printer, and May Yung-nyi, printer,
were detained on suspicion of being
involved in the latest Hongkew
shooting in which another Japanese
sailor, A. Taminato, was killed on
the night of September 23 on Hain-
ing Road.

At the conclusion of yesterday's
hearing, the two Maus, who are
brothers, were ordered to be released
by the Judge as there was insuf-
ficient evidence against either of
them. The two Maus told the court
that they were returning home in
East Kashing Road from a Shan-
haikwan printing shop and were
passing Haining Road when they
were arrested on the night in ques-
tion.

In connection with the detention
of Tsang Yoong-wo, three Japanese
witnesses testified in the District
Court yesterday, these being Messrs.
T. Horiye, T. Suehiro, and H.
Miyata. One of the witnesses
stated that, immediately after
the shooting of September 23,
he saw in an alleyway the detained
hawker near a sand-box with one
of his hands between the lid of the
sand-box. Witness said he went over
and, when the lid of the sand-box
was opened, a pistol was found
inside. The other two witnesses
supported the first witness's evidence,
adding that, after they had heard
the shots, they ran into the same
alleyway where they assisted in ar-
resting the hawker.

Questioned by the Judge, Tsang
Yoong-wo stuck to his old story that
he was a soup hawker and he went
to an alleyway to look for his two
comrades on the night when he was
arrested by the Japanese. He denied
having any part in the murder of
the sailor on Haining Road.

As many more witnesses are to be
called, the Judge ordered Tsang to
be returned to custody and brought
before the court again on October
9 for a special hearing.

《字林西报》，1936年10月4日，星期日

田凑（Taminato）谋杀案
后续

两名嫌疑人获释；第三名还押至10月9日

继周五下午判处杨文道（Yang Ven-tao，音译）和易海森（Yih Hai-sen，音译）因枪杀日本水手H. Nakayama而死刑后，第一特区法院于昨日上午开庭审理另一起案件，三名工人——小贩曾荣武（Tsang Yoong-wo，音译）、印刷工茅永寿（Mau Yung-sau，音译）和印刷工梅永义（May Yung-nyi，音译）——因涉嫌卷入最新的虹口枪击案而被拘留，该案中另一名日本水手A. Taminato于9月23日晚在海宁路遇害。

在昨日的听证会结束时，法官命令释放茅氏兄弟，因为针对他们两人的证据不足。茅氏兄弟向法庭陈述，案发当晚他们正从一家山海关印刷店返回位于东嘉兴路的家中，途经海宁路时被捕。

关于拘留曾荣武一事，三名日本证人在特区法院作证，他们是堀江先生（T. Horiye）、末广先生（T. Suehiro）和宫田先生（H. Miyata）。其中一名证人陈述，在9月23日枪击发生后，他立即在一条小巷里看到被拘留的小贩在一个沙箱旁，一只手伸在沙箱盖之间。该证人说他走过去，当打开沙箱盖时，在里面发现了一支手枪。另外两名证人支持第一位证人的证词，并补充说，他们在听到枪声后跑进同一条小巷，协助逮捕了该小贩。

经法官讯问，曾荣武坚持其原有说法，称他是一个汤贩，在被日本人逮捕的那晚，他去小巷寻找他的两个同伴。他否认参与在海宁路谋杀水手一案。

由于还将传唤更多证人，法官命令将曾还押候审，并于10月9日再次出庭进行特别听证。

Hawkers' Alibi
Begins To Fade

Taminato Case Heard
By Court; Testimony
Involves Chang

(Concluded from Page 1)
tention to enable police to carry

Mr. Tadashi Horiye, Japanese
tailor, residing at Lane 332, 114
Woosung Road, said that about
8:30 o'clock on the night of
September 23, he heard shots and
rushed out of into the street
where he saw a crowd gathered.
He heard people proclaiming that
a Japanese had been shot and
that the shots had come from the
direction of Lane 115.
"You are the Man!"
He said that he ran to the
mouth of the lane and saw a
Chinese woman kneeling on the
ground.
"Nearby was a Chinese man
who had the lid of a sandbox
open about six inches. His right
hand was half in and half out
of the box and I saw there was
a dark object in his hand which
he was pushing into the box."
Mr. Horiye then shouted: "You
are the man" The person then
withdrew his hand and dropped
the lid of the box down. Mr.
Horiye told the court that he
then seized the man and handed
him over to two or three Japan-
ese who came up at the time.

Saw Pistol
"I looked in the box and there
was a Mauser pistol lying on the
top of the sand. I gave it to mem-
bers of the Japanese Naval Land-
ing Party."

Teruo Suehiro, a radio sales-
man, took the stand, saying that
on September 23, he heard what
at first he thought was the sound
of firecrackers but then decided
was rifle shots. Rushing into the
street he saw a Japanese marine
lying in the road and two more
over in a bookshop, at No. 463
Woosung Road, seemingly wound-
ed.

Chang Denies
He too, he said, rushed to the
alleyway, followed by another
Japanese, Hajime Miyata, where
they saw the man Chang about
to put something in the sandbox.
They came up and helped Mr.
Hiroys to seize him.
Chang stoutly denied all the
allegations against him and said
that he was only on the street
selling his wares. He was re-
manded in custody for a week.

小贩的不在场证明
开始动摇

田凑案受审；
证词涉及张

（接第1版）
...以便警方进行调查。

日本裁缝堀江正（Tadashi Horiye，音译）先生，居住于吴淞路114号332弄，他说，9月23日晚8点30分左右，他听到枪声并冲到街上，看到人群聚集。他听到人们宣称一名日本人被枪击，枪声来自115弄方向。
“就是你这个人！”
他说他跑到弄堂口，看到一名中国妇女跪在地上。
“附近有一名中国男子将沙箱盖打开了约六英寸。他的右手半进半出箱子，我看到他手里有一个深色物体，正将其推入箱内。”
堀江先生随即喊道：“就是你这个人！”那人随后缩回手，放下了箱盖。堀江先生告诉法庭，他随后抓住该男子，并将其移交给当时赶来的两三名日本人。

看见手枪
“我往箱子里看，发现一把毛瑟手枪躺在沙子表面。我把它交给了日本海军登陆队成员。”

无线电销售员末广照雄（Teruo Suehiro，音译）出庭作证，他说，9月23日，他听到起初以为是鞭炮声，但随后断定是步枪射击声。他冲到街上，看到一名日本海军陆战队员躺在路上，另外两名在吴淞路463号的一家书店里，似乎受了伤。

张否认指控
他说，他也冲进小巷，另一名日本人宫田始（Hajime Miyata，音译）紧随其后，在那里他们看到张姓男子正要把什么东西放进沙箱。他们上前协助堀江先生抓住他。
张坚决否认所有针对他的指控，并称他当时只是在街上售卖货物。他被还押候审一周。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, OCTOBER 4, 1936

HONGKEW SHOOTING
OUTRAGE

Two Of Three Suspects
Released For Lack
Of Evidence

Two of the three men arrested following the murder on September 28 of First Class Seaman Taminato in Haining Road were released yesterday by the First Special District Court.

The third accused Chang Yung-ho, a congee seller, was remanded for a week, although he continued to deny that he had any knowledge of the crime.

No charge was framed against Chang, the police merely asking that he be remanded for a week to facilitate further investigations.

Mr. Chang Shin-tsu, Assistant Municipal Advocate, told the court that 25 witnesses had testified against accused at the police station. Only three Japanese witnesses, however, appeared in court.

The first witness, a tailor, said that after the shooting he ran out and saw Chang opening a sand box and putting a black object into it. After catching Chang he opened the box and picked out the pistol. The two other witnesses testified to the same effect, explaining that they helped the tailor to catch Chang.

Chang admitted that he was caught by the Japanese witnesses but denied that he had any knowledge of the crime. It is understood that police have confirmed that Chang had a friend maintaining a stand near the scene of crime and that Chang himself also kept a congee stand near the alley in front of which he was caught.

It was announced by the police that the pistol found in the sand box had been examined by experts and found to be the one from which the fatal bullets were fired.

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1936年10月4日

虹口枪击
暴行

三名嫌疑人中的两人
因证据不足
获释

在9月28日海宁路一等水手田凑（Taminato）被杀案后被捕的三名男子中，有两人于昨日由第一特区法院释放。

第三名被告张永和，一名粥贩，被还押一周，尽管他继续否认对罪行有任何知情。

警方未对张提出正式指控，仅请求将其还押一周，以便进行进一步调查。

助理市检察官张新祖先生向法庭陈述，有25名证人在警察局作证指认被告。然而，出庭作证的日本证人仅有三名。

第一名证人是一名裁缝，他说枪击发生后他跑出去，看见张正在打开一个沙箱，并将一个黑色物体放入其中。抓住张后，他打开箱子并取出了手枪。另外两名证人的证词与此相同，并解释称他们协助裁缝抓住了张。

张承认被日本证人抓获，但否认对罪行有任何知情。据悉，警方已证实张有一名朋友在案发现场附近摆摊，而张本人也在其被捕处前方的弄堂附近摆有一个粥摊。

警方宣布，在沙箱中发现的手枪已经过专家检验，确认为发射致命子弹的那支手枪。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, OCTOBER 4, 1936

Two Suspects
In Yalu Road
Affray Freed

Printers Released But
Food Hawker Held
Another Week

Two suspects of the murder of First Class Seaman Asamitsu Tamisato on September 23 were released yesterday morning because of lack of evidence, while the third suspect was ordered to be held on a writ of detention for a week for another session of the First Special District Court. Two other members of the Landing Party were wounded at the same time.

The two released were Ma Pung-tsai and his brother, Ma Yung-nien.

The third suspect, Chang Yung-ho, 21-year-old food hawker, continued to deny any implication in the shooting. He told the court again that he had only run to the scene of the shooting after he had heard shots fired.

Three Japanese witnesses testified at the session yesterday, one of whom said that he saw Chang's hand in the sand box in which he found the Mauser pistol. The other two testified only that they had assisted in arresting Chang.

Tadashi Horiye, 34, a Japanese tailor living on Woosung Road, first took the stand and said he saw Chang pushing his right hand into the sand box and that there was a black object in the hand.

Shouting "you're the man" in Japanese, he grabbed Chang by the arm and held him until other Japanese arrived on the scene. Handing Chang over to them, he opened the sand box and found a Mauser pistol there. He turned this pistol over to members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party.

Yoshio Kuroda, a Japanese radio salesman, testified that he had heard shots and had rushed to the scene. He heard Horiye shout "you're the man" and rushed to assist in arresting Chang.

When questioned by the judge, he said that he did not see Chang put anything into the sand box.

Hajime Miyata, who accompanied Kuroda, told the court that his story was similar to that of Kuroda's.

Assistant Municipal Advocate T. T. Tsang presented the evidence which was prepared by the police and asked the court, on behalf of the police, that Chang be detained further to give the police more time to carry on its investigation.

Chang will be detained until the next trial being set for Friday.

（批：ehs）

《字林西报》，1936年10月4日，星期日

鸭绿路斗殴案
两名嫌疑人
获释

印刷工获释，但
食品小贩再被
羁押一周

9月23日一等水手浅光民藏（Asamitsu Tamisato）被杀案的两名嫌疑人，昨晨因证据不足获释，而第三名嫌疑人则被签发拘留令，还押一周，以待第一特区法院下一次开庭审理。另有两名登陆队成员在同一事件中受伤。

获释的两人为马鹏才及其弟马永年。

第三名嫌疑人，21岁的食品小贩张永和，继续否认与枪击案有任何牵连。他再次向法庭表示，他只是在听到枪声后才跑向现场。

昨天的庭审中有三名日本证人作证，其中一人称，他看见张的手伸进沙箱，并在其中发现了那支毛瑟手枪。另外两人仅作证称他们协助逮捕了张。

堀江正（Tadashi Horiye），34岁，居住在吴淞路的日本裁缝，首先出庭作证，称他看见张将右手伸入沙箱，手中握有一个黑色物体。

他用日语大喊“就是你”，抓住张的手臂并将其控制住，直到其他日本人到达现场。他将张移交给这些人，随后打开沙箱，发现里面有一支毛瑟手枪。他将这支手枪交给了日本海军登陆队成员。

黑田芳雄（Yoshio Kuroda），一名日本无线电推销员，作证称他听到枪声并赶至现场。他听见堀江大喊“就是你”，便冲上前协助逮捕张。

当法官询问时，他表示并未看见张将任何东西放入沙箱。

陪同黑田前来的宫田始（Hajime Miyata）向法庭陈述，他的说法与黑田相似。

助理市检察官T. T. Tsang提交了警方准备的证据，并代表警方请求法庭继续羁押张，以便警方有更多时间进行调查。

张将被羁押至定于周五进行的下一次审判。

（批注：ehs）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, OCTOBER 5, 1936

D. 7538
5 . 10 . 36

CALM IN HONGKEW
AND CHAPEI

Substantial Reduction of the
Japanese Patrols

EXODUS IS DEFINITELY
CHECKED

Tension in the Hongkew area was markedly less yesterday, with a further withdrawal of Japanese sentries from Settlement streets, whilst none could be seen in Chapei. A decrease in the number of Chinese residents evacuating Chapei and Kiangwan again was noted, even over Saturday's substantial reduction as compared with the three preceding days, while several rickshaws piled high with household goods were observed returning to the Chinese-controlled area..

No untoward incidents were reported during the day. A tour of the Hongkew area just before dusk confirmed reports of the decreased number of sentries. Whereas a few days ago every important intersection of North Szechuen Road was heavily guarded, yesterday only three were watched by sentries. Two men and an N.C.O. were on guard outside the Isis Theatre, in Jukong Road; another small party, including a machine-gun motor cycle and an armoured car, was seen outside a Japanese Naval Landing Party post almost opposite the site of the old Odeon Theatre, which was burned down during the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1932; and three sentries and an N.C.O. were on guard outside the Japanese Public School, 141a North Szechuen Road.

One marine was guarding an empty lorry and an armoured car near the old Japanese garden in Dixwell Road, while four more were stationed by a furniture shop by the Chinese bridge leading over the Hongkew Creek. A lone sentry stood at the corner of Range Road and Woosung Road, by the Hongkew Fire Station.

Noticeable yesterday was the fact that, not only did all the sentries carry their rifles in the "at ease" position, but in every case bayonets were unfixed. Motor cycle patrols were scarce and seemed to confine their activities to the Dixwell Road and North Szechuen Road areas.

16907
《字林西报》，1936年10月5日，星期一

D. 7538
5 . 10 . 36

虹口与闸北
恢复平静

日军巡逻大幅
减少

外逃潮已明确
得到遏制

昨日虹口地区的紧张局势显著缓和，公共租界街道上的日本哨兵进一步撤离，而在闸北已看不到任何哨兵。值得注意的是，从闸北和江湾撤离的中国居民人数进一步减少，甚至相比前三天，周六的大幅减少趋势仍在持续，同时观察到几辆堆满家用物品的黄包车返回华界控制区。

当日未报告发生任何不良事件。黄昏前夕对虹口地区的一次巡视证实了哨兵数量减少的报道。就在几天前，北四川路的每个重要路口都有重兵把守，而昨日仅有三个路口有哨兵看守。两名士兵和一名军士在九江路的伊西斯大戏院（Isis Theatre）外站岗；另一小队人马，包括一辆机枪摩托车和一辆装甲车，出现在日本海军登陆队一处哨所外，该哨所几乎正对着旧奥迪安大戏院（Odeon Theatre）遗址，该剧院在1932年中日冲突期间被焚毁；三名哨兵和一名军士在北四川路141a号的日本公学外站岗。

一名海军陆战队员在狄思威路旧日本花园附近看守一辆空卡车和一辆装甲车，另有四名士兵驻守在通往跨越虹口港的中式桥梁旁的一家家具店附近。一名孤零零的哨兵站在虹口救火会旁的雷恩路与吴淞路转角处。

昨日引人注目的是，不仅所有哨兵都以“稍息”姿势持枪，而且在所有情况下刺刀均未安装。摩托车巡逻队很少见，似乎将其活动限制在狄思威路和北四川路区域。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, OCTOBER 4, 1936

HONGKEW SITUATION
A Timely Warning

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Referring to the recent incidents related by C.T.S. and COLD COMFORT and HONGKEW RESIDENT in your correspondence columns, may I take this opportunity of issuing a timely warning, so that Europeans may avoid any possible trouble or misunderstandings which may lead to "serious consequences."
It is a very natural thing for anyone to step out on to the pavement and call for a "Rikkshaw," and they would no doubt be astounded if they found that their simple request led them into considerable trouble, and even possible harm. Yet such a thing is very very possible. One of the worst insults in the Japanese language is the word "Chikkusho" (pronounced "Chikksho"), and it is hardly necessary for me to explain the possible happenings were some one to step out on to the pavement, close to a Japanese sentry, and call for a "Rikkshaw." He might even be promptly bayoneted if the individual in question should happen to be short-tempered, especially with the present mental condition prevailing, for the word "Chikkusho" means a "beast."
Therefore, please bear in mind when in the Hongkew district avoid using the word "Rikkshaw" or "Chikkusho," if you wish to preserve the peace of the Orient, and even perhaps the World."
CAUTIOUS.
Shanghai, Oct. 3.

《字林西报》，1936年10月4日，星期日

虹口局势
及时警告

致《字林西报》编辑
先生，——鉴于C.T.S.、COLD COMFORT以及“虹口居民”在贵报来信专栏中所述的近期事件，请允许我借此机会发出及时警告，以便欧洲人避免任何可能导致“严重后果”的麻烦或误解。
任何人走到人行道上叫一辆“人力车”（Rikkshaw）是很自然的事，如果他们发现这简单的请求竟导致相当大的麻烦，甚至可能的伤害，无疑会感到震惊。然而，这种事是非常非常可能发生的。日语中最严重的侮辱性词汇之一是“Chikkusho”（发音为“Chikksho”），我几乎无需解释，如果有人走到靠近日本哨兵的人行道上，喊叫“Rikkshaw”，可能会发生什么情况。如果当事人恰好脾气暴躁，尤其是在目前普遍的心理状态下，他甚至可能立即被刺刀刺伤，因为“Chikkusho”一词意为“畜生”。
因此，请记住，在虹口地区时，若希望保持东方乃至世界的和平，请避免使用“Rikkshaw”或“Chikkusho”一词。
谨慎者。
上海，10月3日。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, OCTOBER 4, 1936

Japanese Point of View
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—A number of your correspondents, during the last few days, have set forth opinions that the measures taken in Hongkew by the Japanese Naval Landing Party were unnecessary; that they interfered with the administration of the International Settlement, and that they were not conducive to peace and order in the community.
While I am not assuming to set forth the official Japanese view, permit me to present here what I believe to be the views held by most of my co-nationals residing in the northern district.
1. From the viewpoint of the commander of the Special Naval Landing Party, the measures are reasonable and appropriate. It must not be forgotten that the force is here to protect Japanese residents. It is maintained by Japanese taxpayers for that specific purpose and the failure of the commander to take all possible steps to prevent any Japanese, civilian or otherwise, from being harmed would be regarded as criminal, here as well as in Japan.
2. The murders of Warrant-Officers Hideo Nakayama and Asamitsu Taminato on Settlement roads have conclusively proven that unless the Shanghai Municipal Police Force, as efficient as it is to-day, could not prevent the recurrence of similar outrages unless increased a thousand-fold.
3. If the naval measures have created concern, the blame should be put on the circumstances that led to the adoption of those very measures. The way in which three Japanese have lost their lives at the hands of gunmen in Shanghai has been identical. They were all shot in the back. I believe most of your readers will agree with me that there is no more unpleasant or "jittery" feeling than that of being threatened with sudden death that strikes you from behind. (Not that being shot in the face is pleasant). The fact that in time of war, snipers are summarily shot upon capture clearly illustrates how this constant feeling of lurking danger is regarded as dangerous to an army's morale. One of your correspondents stated that "it is no joke to walk by sentries or to be passed by sentries when the accidental pressure of one inch per trigger finger separates you from eternity." May I state that it is no fun either for the sentry to know that a second's delay in pulling that trigger may lead him to eternity.
4. The old adage that an ounce of prevention is better than a pound of cure is the underlying factor in the Japanese military measures. Commenting editorially on the steps taken by the Landing Party following the Haining Road tragedy you stated that there seemed to be an "element of shutting the stable door after the horse has been stolen about the Japanese precautions." If we recall that Mr. Kosaku Kayau was shot to death a few hours after a serious development had taken place in the trial of the now-convicted slayers of Warrant-Officer Nakayama, it seems only natural for the Japanese naval command to have strengthened precautionary measures at a time when the same judicial proceedings were reaching a climax.
5. The fact that the series of slaying have established that they were planned without specific motive against anyone in particular so long as the victims were Japanese naturally makes the adoption of extraordinary measures necessary. To use the words of your correspondent it is no joke to walk down the street when the accidental pressure of one inch per gunman's trigger-finger separates you from eternity. Whether we Japanese are justified in feeling so or not is another matter. Allow me, however, to quote here a statement made to me yesterday by a Briton, whom I consider one of the best-informed men in Shanghai; "There will be another shooting of a Japanese. But no-one knows when or where it will be."
6. Lastly about the trouble about photographers. The taking of photographs of a military position in an emergency is prohibited in most countries. The present situation in Hongkew is an emergency in every sense of the word, the Japanese Naval Landing Party co-operating with Japanese and other law-enforcement agencies in a "war" against a hidden enemy.
Pictures of Japanese sentry positions, printed in newspapers or acquired by some other means, would provide this enemy a splendid basis on which to map out its next attack without running the danger of engaging in a reconnaissance of the spot in person. Moreover, a photograph, more than a personal observation, gives the opportunity to the accomplices of the gunman to discuss possible approaches to the "job." Herein lies, I am sure, the reason why Japanese naval officers object to the indiscriminate snapping of sentry posts.
In conclusion, I wish to express my regrets at the various "incidents" involving foreigners and the Naval Landing Party. But I can easily see why in one case, the pungent, seafaring language of an old salt did not find a welcome echo in a tin-helmeted sailor of Nippon. Both were on land at the time.
TOZAI.
Shanghai, Oct. 3.

《字林西报》，1936年10月4日，星期日

日本人的观点
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——在过去几天里，贵报多位来信者提出如下看法：日本海军陆战队在虹口采取的措施是不必要的；这些措施干涉了公共租界的行政管理，且不利于社区的和平与秩序。

虽然我不敢妄称代表日本官方观点，但请允许我在此陈述我认为居住在北部地区的大多数同胞所持有的看法。

1. 从特别海军陆战队指挥官的角度来看，这些措施是合理且适当的。切勿忘记，这支力量的存在是为了保护日本居民。它由日本纳税人出资维持，专门用于此目的，如果指挥官未能采取一切可能步骤防止任何日本人（无论是平民还是其他身份）受到伤害，那么无论在日本还是在这里，这种行为都将被视为犯罪。

2. 中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）和民名浅光（Asamitsu Taminato）两位准尉在租界道路上被谋杀，确凿地证明，除非上海工部局警务处的警力增加一千倍，否则即便其目前效率如此之高，也无法防止类似暴行的再次发生。

3. 如果海军的措施引起了担忧，那么责任应归咎于导致采取这些措施的环境。三名日本人在上海死于枪手之手的经过如出一辙。他们都是从背后被枪杀的。我相信贵报大多数读者会同意我的观点，没有什么比那种来自背后的、突如其来的死亡威胁更令人不快或“紧张”的了。（当然，正面中弹也不令人愉快）。在战争时期，狙击手一旦被俘即被就地正法，这一事实清楚地说明了这种潜伏的危险感对军队士气被视为多么危险。贵报一位来信者称，“走过哨兵身边或被哨兵盘查绝非儿戏，因为食指在扳机上偶然的一英寸按压就能让你通往永恒。”容我指出，对于哨兵来说，知道扣动扳机时的片刻迟疑可能导致他自己通往永恒，这也绝非乐事。

4. “预防胜于治疗”这句老话是日本军事措施背后的根本因素。你们在社论中评论海军陆战队在海宁路惨案后采取的步骤时指出，日本的预防措施似乎有一种“亡羊补牢”的成分。如果我们回顾一下，在如今已被定罪的杀害中山准尉凶手的审判出现重大进展几小时后，加屋幸作（Kosaku Kayau）先生即被枪杀，那么在日本海军指挥部看来，在同样的司法程序达到高潮之时加强预防措施似乎是自然而然的。

5. 一系列杀戮事件的事实表明，只要受害者是日本人，这些袭击就是有计划进行的，而并非针对特定个人，这自然使得采取非常措施成为必要。借用贵报来信者的话来说，当枪手食指在扳机上偶然的一英寸按压就能让你通往永恒时，走在街上绝非儿戏。我们日本人是否有理由如此感受是另一回事。然而，请允许我引用昨天一位英国人对我说的话，我认为他是上海消息最灵通的人士之一：“还将会有日本人被枪击。但没人知道何时何地会发生。”

6. 最后谈谈关于摄影师的麻烦。在紧急状态下拍摄军事阵地照片在大多数国家都是被禁止的。虹口目前的局势在任何意义上都处于紧急状态，日本海军陆战队正与日本及其他执法机构合作，进行一场对抗隐蔽敌人的“战争”。

日本哨位照片若刊登在报纸上或通过其他手段获取，将为该敌人提供极佳的基础，使其无需亲自侦察现场即可策划下一次攻击。此外，与个人观察相比，照片为枪手的同伙提供了讨论实施“任务”的可能途径的机会。我相信，这就是日本海军军官反对随意拍摄哨位的原因所在。

总之，我对涉及外国人和海军陆战队的各种“事件”表示遗憾。但我很容易理解，为何在一个案例中，一位老水手辛辣的海员语言未能在一名头戴钢盔的日本水兵那里得到友好的回应。当时两人都在陆地上。

TOZAI.
上海，10月3日。

谣言仍在华人中盛行

居民外迁
目前闸北居民
外流已微乎其微

杨树浦进行
炮兵演习

尽管闸北的恐慌似乎已经平息，导致中国居民涌入公共租界的人数显著减少，但关于中日即将发生敌对行动的谣言仍然盛行，紧张气氛依然存在。

虹口地区的日本巡逻队和哨兵已大幅减少，最后的路障也已拆除，昨天一天平安无事，未发生任何事件。

中山案件的结果，加上东京决定派遣东亚事务局局长桑岛先生（Mr. Kuwajima）来华所带来的喘息之机，已平息了日本侨民中的恐惧情绪，尽管据报道，许多此前居住在闸北的家庭已搬至虹口。

昨天上午7点30分起，日本海军陆战队在杨树浦平凉路地区进行炮兵演习，引起了广泛关注。

日本海军陆战队特别关注的地区昨晚已恢复正常状况，尽管偶尔仍可见巡逻队执行例行任务。

《大美晚报》，1936年10月4日，星期日

虹口地区
平静；外迁
几乎停止

尽管表面平静
情绪依然紧张

虽然由于日本海军陆战队在这两个地区的守卫几乎全部撤出，昨天虹口和闸北（Chapel，此处原文误拼，应为Chapei/闸北）的局势明显普遍改善，但该地区的紧张和担忧暗流仍在持续。

自日本人架设铁丝网并增加哨兵后，始于周四的该市部分地区居民外迁潮，到昨天上午已基本完全停止。有人看到几批中国人正返回他们在闸北（Chapel，同上）的家中。

哨兵减少
在虹口，除仍驻扎在百老汇路（Boone Road）和乍浦路（Chapoo Road）附近的小股部队外，所有日本巡逻队和守卫均已撤出。部署在中国领土铁路轨道对面的日本哨兵也已撤回。然而，仍有三四名身穿蓝制服的水兵驻扎在闸北（Chapel，同上）八字桥（Paitzechiao）的一块土地上。

然而，昨天临近中午，当日本学童回家吃午饭时，守卫人数又略有增加，但其数量根本无法与周四和周五的强大分队相比。

昨天局势缓和，大概是因为日本人对两名中山案被告被判死刑感到满意。

与此同时，日本和中国当局都在尽力安抚居民的恐惧情绪。吴铁城市长在昨天的一道命令中，要求市政府所有工作人员不要搬离江湾市中心区域。

这份通告，连同市政府局官员为驳斥市内流传谣言所做的努力，成功遏制了昨天从江湾外迁的任何行动。

学校照常上课
位于该地区的各学校昨天上午继续照常上课。市教育局官员否认了周末后可能停课的报道。

位于江湾的复旦大学的学生昨天声明，他们将继续上课，该校女生已于周五搬至徐家汇校区。其他机构的行政官员也证实了这一说法。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, October 3, 1936

Hongkew Beyond
SMC Authority

Situation Remains One
Diplomacy, Declares
Fessenden

The Shanghai Municipal Police are the authority entrusted with the task of maintaining law and order within the limits of the International Settlement. But when a situation develops beyond the control of a municipal government, it then becomes a matter for national diplomacy and is more or less out of the hands of the municipal authorities.

That was the statement made to a representative of the Shanghai Evening Post this morning by Mr. Sterling Fessenden, secretary general of the Shanghai Municipal Council, when interviewed expressly on the Council's attitude towards the extraordinary situation that has prevailed in the Hongkew area of the Settlement for the past few days.

Soldiers Zealous

The Japanese Naval Landing Party has no legal authority permitting them to restrain officials of the Municipal Police from moving about freely in the course of their duties, Mr. Fessenden declared, as has been the case in various incidents in the past few days. But private soldiers whether Japanese or of any other nationality, are likely to be over-zealous in the performance of what they consider their duty, especially in times of tension when they feel their national honor is at stake. Due to their occasional ignorance, they are apt to go beyond their legal rights.

In addition, the Japanese Landing Party has no legal authority permitting it to detain and confiscate the property of non-Japanese subjects within the territory of the Settlement as has happened occasionally lately.

Overrate Power

Shanghai residents, however, are inclined to over-estimate the authority vested in the Municipal Police through the Council, for they forget that the S.M.C. is guided by the Land Regulations and extraordinary decisions must be referred to the Consular Body.

All powers represented in Shanghai have the right to land troops in the Settlement to protect the lives and property of their nationals. The Council is entrusted to maintain peace and order in the Settlement through authority of the powers but its authority is that of a municipality and not of a power in itself. When the Japanese land, taking over Hongkew area control, then there occurs a situation beyond municipal control and one which must be arbitrated through diplomatic channels by the officials of the nationalities involved, the secretary-general pointed out.

If the police arrest any person, such action is entirely under Mr. Fessenden said, but there is no power municipal or otherwise to cover that family. It still remains a question to be settled by diplomatic negotiations. The Council has no legal authority covering such cases stated in general terms. It has not the power of a sovereign nation.

In case, Mr. Fessenden said, the situation reaches a crisis, it must be referred to the Consular Body.

虹口之外
工部局权限

费森登称局势仍属
外交范畴

上海公共租界工部局警务处是受委托在公共租界范围内维持治安的当局。但是，当出现市政政府无法控制的局势时，这就变成了国家外交事务，或多或少超出了市政当局的掌控范围。

这是上海公共租界工部局总董秘书斯特林·费森登（Sterling Fessenden）先生今天上午对《上海晚邮报》代表所作的陈述，当时他就工部局针对过去几天租界虹口地区出现的非常局势所持态度接受了专门采访。

士兵过于热心

费森登先生宣称，日本海军陆战队没有任何法律授权可以限制工部局警务人员在执行公务期间自由行动，正如过去几天发生的几起事件那样。但是，无论是日本籍还是其他国籍的普通士兵，在履行他们认为的职责时，往往过于热心，尤其是在他们感到国家荣誉受到威胁的紧张时期。由于偶尔无知，他们往往会超越其法定权利。

此外，日本陆战队没有任何法律授权允许其在租界领土内拘留和没收非日本臣民的财产，尽管最近偶尔发生过此类事件。

高估权力

然而，上海居民倾向于高估通过工部局赋予工部局警务处的权力，因为他们忘记了工部局受《土地章程》指导，非凡决定必须提交领事团裁决。

在上海拥有权益的所有列强都有权在租界登陆军队，以保护其国民的生命和财产。工部局受托通过列强的授权在租界维持和平与秩序，但其权力是市政性质的，而非作为一个主权国家本身的权力。总董秘书指出，当日本人登陆并接管虹口地区的控制权时，就会出现超出市政控制范围的局势，这种局势必须由相关国家的官员通过外交渠道进行仲裁。

费森登先生说，如果警察逮捕任何人，这种行动完全在……（原文不清/句子中断），但没有市政或其他权力涵盖该家庭。这仍然是一个需要通过外交谈判解决的问题。工部局没有涵盖此类案件的一般性法律授权。它不具备主权国家的权力。

费森登先生说，如果局势达到危机程度，必须提交领事团处理。
