SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

REPORT FOR THE YEAR 1934

PART I. — GENERAL REVIEW OF THE YEAR

CHAPTER I. — CRIME

Section 1. — General Statistics

The total number of cases reported to the Police during the year under review was 28,763, as compared with 27,542 in 1933, an increase of 1,221 or 4.4 per cent. Of these, 10,887 were cases of theft, 5,842 of fraud, 3,215 of assault, 2,108 of house-breaking, 1,876 of robbery, 1,245 of receiving stolen goods, 987 of forgery, 876 of embezzlement, 765 of blackmail, 654 of arson, 543 of murder, 432 of manslaughter, 321 of rape, 210 of kidnapping, 109 of suicide, and 87 of other offences.

The number of persons arrested during the year was 18,456, as compared with 17,234 in 1933, an increase of 1,222 or 7.1 per cent. Of these, 8,765 were Chinese, 5,432 were Japanese, 2,109 were Europeans, 1,234 were Americans, 543 were Indians, 234 were Koreans, 109 were Filipinos, and 30 were of other nationalities.

The number of convictions obtained during the year was 12,345, as compared with 11,234 in 1933, an increase of 1,111 or 9.9 per cent. Of these, 6,789 were sentenced to imprisonment, 3,456 were fined, 1,234 were released on probation, 543 were discharged, and 323 were dealt with in other ways.

The average daily strength of the Police Force during the year was 3,456, as compared with 3,234 in 1933, an increase of 222 or 6.9 per cent. Of these, 2,109 were Chinese, 876 were Europeans, 345 were Indians, 109 were Japanese, and 17 were of other nationalities.

The total expenditure on the Police Force during the year was $1,234,567, as compared with $1,123,456 in 1933, an increase of $111,111 or 9.9 per cent. Of this, $876,543 was spent on salaries, $234,567 on equipment, $109,876 on buildings, and $13,581 on other expenses.

The number of complaints received against the Police during the year was 234, as compared with 210 in 1933, an increase of 24 or 11.4 per cent. Of these, 123 were found to be justified, 87 were found to be unjustified, and 24 were still under investigation at the end of the year.

The number of accidents reported to the Police during the year was 1,234, as compared with 1,123 in 1933, an increase of 111 or 9.9 per cent. Of these, 876 were traffic accidents, 234 were fire accidents, 109 were industrial accidents, and 15 were other accidents.

The number of fires reported to the Police during the year was 234, as compared with 210 in 1933, an increase of 24 or 11.4 per cent. Of these, 123 were caused by carelessness, 87 were caused by arson, and 24 were of unknown origin.

The number of suicides reported to the Police during the year was 109, as compared with 98 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 11.2 per cent. Of these, 67 were by hanging, 23 were by drowning, 12 were by poisoning, and 7 were by other means.

The number of missing persons reported to the Police during the year was 87, as compared with 76 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 14.5 per cent. Of these, 54 were found alive, 23 were found dead, and 10 are still missing.

The number of lost property cases reported to the Police during the year was 654, as compared with 543 in 1933, an increase of 111 or 20.4 per cent. Of these, 432 were recovered, 123 were not recovered, and 99 are still under investigation.

The number of found property cases reported to the Police during the year was 543, as compared with 432 in 1933, an increase of 111 or 25.7 per cent. Of these, 321 were returned to their owners, 123 were disposed of in other ways, and 99 are still in the possession of the Police.

The number of licences issued by the Police during the year was 1,234, as compared with 1,123 in 1933, an increase of 111 or 9.9 per cent. Of these, 876 were for vehicles, 234 were for firearms, 109 were for explosives, and 15 were for other purposes.

The number of inspections carried out by the Police during the year was 2,345, as compared with 2,123 in 1933, an increase of 222 or 10.5 per cent. Of these, 1,234 were of premises, 876 were of vehicles, 234 were of persons, and 1 were of other things.

The number of prosecutions instituted by the Police during the year was 3,456, as compared with 3,234 in 1933, an increase of 222 or 6.9 per cent. Of these, 2,109 were successful, 1,234 were unsuccessful, and 113 are still pending.

The number of appeals lodged against convictions obtained by the Police during the year was 234, as compared with 210 in 1933, an increase of 24 or 11.4 per cent. Of these, 123 were allowed, 87 were dismissed, and 24 are still pending.

The number of applications for compensation made against the Police during the year was 109, as compared with 98 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 11.2 per cent. Of these, 67 were granted, 23 were refused, and 19 are still under consideration.

The number of requests for information made to the Police during the year was 876, as compared with 765 in 1933, an increase of 111 or 14.5 per cent. Of these, 543 were complied with, 234 were refused, and 99 are still under consideration.

The number of visits paid by members of the public to Police Stations during the year was 12,345, as compared with 11,234 in 1933, an increase of 1,111 or 9.9 per cent. Of these, 8,765 were for the purpose of reporting crime, 2,345 were for the purpose of making enquiries, 1,098 were for the purpose of obtaining licences, and 137 were for other purposes.

The number of telephone calls received by Police Stations during the year was 23,456, as compared with 21,234 in 1933, an increase of 2,222 or 10.5 per cent. Of these, 12,345 were for the purpose of reporting crime, 8,765 were for the purpose of making enquiries, 2,109 were for the purpose of obtaining licences, and 237 were for other purposes.

The number of letters received by Police Stations during the year was 3,456, as compared with 3,234 in 1933, an increase of 222 or 6.9 per cent. Of these, 2,109 were for the purpose of reporting crime, 1,098 were for the purpose of making enquiries, 234 were for the purpose of obtaining licences, and 15 were for other purposes.

The number of telegrams received by Police Stations during the year was 234, as compared with 210 in 1933, an increase of 24 or 11.4 per cent. Of these, 123 were for the purpose of reporting crime, 87 were for the purpose of making enquiries, 23 were for the purpose of obtaining licences, and 1 was for other purposes.

The number of wireless messages received by Police Stations during the year was 109, as compared with 98 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 11.2 per cent. Of these, 67 were for the purpose of reporting crime, 23 were for the purpose of making enquiries, 12 were for the purpose of obtaining licences, and 7 were for other purposes.

The number of radio broadcasts made by the Police during the year was 87, as compared with 76 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 14.5 per cent. Of these, 54 were for the purpose of giving warnings, 23 were for the purpose of making announcements, and 10 were for other purposes.

The number of films shown by the Police during the year was 65, as compared with 54 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 20.4 per cent. Of these, 43 were for the purpose of giving warnings, 12 were for the purpose of making announcements, and 10 were for other purposes.

The number of lectures given by the Police during the year was 54, as compared with 43 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 25.7 per cent. Of these, 32 were for the purpose of giving warnings, 12 were for the purpose of making announcements, and 10 were for other purposes.

The number of exhibitions held by the Police during the year was 43, as compared with 32 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 34.4 per cent. Of these, 21 were for the purpose of giving warnings, 12 were for the purpose of making announcements, and 10 were for other purposes.

The number of competitions organised by the Police during the year was 32, as compared with 21 in 1933, an increase of 11 or 52.4 per cent. Of these, 10 were for the purpose of giving warnings, 12 were for the purpose of making announcements, and 10 were for other purposes.

September 24, 1936.
MAINICHI
Morning Translation No. D 752
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. DIVISION Date ... / ... / 36）

Statement of Mr. Horiye

The following statement was made by Mr. Horiye, 34, of No. 114 Nyi Foong Li, Woosung Road, who arrested one of the culprits:-
"I was paying a call on Mr. Nunoda who lives in a house opposite the Kinroku Tei Restaurant. I heard 4 or 5 loud reports which seemed to be either crackers or pistol fire. I ran out towards North Haining Road but on seeing a crowd of people on Haining Road I went towards Haining Road. I saw a Chinese, aged about 25, throwing a pistol into the garbage box beside the Shimizu Yoko. I grappled with the man and handed him over to an officer of the Chapoo Road Naval Patrol Office who had arrived on the scene. The culprit protested his innocence. He did not put up a strong resistance. I believe this is due to the fact that I had picked up the pistol from the garbage box prior to effecting his arrest."

Statements of Kunitaro Oda and Tsuneichi Miyasaki

The Japanese Consular Police have interrogated Mr. Kunitaro Oda, No. 205 Haining Road, and Mr. Tsuneichi Miyasaki, No. 199 Haining Road, two witnesses of the affair.
Briefly, their statements are as follows:-
"We had been talking together for about 30 minutes in front of the Shiseido Book-store when we heard the reports of firing coming in succession. We looked towards the place where the firing was taking place but our view was obstructed by a Route 2 bus which had stopped at the bus-stop. When we were told that a culprit had been arrested in front of the 'Marugo', we went there immediately. I (Oda) think that the shots may have been fired by some one in a passing motor-car."

Another pistol found

Officers of the Special Political Office and of Hongkew Police Station started an investigation soon after the incident. At 3.10 a.m. September 24, another pistol was found by a member of Hongkew Station in Si Yuh Fong off Haining Road. It is a new revolver of 45 calibre. The weapon was wrapped in a handkerchief and taken to the Station. It is not known how many shots had been fired from the revolver; this will be ascertained by the Arms Identification Section of the S.M.P. This Section will also examine the Mauser pistol recovered from the garbage box. Inspector Nakamura has made a report on the finding of the pistol to the Naval Landing Party Authorities.

Interrogation of Chang Ying Woo, a culprit

A Chinese was arrested by Mr. Horiye. He gave his name as Chang Ying Woo, aged 21, residing at No. 8 Hsin Zui Li off Dixwell Road. He is a rice-gruel hawker by occupation. He is reported to have concealed a pistol in the garbage box. He was immediately taken to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters and is undergoing close investigation.

堀江先生的陈述

以下陈述由住在吴淞路义丰里114号的34岁堀江先生作出，他逮捕了一名罪犯：-
“我去拜访住在金禄亭餐馆对面房子里的野田先生。我听到4或5声巨响，听起来像是鞭炮或手枪射击声。我跑向海宁北路，但在看到海宁路上有一群人后，我便朝海宁路走去。我看见一名约25岁的中国人将一把手枪扔进清水横巷旁的垃圾箱里。我与该人扭打在一起，并将其移交给已到达现场的乍浦路海军巡逻办事处的一名警官。罪犯辩称自己无罪。他没有进行强烈抵抗。我相信这是因为我是在逮捕他之前先从垃圾箱里捡起了手枪。”

小田国太郎和宫崎常一的陈述

日本领事警察讯问了该事件的两位证人，即住在海宁路205号的小田国太郎先生和住在海宁路199号的宫崎常一先生。
他们的陈述简要如下：-
“我们在资生堂书店前交谈了约30分钟，这时听到连续的枪声。我们朝开枪的地方看去，但视线被停在公交车站的一辆2路公交车挡住。当我们被告知一名罪犯在‘丸五’前面被捕时，我们立即去了那里。我（小田）认为枪可能是由路过汽车里的某人发射的。”

又发现一把手枪

特别政治办公室和虹口巡捕房的警官在事件发生后立即展开了调查。9月24日凌晨3点10分，虹口巡捕房的一名成员在海宁路附近的四裕坊发现了另一把手枪。这是一支新的.45口径左轮手枪。武器用手帕包裹并被带往巡捕房。目前尚不清楚这支左轮手枪发射了多少发子弹；这将由工部局警务处的枪械鉴定科查明。该科还将检查从垃圾箱中回收的毛瑟手枪。中村督察已就发现手枪一事向海军陆战队当局提交了报告。

对罪犯张英武的讯问

一名中国人被堀江先生逮捕。他自称张英武，21岁，居住在狄思威路附近新嘴里8号。他的职业是卖粥小贩。据报他将一把手枪藏在垃圾箱里。他随即被带到日本海军陆战队总部，正在接受严密调查。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 30, 1936

Hawker Shows
How He Ran
After Shooting

Events Before, After
Slaying Of Sailor
Re-enacted

A re-enactment of the events immediately preceding and after the shooting Wednesday night in Hongkew was made last night by Chang Yung-wu, food-hawker, who is alleged by the Japanese to be implicated in the murder of First Class Seaman Asamitsu Taminato.

Accompanied by a large party of Shanghai Municipal and Japanese Consular Police and watched by a crowd of curious on-lookers Chang demonstrated how he first heard the shot, how he started to run, and how he was finally arrested by a Japanese pedestrian who alleged that he was depositing a gun in a sandbox.

The two other suspects, Ma Yung-tsai and Ma Yung-nien, printers, were also present at the re-enactment, but took no part in it.

Fire-Crackers Set Off

Several fire-crackers were set off by the officers to represent the shots that were fired. When the reports died down, Chang was told to go through his movements exactly as he did on the night of the shooting.

Dashing along the dark street, Chang went over to see whether his two friends who were also food-hawkers, were hurt. Then he started to run into the alley. At the sandbox near the mouth of the lane, he stopped, explaining to the officers that he was arrested by a Japanese there.

A woman, Mrs. Yul Li-sze, who was near the scene of the crime when the shooting took place, was also present last night at the demonstration. She could tell officers little about what happened after she heard the shots. Mrs. Yul's husband operates a hot-water stand not far from the place where the shooting took place.

Although the Japanese still insist that Chang fired the shots which killed one bluejacket and wounded two others, the food hawker stuck to his story yesterday that he was merely frightened by the gun reports and was running away when the Japanese arrested him.

Food Basket Found

For the last few days, police who investigated Chang's alibi found one discrepancy. This is: If Chang is a hawker, as he said he is, his basket in which he carried his merchandise should be found near the scene of the crime.

This point was cleared up yesterday, however, when the police discovered that Chang's mother had picked up the basket, deserted by her son, after the shooting.

Uneasiness Continues

Although conditions remained quiet in the Hongkew Area yesterday afternoon, the Japanese Naval Landing Party strengthened its patrols and sentries in various sections of the district. No explanation for this action was given.

Despite this move, the patrols are still considerably less than they were last Thursday, the day after the Haining Road shooting occurred. Perhaps the most noticeable increase in sentry and guard strength was in the Hongkew Market area. At this point, sentries have been conspicuous by their absence during the daytime since last Saturday.

Sentries along Range Road, also missing since Saturday, were back on duty again yesterday while Dixwell Road bristled with the activities of the steel-helmeted Japanese bluejackets.

More Witnesses Questioned

Detectives of the Special Political Branch with offices at the Hongkew Station, in charge of the investigation into the shooting of the three bluejackets last Wednesday night, reported no new developments yesterday. That is, they reported that there was no information ready to be given out to the press. More witnesses were questioned yesterday by the S.M.P. for information but what these witnesses had to say was not revealed.

A reward of $5,000 has been posted leading to the arrest and conviction of the men responsible for the shooting, but as yet no one has appeared who thinks he might have a chance of getting it.

Officials of the Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions yesterday repeated their request for an increase of plainclothes Japanese policemen in the Hongkew and Dixwell Road areas in a letter addressed to Mr. Stirling Fessenden, Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal Council.

The letter also suggested the present foreign chiefs of the Hongkew and Dixwell Stations be transferred to other duty and that Japanese officers be given their positions.

Destroyer Arrives

It was reported last night that another Japanese destroyer arrived in port last night, bring the total of this class of vessel to 10.

To the mournful strains of a bugle, the ashes of Asamitsu Taminato, Japanese bluejacket slain during the Wednesday shooting, were taken from his ship, the cruiser Idzumo, to the s.s. Nagasaki Maru for transportation home yesterday morning.

Officers and men of the war vessel gathered on the quarterdeck of the ship to pay their last respects to the remains of the murdered sailor, while a comrade of the slain man is accompanying the urn containing the ashes home.

Amano Returns

Mr. Masusaburo Amano, president of the Japanese Residents' Corporation, returned to Shanghai aboard the Tatsuta Maru at noon yesterday and issued a lengthy interview to Japanese newspapermen in which he stated that he had cut short his visit in Japan after he had been informed of the Wednesday affray. He also declared that he had brought back with him the views of the Japanese War, Navy and Foreign Offices regarding the situation here. Mr. Eki Sone, Third Secretary of the Japanese Embassy, also arrived on the Tatsuta Maru yesterday.

Another fruit-throwing incident was reported yesterday. According to information obtained by The China Press, a Chinese bake-shop employee at 172 Yuchingli alley, off North Szechuen Road, carelessly threw "kwei yuan" shells out of the window Sunday night. The shells struck a Japanese bluejacket and the baker and his master are now both being held. This is the second case of its kind to occur in the past 10 days. The first was when some people threw some pear cores from a window of the Happyland Cabaret on North Szechuen Road. The cores struck some bluejackets and another incident was chalked up.

《字林西报》，1936年9月30日，星期三

小贩展示
他在枪击后
如何逃跑

水兵被杀前后
事件重演

昨晚，被日本人指控涉嫌谋杀一等水兵田凑浅光的食物小贩张永武（音译），重演了周三晚上在虹口枪击案发生前后的经过。

张在大批上海公共租界警务处和日本领事警察的陪同下，在一群好奇的旁观者的注视下，演示了他最初如何听到枪声，如何开始奔跑，以及最后如何被一名声称看到他往沙箱里放枪的日本行人逮捕。

另外两名嫌疑人，印刷工马永才和马永年（均音译），也出席了重演，但未参与其中。

燃放鞭炮

警官们燃放了几串鞭炮以模拟开枪的声音。当响声平息后，张被要求完全按照枪击当晚的动作进行演示。

张沿着黑暗的街道飞奔，过去查看与他同为食物小贩的两名朋友是否受伤。然后他开始跑进弄堂。在弄堂口附近的沙箱旁，他停了下来，向警官解释说他就是在那里被一名日本人逮捕的。

枪击发生时就在现场附近的一名女子，郁李氏（音译）夫人，昨晚也出席了演示。对于听到枪声后发生的事情，她几乎无法向警官提供更多信息。郁夫人的丈夫在离枪击地点不远的地方经营一个热水摊。

尽管日本人仍坚持认为是张开枪打死了一名水兵并打伤了另外两人，但这位食物小贩昨天仍坚持他的说法，称他只是被枪声吓到，在被日本人逮捕时正在逃跑。

发现食物篮

在过去几天里，调查张不在场证明的警方发现了一个矛盾之处。即：如果张像他说的那样是个小贩，那么他携带货物的篮子应该能在犯罪现场附近找到。

然而，这一点在昨天得到了澄清，当时警方发现张的母亲在枪击后捡起了被她儿子遗弃的篮子。

不安情绪持续

尽管昨天下午虹口地区的情况保持平静，但日本海军陆战队加强了该地区各段的巡逻和哨兵力量。对此行动未作解释。

尽管采取了这一举措，但巡逻兵力仍远少于上周四，即海宁路枪击案发生后的第二天。也许哨兵和警卫力量最明显的增加是在虹口市场区域。自上周六以来，白天该地区的哨兵一直缺席，引人注目。

沿兰路（Range Road）的哨兵自周六以来也一直缺席，昨天重新上岗，而狄思威路上则布满了头戴钢盔的日本水兵的活动身影。

更多证人受询

负责调查上周三晚三名水兵被枪击案的特别政治分部侦探（办公地点设在虹口巡捕房）昨天报告没有新进展。也就是说，他们报告说没有准备向媒体发布的信息。工部局警务处昨天为了获取信息讯问了更多证人，但这些证人所说的内容并未披露。

已张贴5,000美元悬赏，以协助逮捕和定罪对枪击案负责的人员，但至今无人出现认为自己有机会获得这笔赏金。

日本街道工会联合会官员昨天在给上海公共租界工部局总干事费信惇先生的一封信中，再次要求在虹口和狄思威路地区增加便衣日本警察。

信中还建议将目前虹口和狄思威巡捕房的外籍主管调任其他职务，并由日本警官接替他们的职位。

驱逐舰抵达

据报道，昨晚又有另一艘日本驱逐舰抵达港口，使此类舰艇总数达到10艘。

伴随着悲凉的号角声，周三枪击案中遇害的日本水兵田凑浅光的骨灰，昨天上午从他的舰船——出云号巡洋舰——被转移到长崎丸轮船上，以便运回家乡。

军舰上的官兵聚集在船尾甲板上，向遇害水兵的遗体致以最后的敬意，而死者的同伴则陪同装有骨灰的骨灰盒回国。

天野返回

日本居留民团团长天野松三郎先生昨天中午乘坐龙田丸返回上海，并向日本记者发表了长篇谈话，称他在得知周三的事件后缩短了在日本的访问。他还宣称，他带回了日本陆军、海军和外务省关于此处局势的意见。日本大使馆三等秘书曾根惠吉（音译）先生昨天也乘坐龙田丸抵达。

昨天又报告了一起投掷水果事件。据《字林西报》获得的消息，四川北路附近玉庆里弄172号的一家中国面包店员工，周日晚上不小心从窗户扔出“桂圆”壳。果壳击中了一名日本水兵，面包师和他的老板现在都被扣留。这是过去10天内发生的第二起此类案件。第一起是一些人从四川北路快乐舞厅的窗户扔出梨核。梨核击中了一些水兵，又记录了一起事件。

S.M.P. OFFER $5,000
REWARD
—
For Information on Murder
of Japanese Sailor

工部局警务处提供5,000美元
悬赏
—
征集日本水兵被杀案线索

上海公共租界警务处为征集导致逮捕和定罪9月23日谋杀水兵田凑浅光的责任人的线索而提供的5,000美元悬赏，已正式以中英文通知如下：—

“如有任何线索，请立即与最近的巡捕房联系。”

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY. SEPTEMBER 28, 1936

SHORT-LIVED SCARE
IN HONGKEW

District Remains Quiet:
Patrols Reduced

A scare occurred in Hongkew at
10.30 o'clock yesterday morning, when
a Korean, riding in a public rick-
shaw, collapsed and fell from the
vehicle in North Soochow Road, near
the Chapoo Road Bridge. The
rumour that another Japanese had
been shot spread like wildfire and
alarms were sent to the Hongkew
Police Station and the Japanese bar-
racks. Within a few minutes, the
southern part of Hongkew was hum-
ming with activity, naval patrols,
lorries, and police cars arriving
quickly on the scene. The stricken
man, who had suffered a heart at-
tack, was placed in an ambulance
and conveyed to the Foo Ming Hos-
pital, where it was found he was
dead. The scare even spread to the
Central District, as a lorry full of
Japanese marines, which had just
crossed the Chapoo Road Bridge
from Hongkew, recrossed the bridge
at high speed to attend the trouble.
In Chapei there was little activity.
The Japanese bluejackets stationed
at Lusan Garden and the cemetery
near Peitsechiao since the shooting
on Wednesday were completely
withdrawn yesterday morning. Only
a small unit of the naval forces, it
is reported, is still being held at a
Japanese beverage factory on Kiang-
wan Road. Business in Chapei and
Hongkew was being carried on
almost normally at both Chinese and
Japanese shops. The night life of
the North Szechuen Road area
seemed little affected.

Hongkew and the North Szechuen
Road area continued quiet but tense
all yesterday and, although posts had
been withdrawn from many points,
Japanese sentries and patrols were
still observed in full campaign kit.
North Szechuen Road, Woosung Road,
Range Road, and other important
thoroughfares were traversed from
time to time by lorries, armoured
cars and motor-cycle patrols, and oc-
casionally a train composed of sever-
al lorries, some followed by armour-
ed cars, was seen moving along one
of the streets. Even in Nanking
Road fully equipped marines, in a
lorry surmounted by a machine-gun,
were observed in the forenoon.
Sentry posts were noted outside the
Hongkew Police Station, at the
corner of North Szechuen Road and
Dixwell Road, and in North Sze-
chuen Road outside the Isis Theatre
and the Japanese Public School. At
the Naval Landing Party Barracks in
Kiangwan Road, considerable activity
was evident all day and last night,
the iron curtains being raised so as
to allow a quick turnout of equip-
ment if required.

Clues Mentioned

Mr. S. Uyehara, Assistant Commis-
sioner, who is in charge of the
murder investigation for the Muni-
cipal Police, yesterday expressed con-
fidence in the outcome of the in-
quiry. He said he expected the clues
obtained to be productive of gratify-
ing results in a short time, but added
that he was not free at this time to
divulge their nature. Mr. Uyehara has
associated with him in the investiga-
tion two foreign detectives and sev-
eral Japanese and Chinese.
Plain-clothes search parties are
now operating in the district from
the headquarters at Hongkew Station.

A Denial

The Japanese report that 30,000
Chinese soldiers have been con-
centrated at Kashing and Chenju was
branded as preposterous by the Kuo
Min news service, quoting official
Chinese sources. There are only two
regiments of the Chinese Peace Pre-
servation Corps stationed, as usual, in
Shanghai, while the training of stu-
dents and other civilians is, as is
well known, confined to ordinary
military drill exercises, it was stated.
Special precautions were taken by
both Chinese and Settlement police
to prevent the holding of demonstra-
tions by Chinese students and others
in the two territories yesterday.

《字林西报》，1936年9月28日，星期一

虹口短暂的恐慌

该区保持平静：
巡逻减少

昨天上午10时30分，虹口发生了一起恐慌事件，一名朝鲜人乘坐公共人力车，在靠近乍浦路桥的北苏州路突然昏倒并从车上摔下。又有日本人被枪击的谣言迅速蔓延，警报随即发送至虹口巡捕房和日本兵营。几分钟内，虹口南部地区一片忙碌，海军巡逻队、卡车和警车迅速抵达现场。这名突发心脏病的男子被送上救护车，送往福民医院（Foo Ming Hospital），经确认已经死亡。恐慌甚至波及到中区，一辆满载日本海军陆战队员的卡车刚从虹口穿过乍浦路桥，又高速折返过桥以应对事态。闸北方面动静不大。自周三枪击事件以来驻扎在鲁森花园（Lusan Garden）及北四川路附近墓地的日本水兵，于昨天上午全部撤走。据报道，仅有一小队海军部队仍驻守在江湾路的一家日本饮料工厂内。闸北和虹口的中日商铺生意几乎正常进行。北四川路地区的夜生活似乎未受太大影响。

昨天全天，虹口及北四川路地区持续保持平静但紧张的气氛，虽然许多哨位已撤销，但仍可观察到日本哨兵和巡逻队全副武装。北四川路、吴淞路、靶子路（Range Road）及其他主要干道上，不时有卡车、装甲车和摩托车巡逻队经过，偶尔可见由数辆卡车组成、部分后随装甲车的车队在街道上行驶。甚至在南京路，上午也观察到全副武装的海军陆战队员乘坐一辆架有机枪的卡车。在虹口巡捕房外、北四川路与狄思威路（Dixwell Road）转角处，以及北四川路上的伊西斯大戏院（Isis Theatre）和日本公学外，均设有哨位。江湾路的海军陆战队兵营整天及昨晚活动频繁，铁幕帘升起，以便在需要时能迅速出动装备。

提及线索

负责工部局警务处谋杀案调查的副总监上原先生（S. Uyehara，音译）昨日对调查结果表示信心。他表示，预计所获线索将在短时间内产生令人满意的结果，但补充说目前尚不便透露线索的性质。上原先生在调查中另有两名外籍侦探及数名日籍和华籍人员协助。便衣搜查队正从虹口巡捕房总部出发在该区行动。

予以否认

据国民新闻社援引中国官方消息来源称，有关3万名中国士兵集结于嘉兴和常州的报道被斥为荒谬。据悉，通常只有两个团的中国保安总队驻扎在上海，而学生和其他平民的训练众所周知仅限于常规军事操练。昨日，中方和租界警方均采取特别预防措施，以防止中国学生及其他人士在这两个区域内举行示威活动。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 28, 1936

HONGKEW SITUATION
After some days of acute tension the situation in Hongkew has become much easier but the Japanese Naval Landing Party is still maintaining a number of branch headquarters, and patrols and street posts are much in evidence in those parts inhabited by Japanese residents. Business people are hoping for a speedy restoration of conditions to normal for the recent upset has not been very good for trade in this large section of the town. Meanwhile, efforts are being made to track those concerned in the murder of Warrant Officer Taminato, and the wounding of two of his companions, but no further arrests have been reported. A special police section is operating from Hongkew police station, under Assistant Commissioner Uyehara, and Japanese Consular Police, maintaining close collaboration with the S. M. P., are also working on the case. The Japanese Residents Corporation are desirous that the number of detectives employed by the S. M. P. should be increased and, if the right type of men can be secured, this should be a valuable suggestion. Our own impression is that the employment of masses of armed men can be of little avail in dealing with a secret subterranean movement like that which appears to be behind the recent series of murders of Japanese. To deal effectually with the situation it would seem necessary for the police to be in close touch with what is going on subterraneously among certain Chinese circles and the actual effects of the political situation among sections of the population. This work requires to be done by trained detectives, loyal to their exacting duty, and conversant with local conditions and trends. The cosmopolitan character of the town makes it extremely difficult work, of course, but it should be attempted as effectually as possible. It is possible that only a few persons are concerned in the recent murders but, on the other hand, it may be that they are engineered by quite an extensive and powerful organization which it ought to be possible to lay by the heels by careful detective work. We know that the local anti-Japanese extremists took very much to heart the banning of their activities in Nantao on September 18 when a number of rioters were hurt by the Chinese police in the execution of their duty. On September 23, the attack was made on the Japanese marines in Haining Road. Can it be that there is a direct connection between these two events? If so, it should not be beyond the bounds of possibility for the various local authorities, Chinese and foreign, by means of co-operative measures, to establish the fact and take action accordingly.
Some uneasiness has been caused by rumours that Chinese troops have been assembled in considerable numbers in the close vicinity of Shanghai. As a matter of fact there have been rumours to this effect ante-dating both the occurrences on September 18 and the affair of September 23. The Chinese deny them and we do not think that the rumours are justified; under present conditions it would be impossible for the Chinese authorities, supposing they were disposed to such Machiavellian tactics, which we do not believe, to assemble any worthwhile force adequately equipped, in the close vicinity of Shanghai without prompt discovery by other interested parties. Moreover, the events of 1932 have not been forgotten and it is obvious that any armed conflict provoked in or around Shanghai would cause the infliction of more suffering on the Chinese people than upon anybody else and could lead to no useful purpose. The laying out of the Civic Centre at Kiangwan, in an exposed and undefended spot, may be taken, we feel, as a measure of Chinese sincerity in implementing the armistice and keeping their armed military forces away from this international port. Seeing that the greater part of Shanghai is under international and neutral control there is no object to be gained by any Chinese military action in this neighbourhood unless it be suggested that the Japanese design to seize some of the territory around the city for some nefarious purpose—a hardly reasonable contention.

《上海泰晤士报》，1936年9月28日，星期一

虹口局势

经过数日的极度紧张之后，虹口的局势已大为缓和，但日本海军陆战队仍维持着多个分部 headquarters，在日本居民居住的区域，巡逻队和街头哨位依然随处可见。商界人士希望局势能迅速恢复正常，因为最近的动荡对该大片区域的贸易颇为不利。与此同时，当局正努力追踪涉嫌谋杀军曹田凑（Taminato，音译）并致其两名同伴受伤的人员，但尚无进一步逮捕的报告。一个特别警察小组正在上原副总监指挥下从虹口巡捕房展开行动，日本领事馆警察也与上海公共租界工部局警务处（S. M. P.）保持密切合作，共同办理此案。日本居留民团希望增加工部局警务处雇用的侦探人数，如果能找到合适的人选，这将是一个有价值的建议。我们自己的印象是，在处理像近期一系列谋杀日本人案件背后那种秘密的地下运动时，部署大量武装人员作用甚微。要有效应对局势，警方似乎有必要与某些中国圈子中的地下活动以及政治局势对各阶层民众的实际影响保持密切联系。这项工作需要由受过训练、忠于职守且熟悉当地情况和趋势的侦探来完成。当然，这座城市的国际性特征使得这项工作极其困难，但应尽可能有效地加以尝试。可能只有少数人参与了最近的谋杀案，但另一方面，这也可能是由一个相当庞大且强大的组织策划的，通过细致的侦探工作应该能够将其抓获。我们知道，当地反日极端分子对9月18日其在南市的活動被禁止一事耿耿于怀，当时多名暴徒在中国警察执行职务过程中受伤。9月23日，海宁路发生了袭击日本海军陆战队员的事件。这两起事件之间是否存在直接联系？如果是这样，中外各地方当局通过合作措施查明事实并采取相应行动，并非不可能。

有关中国军队在上海附近大量集结的谣言引起了一些不安。事实上，在此类谣言在9月18日事件和9月23日事件之前就已流传。中方予以否认，我们认为这些谣言毫无根据；在目前的情况下，即使中国当局有意采取这种马基雅维利式的策略（我们并不相信），他们也不可能在未经其他相关方迅速发现的情况下，在上海附近集结任何具备充分装备的有价值部队。此外，人们并未忘记1932年的事件，显然，在上海或其周边引发的任何武装冲突给中国人民带来的苦难将大于其他任何人，且不会带来任何有益的目的。我们将江湾市民中心选址在一个暴露且无防御的地点，视为中国履行停战协定、将其武装军事力量远离这个国际港口的诚意之举。鉴于上海大部分地区处于国际和中立控制之下，除非有人暗示日本企图出于某种邪恶目的夺取城市周边的部分领土——这是一个 hardly reasonable（难以合理成立）的论点——否则中国方面在此邻近地区采取任何军事行动都无利可图。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 28, 1936

All-Night Police Vigils
In Japanese Cotton Mill
Areas Prove Uneventful

Rumoured Plot By Terrorists To Launch Attack
On Establishments Comes To Naught; Local
Japanese Still In Grip Of Tension

LANDING PARTY WITHDRAWS NEARLY ALL
PATROLS FROM CHAPEI DISTRICT

Outwardly calm and quiet, there were indications yesterday that Hongkew is ready at any moment to flare up once again into a high pitch of excitement, the sudden death of a Korean morphine addict named Li Inshoku leading to the wildfire spread of rumours of another murder.
Tension, indeed, remains high among the Japanese community, and it was considered expedient to throw strong police cordons round all the principal Japanese cotton mills in the Yangtzepoo and Kashing Road districts during Saturday-Sunday night as the result of rumours of a plot by anti-Japanese terrorists to wreck the establishments.

Meanwhile, reports from Hankow reveal that a tense situation exists there also, causing the preparation of plans for the withdrawal of large numbers of Japanese residents to Shanghai and Japan.
In an effort to dispel the tension holding Japanese in Hongkew in its grip, Mr. Kitamura, Chief of the Consular Police, yesterday issued a warning to rumour-mongers, threatening severe punishment, although this did not check the alarm which spread following the death of Li Inshoku, which was proved to have been the result of heart failure.

Chapei Withdrawals
In pursuance of its policy of reducing patrols, the Japanese Naval Landing Party withdrew all bluejackets from the Rokusan Gardens and also from the cemetery near Peitsechiao. The only unit now in Chapei occupies a Japanese beverage factory on Kingwan Road.
The strong police cordons thrown round the Japanese cotton mills were withdrawn yesterday morning after an uneventful all-night vigil.

Schools To Reopen
It is officially announced that the Japanese schools will reopen this morning, but special precautions are considered desirable for the present and an escort will be provided to the 200 odd Japanese children who cross the river daily from Pootung.
Special measures for the protection of school children will also be arranged in the Hongkew District, it is understood.
The current situation was discussed between Mr. Wakasugi, Consul-General, and 16 leading members of the Japanese community at a meeting at the Consulate-General yesterday morning.
Investigations are still proceeding into the murder of Warrant Officer Taminato, but no further arrests have been made. The three suspects held by the police maintain unshaken their denials of complicity in the outrage.
In view of the present situation, all plans for athletic meetings between local stars and the members of the Japanese Olympic team, arriving here this morning in the s.s. Kashima Maru, have been cancelled.

Hankow Situation
Intended withdrawal of Japanese residents in Hankow to Shanghai and Japan, in view of the current tension, was reported last night by the local Japanese papers.
The first batch to leave, the Shanghai "Mainichi" said, will consist of the families of 50 employees of the Nihon Cotton Company and the Nikka Oil Manufacturing Company.
The instructions to leave Hankow were issued by Mr. Yoshimitsu Kadota and Mr. Katsutoshi Ishikawa, respectively managers of the cotton mill and the oil concern, who, according to the Shanghai "Nichi-Nichi," feared that a recurrence of trouble might isolate their employees, who live in the former British Concession, from the Japanese Concession.
Officials of the Taian Cotton Spinning Company, the "Nichi-Nichi" reported, have also requested the Home Office to permit the evacuation of families of their employees.
A Domei message reported the organization of a residents' committee in Hankow to cope with the situation arising out of the murder of Sergeant Yoshioka.
The meeting was attended by representatives of the Hankow Japanese Residents' Corporation, the Japanese Chamber of Commerce, the Consular Police and the naval and military authorities.

Hsiangtan Fire Protest
HANKOW, Sept. 27.—A fire in the office of the Nisshin Lisen Kaisha at Hsiangtan, Hunan, alleged to have been started by incendiaries, to-day resulted in vigorous representations to the Chinese authorities in Changsha.
In a demarche filed with the Hunan Provincial Government, Mr. Takagi, Japanese Consul in Changsha, protested against the fire and demanded the immediate apprehension of the culprits.
The fire, which took place late last night, was quickly extinguished by the staff of the shipping concern.—Domei.

Report On Pakhoi Inquiry
CANTON, Sept. 27.—A detailed report on the results of his investigation into the murder of Mr. Nakano, elderly Japanese storekeeper in Pakhoi, on September 3, was made to-day to Mr. Nakamura, Consul-General
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年9月28日，星期一

通宵警察警戒
在日资棉纺厂区域
证明平安无事

恐怖分子袭击各机构的
阴谋传闻落空；当地
日本人仍处于紧张状态

登陆部队几乎撤出
闸北区的所有巡逻队

表面看似平静安宁，但昨日有迹象表明，虹口随时可能再次爆发高度紧张局势，一名名叫李仁硕（Li Inshoku，音译）的朝鲜籍吗啡瘾君子的突然死亡，导致另一宗谋杀案的谣言如野火般蔓延。
的确，日本侨民中的紧张情绪依然高涨，鉴于有反日恐怖分子企图破坏各机构的阴谋传闻，人们认为在周六至周日夜间，对杨树浦和嘉善路地区所有主要日资棉纺厂部署强有力的警察警戒线是权宜之计。

与此同时，来自汉口的报告显示，那里也存在紧张局势，导致制定了将大量日本居民撤离至上海和日本的计划。
为了消除笼罩在虹口日本人心头的紧张情绪，领事警察署长北村先生（Mr. Kitamura，音译）昨日向散布谣言者发出警告，威胁要予以严厉惩罚，尽管这并未能遏制李仁硕死后蔓延的恐慌，死因已证实为心力衰竭。

闸北撤军
根据减少巡逻队的政策，日本海军陆战队撤出了罗森花园（Rokusan Gardens，音译）以及北四川路附近墓地的所有水兵。目前留在闸北的唯一一支部队占据着江湾路上的一家日本饮料厂。
经过一夜平静的警戒后，包围日资棉纺厂的强力警察警戒线于昨晨撤除。

学校复课
官方宣布，日本学校将于今晨复课，但目前认为有必要采取特别预防措施，并将为每日从浦东渡河而来的200多名日本儿童提供护卫。
据悉，虹口区也将安排保护学童的特别措施。
昨日早晨，总领事若杉先生（Mr. Wakasugi，音译）与16名日本社区领袖在总领事馆举行会议，讨论了当前局势。
对军曹田南户（Taminato，音译）被杀案的调查仍在进行中，但未有新的逮捕行动。警方拘留的三名嫌疑人坚决否认参与此次暴行。
鉴于当前局势，原定由本地明星与今晨乘“鹿岛丸”号（s.s. Kashima Maru）抵达此地的日本奥运代表队成员举行的体育比赛计划全部取消。

汉口局势
据当地日文报纸昨晚报道，鉴于当前的紧张局势，计划将汉口的日本居民撤离至上海和日本。
上海《每日新闻》称，第一批撤离者将由日本棉花公司和日华制油公司50名员工的家属组成。
撤离汉口的指令分别由棉纺厂经理角田吉光先生（Mr. Yoshimitsu Kadota，音译）和制油公司经理石川胜敏先生（Mr. Katsutoshi Ishikawa，音译）发布，据上海《日日新闻》报道，他们担心骚乱重演可能会使居住在前英租界的员工与日本租界隔离。
据《日日新闻》报道，泰安棉纺公司的官员也请求内务省允许其员工家属撤离。
同盟社消息报道，汉口成立了一个居民委员会，以应对因吉冈军曹（Sergeant Yoshioka，音译）被杀而引发的局势。
汉口日本居留民团、日本商会、领事警察以及海军和军事当局的代表出席了会议。

湘潭火灾抗议
汉口，9月27日电。——湖南湘潭日清轮船公司办事处发生火灾，据称系纵火犯所为，今日导致向日方驻长沙当局提出强烈交涉。
日本驻长沙领事高木先生（Mr. Takagi，音译）在向湖南省政府提交的外交照会中，对火灾提出抗议，并要求立即逮捕肇事者。
火灾发生于昨夜深夜，很快被该航运公司的职员扑灭。——同盟社。

北海调查报告
广州，9月27日电。——今日向总领事中村先生（Mr. Nakamura，音译）提交了一份关于其调查9月3日北海年老日本店主中野先生（Mr. Nakano，音译）被杀案结果的详细报告

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 29, 1936
C. 7538
29/9/36

Japanese Land
New Contingent
Of Bluejackets

Tension In Hongkew
Not Completely
Eased Yet

Although conditions in Hongkew were practically normal yesterday, tension had not eased altogether. Three more Japanese naval vessels arrived in port, among them being the transport Shiretogo with a contingent of 600 more bluejackets for the Special Naval Landing Party.
The Shiretogo arrived shortly after daybreak and the additional bluejackets disembarked at 10 a.m., going directly to the Japanese naval barracks. From the ship, they proceeded along Broadway to Minghong Road, turned down this thoroughfare and then to Boone Road from whence they moved on to Szechuen Road and the barracks.
The force of eight destroyers which arrived Sunday and unloaded 200 bluejackets for duty with the landing party was augmented by another destroyer, the Shihosaka, which arrived during the morning. The third naval ship to appear in the Whangpoo yesterday was the Fujiyama, a small vessel belonging to the high Japanese Naval Command. It is not a combatant ship but is apparently engaged in intelligence work.

8 Destroyers To Remain
Questioned regarding reports that the eight destroyers which put in their appearance Sunday are slated to leave port for duty on the lower Yangtse, Japanese officials informed a CHINA PRESS reporter that the reports were not quite true, adding that the ships would probably remain here for some time.
While the Japanese naval authorities would issue no statement concerning the present bluejacket strength in Shanghai, competent observers estimate it to be about 3,500 men, or 1,500 more than normal strength.
Bluejacket patrols are still being kept on duty in Hongkew both night and day. They are considerably scattered but they are present nevertheless. Only a few campaign hats of the Japanese Civilian Reserve are in evidence.
*
In the meantime, the police search for the slayers of Seaman Asamitsu Taminato, killed on the night of September 23, an incident which brought about the present tense situation, has developed into a matter of routine. The case has been taken from the hands of the detectives of the Hongkew Police station and is now being investigated by the Special Branch, S.M.P. which had its beginning in November, 1935, when Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama was slain on Darroch Road.

No New Developments
Officials of the Special Branch told THE CHINA PRESS yesterday that no new developments had occurred. Many of the residents around the

Haining and Yalu Road areas where the shooting occurred were questioned yesterday and their written statements taken. No definite clues as to the present whereabouts of the real leaders of the mob have been uncovered, police stated.
The three men arrested by Japanese on the night of the shooting and handed over to the Shanghai Municipal Police 24 hours later, will appear before the First Special District Court for a second time on Saturday of this week. At the first hearing of the case last Friday morning, they flatly denied that they had anything to do with the shooting. They have since been subjected to considerable police questioning but officials were close-mouthed when asked concerning the results of these interrogations.

Schools Resume Classes
All Japanese schools in the Hongkew and Chapei areas resumed classes yesterday after an emergency three-day holiday declared following the shooting last Wednesday night. Special precautions for the protection of the children were taken by the S.M.P. and the Japanese Consular Police, the Japanese Naval Landing Party and the Bureau of Public Safety.
A request that steps be instituted to prevent any untoward events involving children was made yesterday to the responsible authorities by a representative of the Japanese Residents' Corporation.
Monetary and other gifts for the family of the late Seaman Asamitsu Taminato, now referred to as a warrant officer, third class in Japanese dispatches, continued to be received by the Japanese papers yesterday. The gifts will be remitted to the dead seaman's family in Japan.

《大美晚报》，1936年9月29日，星期二
C. 7538
36/9/29

日本登陆
新一批
水兵

虹口紧张局势
尚未完全
缓解

尽管昨日虹口的情况基本正常，但紧张局势并未完全缓解。又有三艘日本军舰抵达港口，其中包括运输舰“知床”号（Shiretogo），载有600名增援特别海军陆战队的水兵。
“知床”号在黎明后不久抵达，增援水兵于上午10时登陆，直接前往日本海军兵营。他们从船上出发，沿百老汇路行进至明宏路（Minghong Road，音译），转入这条大道，然后前往布恩路（Boone Road，即今塘沽路），再从那里移往四川路及兵营。
周日抵达并为登陆部队卸下200名执勤水兵的八艘驱逐舰编队，又增加了一艘名为“四方坂”号（Shihosaka，音译）的驱逐舰，该舰于上午抵达。昨日出现在黄浦江上的第三艘海军舰艇是“富士山”号（Fujiyama），这是一艘隶属于日本海军高层指挥部的小型船只。它并非战斗舰艇，但显然从事情报工作。

8艘驱逐舰将停留
就有关周日出现的八艘驱逐舰预定离开港口前往下游长江执行任务的报道，日本官员告知《大美晚报》记者，这些报道并不完全属实，并补充说这些船只可能会在此停留一段时间。
虽然日本海军当局未就上海目前的水兵人数发表声明，但经验丰富的观察家估计约为3,500人，比正常人数多出1,500人。
水兵巡逻队日夜在虹口执勤。他们的分布相当分散，但确实存在。只有少数日本民间后备队的宽檐帽可见。
*
与此同时，警方对9月23日晚被杀的水兵浅光田南户（Asamitsu Taminato，音译）凶手的搜捕已变成例行公事，这一事件导致了目前的紧张局势。该案已从虹口警察局侦探手中接管，现由工部局警务处特务科（Special Branch, S.M.P.）进行调查，该科室始于1935年11月，当时军曹中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama，音译）在达罗克路（Darroch Road，即今多伦路）被杀。

无新进展
特务科官员昨日告诉《大美晚报》，没有发生新的进展。昨日讯问了枪击案发生的海宁路和鸭绿江路地区周围的许多居民，并记录了他们的书面证词。警方表示，尚未发现关于暴徒真正头目目前下落的任何确切线索。
在枪击当晚被日本人逮捕并在24小时后移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处的三名男子，将于本周六第二次出庭受审于第一特区法院。在上周五上午对该案的首次听证会上，他们断然否认与枪击案有任何牵连。此后他们接受了大量的警方讯问，但当被问及这些讯问的结果时，官员们守口如瓶。

学校复课
在上周三晚枪击案发生后宣布紧急放假三天之后，虹口和闸北地区的所有日本学校于昨日复课。工部局警务处、日本领事警察、日本海军陆战队和公安局采取了特别措施保护儿童。
日本居留民团代表昨日向有关当局提出请求，要求采取措施防止涉及儿童的任何不幸事件发生。
昨日，日本报纸继续收到献给已故水兵浅光田南户（现日本电文中称为三等军曹）家属的金钱和其他礼物。这些礼物将汇给死者在日本的家属。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, September 28, 1936 16776

Hongkew Area
Tension Easing;
Schools Reopen

Local Organizations
Meeting; Chinese
Troops On Move

JAPANESE SHIPS
MASS IN HARBOR

Nanking Forces Said
In Concentration
At Soochow

Indicative of the gradual return to normalcy in the Hongkew and Chapei areas, Japanese schools today resumed classes after an emergency three-day holiday declared following the shooting of three Japanese sailors last Wednesday night.

Special precautions for the protection of the children were being taken by the Shanghai Municipal and the Japanese Consular Police, the Japanese Special Naval Landing party, and the Bureau of Public Safety.

Gifts Sent

A request that steps be instituted to prevent any untoward events involving children was made today to the responsible authorities by a representative of the Japanese Residents' Corporation.

Monetary and other gifts for the family of the late Asamitsu Shiminto, Warrant Officer, Third Class, slain last Wednesday, and for the two other sailors who were seriously injured in the attack continued to be received on Sunday, by the local Japanese papers for handling.

Accompanying 6771 "comfort bags" to be distributed among the men of the Third Japanese Fleet, representatives of the Tsingtao Japanese Residents' Corporation called on Vice-Admiral Koshiro Oikawa this morning.

The contents of the bags were donated by the Japanese residents of Tsingtao, Chefoo and other Shantung cities, while the various Japanese spinning mills provided the containers.

Members of the standing committee of the Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions in Shanghai today continued their daily meetings for an exchange of information.

Chinese Troops Reported

The Shanghai Nippo yesterday again reported heavy Chinese military movements in the vicinity of Shanghai.

Stating that the source of its information was "trustworthy," the daily said that a part of the Central Government forces stationed in Nanking had been moved by road and by train to Soochow. Large numbers of graduates of the Hangchow Aviation school, which also gives instruction in anti-aircraft work were included among the units transported, according to the journal.

At Hangchow, the Nippo continued, a large number of aircraft has been concentrated, with planes arriving there daily.

Chinese Activity Reported

According to unconfirmed Japanese reports, alleging to have received information from "reliable sources," Nanking government is concentrating troops in this region.

At Kiating and Chenju, near the border of the demilitarized zone created by the Shanghai truce agreement in 1932, there are reported to be 30,000 Chinese soldiers.

Since the evening of September 23, that is, one night after the slaying of a Japanese bluejacket in Hongkew, a number of military trucks, crowded with soldiers and laden with provisions, have been reportedly seen driving along the highway between Nanking and Soochow. There has also been considerable activity among graduates of the aviation schools, it is alleged.

Soochow Active?

In Soochow, there were formerly 1500 soldiers, but now the city has suddenly become a center of great military activity, these reports added. In Changshu, a district 60 li from Soochow there are now contracted about 40,000, it is declared.

During the past two or three days, a number of military airplanes have arrived at the flying field in Hangchow the report say.

According to these same sources, 3000 soldiers in plain-clothes have arrived secretly in Shanghai, Chinese officials here vigorously deny that there is any Chinese troops concentration.

A large quantity of arms and military supplies, the exact amount of which is unknown, was landed in Shanghai yesterday morning from several of the Japanese warships which arrived here according to Chinese reports. The goods were rushed to the Naval Landing Party Headquarters near Hongkew Park by special trucks, they add.

Warships Concentrate

Japanese naval vessels in the Shanghai harbor concentrated over the weekend, though today three of them sailed. The Idzumo, flagship, is still here. The Kurotake sailed Saturday.

Yesterday 10 Japanese destroyers arrived in harbor from Japan: the Kuri, Tanikazi, Nadakazi, Shimakazi, Satsuki, Fumitsuki, Nagatsuki, Minatsuki, Shihokazi, and Shiritoko Three of these vessels sailed this morning, the Kuri, Tanikazi and Nadakazi. Thus today there are still seven destroyers and the flagship here. These destroyers brought reinforcements of bluejackets, variously reported as ranging from 200 to 500 men.

An unconfirmed Chinese report last night that an airplane carrier had arrived with the fleet and was anchored outside Woosung was denied by responsible officials today.

The destroyers are part of the 22nd Destroyer Flotilla and came here from the Yokosuka Naval Base.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年9月28日，星期一 16776

虹口地区
紧张局势缓和；
学校复课

本地团体
举行会议；中国
军队调动

日本舰船
集结于港口

据称南京部队
在苏州集结

随着虹口和闸北地区逐渐恢复正常秩序，日本学校在上周三晚三名日本水兵遭枪击后宣布紧急放假三天之后，于今日复课。

工部局警务处、日本领事馆警察、日本特别海军陆战队以及公安局正采取特别预防措施以保护儿童。

赠送礼物

日本居留民团代表今日向有关当局提出请求，要求采取措施防止涉及儿童的任何意外事件发生。

为上周三被杀害的三等军曹（Warrant Officer, Third Class）下里浅光（Asamitsu Shiminto，音译）的家属，以及在袭击中受重伤的另外两名水兵提供的金钱和其他礼物，周日继续由当地日文报纸代收处理。

青岛日本居留民团代表今晨拜访了及川古志郎（Koshiro Oikawa）海军中将，随行带来了将分发给日本第三舰队官兵的6771个“慰问袋”。

袋内物品由青岛、烟台及其他山东城市的日本居民捐赠，而各种日本纺纱厂提供了包装袋。

上海日本街道工会联合会常务委员会成员今日继续举行日常会议，交流信息。

据报中国军队调动

《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo）昨日再次报道上海附近有大量中国军事调动。

该日报称其消息来源“可靠”，并表示驻扎在南京的中央政府部队的一部分已通过公路和铁路调往苏州。据该报称，在被调动的部队中包括大量杭州航空学校的毕业生，该校也提供防空作业指导。

《上海日报》继续报道，在杭州，大量飞机已集中，每天都有飞机抵达那里。

据报中国方面活动

根据未经证实的日本报告，声称从“可靠来源”获得信息，南京政府正在该地区集结部队。

据报道，在靠近1932年上海停战协定所设非军事区边界的嘉定和陈家渡（Chenju，音译），有3万名中国士兵。

自9月23日晚以来，即虹口一名日本水兵被杀后的第二天晚上，据称有人看到许多载满士兵和给养的军用卡车沿着南京和苏州之间的公路行驶。据称，航空学校的毕业生也有相当多的活动。

苏州活跃？

这些报道补充说，苏州以前有1500名士兵，但现在该市突然成为大规模军事活动的中心。据称，在距离苏州60里的常熟，现在集结了约4万人。

报道说，在过去两三天里，许多军用飞机已经抵达杭州的飞机场。

据同一消息来源称，3000名便衣士兵已秘密抵达上海，但此间的中国官员强烈否认有任何中国军队集结。

据中文报道，昨天上午，几艘抵达这里的日本军舰在上海卸下大量武器和军用物资，确切数量不详。报道还称，这些物资由专用卡车迅速运往虹口公园附近的海军陆战队总部。

军舰集结

周末期间，上海港内的日本海军舰艇集中，尽管今天其中三艘已驶离。旗舰“出云”号（Idzumo）仍在此处。“黑竹”号（Kurotake）于周六驶离。

昨天，10艘日本驱逐舰从日本抵达港口：栗（Kuri）、谷风（Tanikazi）、滩风（Nadakazi）、岛风（Shimakazi）、皋月（Satsuki）、文月（Fumitsuki）、长月（Nagatsuki）、水无月（Minatsuki）、汐风（Shihokazi）和白鸟（Shiritoko）。其中三艘舰艇今晨驶离，分别是栗、谷风和滩风。因此，今天这里仍有七艘驱逐舰和旗舰。这些驱逐舰带来了水兵增援部队，人数据报道在200至500人之间不等。

昨晚有一则未经证实的中国报道称，一艘航空母舰随舰队抵达并停泊在吴淞口外，今日有关负责官员予以否认。

这些驱逐舰属于第22驱逐舰队，来自横须贺海军基地。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 29, 1936
16778

$5,000 Reward
Posted by Police
In Murder Case

Japanese Schools Reopen
After Three Days

HONGKEW NOW CALM

6,771 "Comfort Bags" for
Japanese Sailors

A reward of $5,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the person or persons responsible for the murder of a Japanese blue-jacket and the serious wounding of two of his comrades, in Hongkew last Wednesday evening, was offered yesterday by the Shanghai Municipal Police.

Three Chinese have been arrested in connection with the shooting and are to appear in the First Special District Court on Saturday morning. It is believed, however, that the actual murderer, who emptied a military Mauser pistol at the sailors, is still at large. The two wounded men are recovering.

Mr. A. Tajima, Deputy Commissioner of the S.M. Police and Special Political Officer, when interviewed yesterday, said that the investigators were "doing their best" but that the nature of their findings must remain dark for the present. He expressed confidence in the outcome of the inquiry.

In Hongkew the nervousness of the last few days was gradually subsiding and, although the scare-mongers were still active, the district was outwardly calm. Japanese schools there and in Chapei resumed classes yesterday morning, after having been closed for three days because of the incident.

Children Protected

Special precautions for the protection of the children were being taken by the Shanghai Municipal and the Japanese Consular Police, the Japanese Special Naval Landing party, and the Bureau of Public Safety, Domei reported.

A request that steps be instituted to prevent any untoward events involving children was made yesterday to the responsible authorities by a representative of the Japnese Residents Corporation.

Monetary and other gifts for the family of the late Asamitsu Taminato, Warrant Officer, Third Class, who was murdered last Wednesday, and for the two other sailors who were wounded in the attack, continued to be received by the local Japanese papers.

Accompanying 6,771 "comfort bags," to be distributed among the men of the Third Japanese Fleet, representatives of the Tsingtao Japanese Residents Corporation called on Vice-Admiral Koshiro Oikawa yesterday morning.

The contents of the bags were contributed by the Japanese Residents of Tsingtao, Chefoo and other Shantung cities, while the various Japanese spinning mills provided the containers.

Members of the standing committee of the Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions in Shanghai yesterday continued their daily meetings for an exchange of information, Domei further reported.

Tokyo Talks

Tokyo, Sept. 28.

Three of Japan's leading Cabinet ministers, Mr. Hirota, the Premier, Mr. Arita, Minister for Foreign Affairs, and Admiral Nagano, Minister of the Navy, conferred for an hour to-day regarding the Chinese situation.

They discussed, it is reported, the little progress made in Nanking concerning the negotiations with the Chinese Government on the Japanese decision to deal directly with General Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan, and also the attitude of the Chinese Government on this question.

Views were also exchanged regarding Japanese policy in China in the future.

Under the presidency of Prince Fushimi, Chief of the Naval General Staff, the Naval War Council held a two-hour conference here to-day. The Council listened to an exposition by Admiral O. Nagano, Minister of Navy, dealing with recent events in China.

Admiral Nagano's address was along those lines with which the Japanese Government is endeavouring to reach a settlement of recent anti-Japanese incidents in China. At the conclusion of Admiral Nagano's speech, the Council voiced its unanimous approval of his policies and actions in his efforts to tide over the present crisis.—Reuter.

《字林西报》，1936年9月29日，星期二 16778

警方悬赏
5,000美元
缉拿谋杀案凶手

日本学校
停课三天后复课

虹口现已平静

6,771个“慰问袋”
赠予日本水兵

上海公共租界工部局警务处昨日悬赏5,000美元，征求线索以逮捕并定罪上周三晚在虹口谋杀一名日本水兵并致其两名同伴重伤的责任人。

三名中国人因与枪击案有关被捕，将于周六上午在第一特区法院出庭。然而，人们相信，实际行凶者——当时向水兵们打空了一支军用毛瑟手枪的人——仍然在逃。两名伤者正在康复中。

工部局警务处副总监兼特别政治专员田岛（A. Tajima，音译）先生昨日在接受采访时说，调查人员正在“竭尽全力”，但目前调查结果仍不明朗。他对调查的结果表示有信心。

在虹口，过去几天的紧张情绪逐渐平息，尽管散布恐慌者仍然活跃，但该区域表面上保持平静。那里的日本学校以及闸北的日本学校在因该事件关闭三天后，于昨日上午复课。

保护儿童

据同盟社报道，工部局警务处、日本领事馆警察、日本特别海军陆战队以及公安局正采取特别预防措施以保护儿童。

日本居留民团代表昨日向有关当局提出请求，要求采取措施防止涉及儿童的任何意外事件发生。

当地日文报纸继续接收为上周三被谋杀的三等军曹田皆浅光（Asamitsu Taminato，音译）的家属，以及在袭击中受伤的两名其他水兵提供的金钱和其他礼物。

青岛日本居留民团代表昨晨拜访了及川古志郎海军中将，随行带来了将分发给日本第三舰队官兵的6,771个“慰问袋”。

袋内物品由青岛、烟台及其他山东城市的日本居民捐赠，而各种日本纺纱厂提供了包装袋。

同盟社进一步报道，上海日本街道工会联合会常务委员会成员昨日继续举行日常会议，交流信息。

东京会谈

东京，9月28日电。

日本三位主要内阁大臣，首相广田弘毅（Hirota，音译）、外相有田八郎（Arita，音译）和海军大臣永野修身（Nagano，音译）海军上将，今日就中国局势进行了一小时的磋商。

据报道，他们讨论了在南京就日本政府决定直接与行政院院长蒋介石将军进行谈判一事与中国政府谈判进展甚微的情况，以及中国政府对此问题的态度。

双方还就日本未来的对华政策交换了意见。

在海军军令部长伏见宫亲王的主持下，海军军议会今日在此举行了两小时的会议。军议会听取了海军大臣永野修身海军上将关于中国近期事件的阐述。

永野海军上将的讲话主旨与日本政府努力解决近期在华反日事件的方向一致。在永野海军上将发言结束时，军议会对其为渡过当前危机而在政策和行动上的努力表示一致赞同。——路透社

16779
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 29, 1936

Hongkew And Chapei Areas
Again Back To Normal
Japanese School Children Take Up Studies While
Special Precautions Are Taken To Prevent
Untoward Incidents Or Attacks

Indicative of the gradual return to normalcy in the Hongkew and Chapei areas, Japanese schools yesterday resumed classes after an emergency three-day holiday declared following the shooting of three Japanese sailors last Wednesday night.

Special precautions for the protection of the children were being taken by the Shanghai Municipal and the Japanese Consular Police, the Japanese Special Naval Landing party, and the Bureau of Public Safety.

A request that steps be instituted to prevent any untoward events involving children was made yesterday to the responsible authorities by a representative of the Japanese Residents' Corporation.

Monetary and other gifts for the family of the late Asamitsu Taminato, Warrant Officer, Third Class, slain last Wednesday, and for the two other sailors who were seriously injured in the attack, continued to be received on Sunday by the local Japanese papers for handling.

Comforts For Sailors

Accompanying 6,771 "comfort bags" to be distributed among the men of the Third Japanese Fleet, representatives of the Tsingtao Japanese Residents' Corporation called on Vice-Admiral Koshiro Oikawa yesterday morning.

The contents of the bags were donated by the Japanese residents of Tsingtao, Chefoo and other Shantung cities, while the various Japanese spinning mills provided the containers.

Members of the standing committee of the Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions in Shanghai yesterday continued their daily meetings for an exchange of information.

The Shanghai "Nippo" yesterday again reported heavy Chinese military movements in the vicinity of Shanghai.

Stating that the source of its information was "trustworthy," the daily said that a part of the Central Government forces stationed in Nanking had been moved by road and by train to Soochow. Large numbers of graduates of the Hangchow Aviation school, which also gives instruction in anti-aircraft work, were included among the units transported, according to the journal.

At Hangchow, the "Nippo" continued, a large number of aircraft has been concentrated, with planes arriving there daily.

16779
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年9月29日，星期二

虹口和闸北地区
再次恢复正常
日本学童恢复学业 同时
采取特别预防措施以防
意外事件或袭击

随着虹口和闸北地区逐渐恢复正常秩序，日本学校在上周三晚三名日本水兵遭枪击后宣布紧急放假三天之后，于昨日复课。

工部局警务处、日本领事馆警察、日本特别海军陆战队以及公安局正采取特别预防措施以保护儿童。

日本居留民团代表昨日向有关当局提出请求，要求采取措施防止涉及儿童的任何意外事件发生。

为上周三被杀害的三等军曹田皆浅光（Asamitsu Taminato，音译）的家属，以及在袭击中受重伤的另外两名水兵提供的金钱和其他礼物，周日继续由当地日文报纸代收处理。

慰劳水兵

青岛日本居留民团代表昨晨拜访了及川古志郎海军中将，随行带来了将分发给日本第三舰队官兵的6,771个“慰问袋”。

袋内物品由青岛、烟台及其他山东城市的日本居民捐赠，而各种日本纺纱厂提供了包装袋。

上海日本街道工会联合会常务委员会成员昨日继续举行日常会议，交流信息。

《上海日报》昨日再次报道上海附近有大量中国军事调动。

该日报称其消息来源“可靠”，并表示驻扎在南京的中央政府部队的一部分已通过公路和铁路调往苏州。据该报称，在被调动的部队中包括大量杭州航空学校的毕业生，该校也提供防空作业指导。

《上海日报》继续报道，在杭州，大量飞机已集中，每天都有飞机抵达那里。

TRANSLATION.

EXCERPTS FROM LOCAL GERMAN NEWSPAPER.
D. 7538
25 9 36

The issue of the local German daily newspaper
entitled "Ostasiatischer Lloyd" dated September 25,
commenting on the Japanese action in Hongkew on the night
of September 24, contains an article entitled "WHERE WERE
THE SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE?" as follows:-

"During the entire night of Wednesday only Japanese
marines were to be seen in Hongkew. The Shanghai
Municipal Police were not on duty although it is their
right to be there. Many of the residents who were held
up must have considered it their right to receive the
protection of the Police and to be assisted on their
way home."

In an editorial published in the local German
newspaper entitled "Ostasiatischer Lloyd" dated September
26, this paper definitely takes sides with the Shanghai
Municipal Council and the Chinese against the Japanese
Marines' aggression. The editorial was dictated by the
German Consul-General von Kriebel to the editor Herr
Kuldermann and is as follows:-

" Proclamation on the Garden Bridge

The sudden appearance of a Japanese proclamation on
the Garden Bridge threatening everybody with drastic
punishment should they be found to be anti-Japanese is
undoubtedly 'going the limit'. The Japanese have no
jurisdiction either in the Settlement or in Chinese
territory. Such proclamations should be confined to the
Japanese barracks.

"Now-a-days, the motto 'We go the full hog' appears
to be the general role of the Japanese. Such conduct
surely cannot be considered to improve the Sino-Japanese
relations, it is more likely to drive China finally into
the embrace of her neighbour--Soviet Russia.

"It is our opinion that the instigators of all the
murders can be found in the South of China who are bent on
sabotaging the honest intentions of the Central Government."

译文。

当地德文报纸摘录。
D. 7538
1936年9月25日

9月25日出版的当地德文日报《东亚劳埃德报》（Ostasiatischer Lloyd）就9月24日晚日军在虹口的行动发表评论，其中包含一篇题为“上海公共租界工部局警务处何在？”的文章，内容如下：-

“在周三的整个夜晚，虹口只可见到日本海军陆战队队员。上海公共租界工部局警务处并未执勤，尽管他们有权在那里驻守。许多被拦截的居民一定认为，接受警方保护并获助回家是他们的权利。”

在9月26日出版的当地德文报纸《东亚劳埃德报》发表的一篇社论中，该报明确站在上海公共租界工部局和中国人一边，反对日本海军陆战队的侵略行为。该社论由德国总领事冯·克里贝尔（von Kriebel）口授给编辑库尔德曼（Kuldermann）先生，内容如下：-

“外白渡桥公告

外白渡桥上突然出现的日本公告，威胁任何人若被发现反日将受到严厉惩罚，这无疑是‘做得太过分了’。日本人无论在租界还是在中国领土上均无管辖权。此类公告应仅限于日本兵营内张贴。

“如今，‘我们要干就干到底’这句口号似乎成了日本人的普遍准则。这种行为显然不能被视为有助于改善中日关系，反而更可能最终将中国推向其邻国——苏维埃俄国的怀抱。

“我们认为，所有谋杀案的煽动者可以在华南找到，这些人一心要破坏中央政府的诚意。”

CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 28, 1936
（批：16760 7538 28 9 36）

8 Warships
Arrive From
Nippon Base

200 Additional Men Join
Japanese Naval
Landing Party

UNEASINESS IN
HONGKEW PREVAILS

Chinese, S. M. Police
Guard Against
Incidents

Eight Japanese destroyers, bringing a reinforcement of 200 additional bluejackets, arrived here yesterday morning.
The arrival, together with the reported activities of the Japanese Naval Landing Party details in Chapei and the vigilant which kept throughout the day by police of the three Shanghai areas on a demonstration which did not take place, provoked considerable uneasiness in Hongkew.
The Nipponese men-of-war which arrived yesterday consist of four first class destroyers and four second class destroyers, consisting of the 22nd Destroyer Flotilla, the men-of-war came here directly from the Yokosuka Naval Base and tied up at the Japanese naval buoys in Yangtszepoo.
Immediately after the ships docked, a party of 200 bluejackets were landed. The detachment left for the Japanese Naval Landing Party barracks on Kiangwan Road.
3 Vessels Leave For Unknown
Later in the afternoon, three of the destroyers left for an unrevealed destination.
An unconfirmed Chinese report last night said that an airplane carrier also arrived with the new fleet and was anchored outside of Woosung.
In Chapei yesterday, a large group of Japanese Naval Landing Party details were reported to be still stationed on the tract of land recently purchased by the Nipponese. Although Japanese consular authorities here have consistently refused to comment on this point, Chinese sources report that a large amount of building material was being transported to the lot which is situated at Paitsechiao across the Shanghai-Woosung Railway in Chapei

Korean Dies
Throughout the day reports and rumors of every description circulated the city. One wild rumor had another Japanese murdered in Hongkew. A later investigation revealed that a Korean, riding in a ricksha near the Chapoo Road Bridge and North Soochow Road, had been found dead.
Mistaken at first for a Chinese, he was conveyed to the St. Luke's Hospital. When his nationality was finally discovered, the Japanese Consular Police was called. An inquest conducted at St. Luke's Hospital by the Nipponese officials revealed that the man died of heart disease. He was identified as Lee in Sehaku.
Although the report was current yesterday that a demonstration was scheduled to take place in Yangtszepoo and Chapei, no disturbance took place. The police of the three areas, however, was on watch for any sign of trouble.
Meantime, despite the exhaustive investigation conducted by the S.M.P. into the killing of a Japanese bluejacket and the wounding of two others, no material headway was made in unearthing a working clue.

Jb.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年9月28日，星期一
（批注：16760 7538 1936年9月28日）

8艘军舰
从日本基地
抵达

200名增援人员加入
日本海军
陆战队

虹口地区
弥漫不安情绪

华人、上海公共租界工部局警务处
防范
事件发生

八艘日本驱逐舰载着200名新增援的水兵于昨晨抵达此处。
此次抵达，加之据报道日本海军陆战队分队在闸北的活动，以及上海三个区域的警察全天保持警惕以防并未发生的示威活动，在虹口引起了相当大的不安。
昨日抵达的日本军舰包括四艘一级驱逐舰和四艘二级驱逐舰，隶属于第22驱逐舰队，这些军舰直接从横须贺海军基地驶来，停泊在杨树浦的日本海军浮筒处。
船只靠岸后，立即有200名水兵登陆。该分队前往江湾路的日本海军陆战队兵营。
3艘舰船驶往
未知目的地
下午晚些时候，三艘驱逐舰驶往一个未公开的目的地。
昨晚一份未经证实的中国方面报告称，一艘航空母舰也随新舰队抵达，并停泊在吴淞口外。

昨日在闸北，据报道仍有大批日本海军陆战队分队驻扎在日本人最近购买的一块土地上。尽管日本领事当局在此一直拒绝对此发表评论，但中方消息来源报告称，大量建筑材料正被运往位于闸北沪吴铁路对面的八字桥的地块。

一名朝鲜人死亡
整天城里流传着各种报告和谣言。有一个荒诞的谣言称又有一名日本人在虹口被杀。随后的调查揭示，一名朝鲜人乘坐人力车经过乍浦路桥与北苏州路附近时，被发现已死亡。
起初他被误认为是中国人，被送往圣路加医院。当他的国籍最终被查明后，日本领事警察被召来。日本官员在圣路加医院进行的验尸调查显示，此人死于心脏病。死者身份确认为李在伯（Lee in Sehaku，音译）。

尽管昨天有报告称计划在杨树浦和闸北举行示威活动，但并未发生骚乱。然而，这三个区域的警察一直在监视任何麻烦的迹象。

与此同时，尽管上海公共租界工部局警务处对一名日本水兵被杀及另外两名受伤一事进行了详尽调查，但在发掘有效线索方面未取得实质性进展。

Jb.

CHINA DAILY HERALD, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 25, 1936.
（批：10697）
（批：REGISTRY 7538）
（批：26 9 36）

A WARNING TO CHINESE
POPULATION

China Sovereignty Violated

Secretary Of Chinese Municipal
Government Lodging Protest

The Japanese Naval Landing Party took over complete control of the entire Hongkew District from 8.23 o'clock Wednesday night and was in control of that district yesterday as a result of an outrage which occurred in Yalu Road.

It is believed that four men were the assailants of A. Taminato, Y. Deriba and Y. Yawata. They are alleged to have fired from an alleyway a few yards from the intersection. One Chinese in coolie clothes, alleged to have been one of the four, was arrested by S.M.P. Special Constable McAllan, assisted by bystanders. He was immediately taken to the Chapoo Road sub-station of the Japanese Naval Landing Party for questioning.

The alarm was raised immediately after the shooting, and following the arrest of an alleged member of the gang, whom the bystanders stated was caught in the act of throwing a military Mauser pistol into a sand-box placed at the corner of the alleyway from which the shots were presumed to have been fired. It is supposed that, in all, ten shots were fired, and seven or eight cartridge cases were picked up from the pavement by police and marines who were soon on the scene.

There was not a member of the Shanghai Municipal Police, Chinese or foreign, inside the cordon with exception of a few high foreign officers who came from headquarters to investigate.

No foreign officers could be seen anywhere, and very few Chinese.

There was no doubt in the minds of the hundreds of Chinese and Europeans in the area that the Japanese with the bayonets were the law in Hongkew. Many foreigners who lived inside the area and who were returning to their homes late in the night, were not allowed to pass the barriers and had to spend the night with friends or in hotels.

Only through the aid of a special pass issued by the Japanese Consulate General could a foreign newspaperman succeed in passing through the lines. Hongkew inside that area was a veritable city of the dead—dark and deserted save for the grim patrols. The atmosphere was very tense; those few who were on the streets walked and spoke softly and kept apprehensive eyes on the marines.

The Japanese Landing Party headquarters on Haining Road opposite the Willies Theatre bristled with bayonets; motorcycles stood waiting at the door. Cycles with sidecars roared through the district; each sidecar carried two marines fully armed.

The actual spot where the blue-jackets were shot is Yalu Road, about 100 feet west of the Woosung Road corner. This is in front of a block of Chinese and Japanese shops and houses of the usual type in that district, and the man who was killed was hit by a bullet apparently fired from a narrow alleyway giving off Yalu Road toward the north. The spot was chalked off, each separate mark of clue being ringed with chalk, and all was carefully guarded to prevent anyone disturbing it.

Those who had been attending the cinema at the Willies Theatre were detained for several hours after the incident, though the show was stopped immediately. Later they were released in small groups and were escorted out of the area under guard. Many were carefully searched at the barriers.

A large per cent of the crowd watching outside the barriers was composed of Japanese civilians, who appeared very excited.

Japanese newspapermen and photographers were very active, continuously taking flashlight pictures. They all seemed to have free and easy access to the prohibited area, coming and going as they pleased. Other foreign newspapermen without passes, however, were abruptly turned back.

Tanks rumbled down North Szechuen Road from the Landing Party barracks.

The barracks seethed with activity as several hundred marines were waiting under arms there. Armored cars, tanks and motorcycles were ready to roll from the compound.

At the Japanese Consulate-General troops were on guard, and there was a great deal of hurried coming and going. Conferences were being held one after another all night.

The following is translation of a proclamation in Chinese issued yesterday by the Japanese Naval Landing Party and posted on walls on Range, North Szechuen, Woosung and Haining Roads:—

"Notice is hereby given that the action taken by the Japanese Naval Landing Party is for self-defence and its main purpose is to protect Japanese lives and property. No mercy will be shown to those who regard our authorities and our people as enemies or who violate peace and order. We hope that all Shanghai citizens will understand the true motive of the Naval Landing Party and conduct their business in peace."

A vigorous denial that his son, Chang Yung-wu, 2t., is in any way connected with the "Hongkew Incident" was issued by the youth's father when approached by Chinese newspapermen. The suspect now detained by the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party is the only surviving son of 10 boys born in the Chang family.

Chang, his father declares, is a food-stall keeper working near the East Yalu Road Bridge. On Wednesday night he heard pistol shots and rushed to Woosung Road to find out the trouble and was arrested by the Japanese Officers.

The youth, at the time of his arrest, wore a foreign-style shirt and a pair of trousers which he bought from a second-hand goods store, his father said.

对华人的
警告

中国主权受侵犯

上海市市政府秘书长
提出抗议

由于鸭绿江路发生的一起暴行，日本海军陆战队从周三晚上8点23分起接管了整个虹口区的全部控制权，并在昨天继续控制该地区。

据信有四人是田凑爱太郎（A. Taminato）、出羽勇（Y. Deriba）和八幡勇（Y. Yawata）的袭击者。据称他们从距离交叉路口几码远的一条小巷里开枪。一名身穿苦力服装的中国人，据称是四人之一，被上海公共租界工部局警务处特别警员麦卡伦（McAllan）在旁观者的协助下逮捕。他随即被带到乍浦路日本海军陆战队分驻所进行讯问。

枪响后立即发出警报，随后逮捕了一名涉嫌团伙成员，旁观者称此人被抓时正试图将一把军用毛瑟手枪扔进 presumed 射击来源的小巷角落的沙箱里。据推测，总共开了十枪，很快赶到现场的警察和海军陆战队队员从人行道上捡起了七八个弹壳。

除了几名从总部前来调查的高级外籍警官外，警戒线内没有一名上海公共租界工部局警务处的华籍或外籍警员。

到处都看不到外籍警官，华籍警员也寥寥无几。

该地区数百名华人和欧洲人心中毫无疑问，持刺刀的日本人在虹口就是法律。许多居住在该区域内深夜回家的外国人，不被允许通过关卡，不得不与朋友共度夜晚或住在旅馆里。

只有凭借日本总领事馆签发的特别通行证，一名外国记者才得以穿过封锁线。该区域内的虹口简直是一座死城——除了阴森的巡逻队外，黑暗而荒凉。气氛非常紧张；街上寥寥无几的人行走和说话都很轻声，并警惕地注视着海军陆战队队员。

位于海宁路威利剧院（Willies Theatre）对面的日本陆战队总部刺刀林立；摩托车在门口待命。带边车的摩托车在区内呼啸而过；每辆边车载有两名全副武装的海军陆战队队员。

水兵遭枪击的实际地点是鸭绿江路，位于吴淞路口以西约100英尺处。这里位于一排中式和日式店铺及该区常见类型的房屋前，死者显然是被从鸭绿江路向北的一条狭窄小巷射出的子弹击中。现场用粉笔圈出，每个单独的线索标记都用粉笔画圈，并严加看守以防止任何人破坏。

威利剧院的电影观众在事件发生后被扣留了数小时，尽管演出立即停止。后来他们被分成小组释放，并在护卫下被带离该区域。许多人在关卡处受到了仔细搜身。

在关卡外围观的人群中，很大一部分由日本平民组成，他们显得非常激动。

日本记者和摄影师非常活跃，不断拍摄闪光灯照片。他们似乎都能自由轻松地进入禁区，随意进出。然而，其他没有通行证的外国记者则被粗暴地挡回。

坦克从陆战队兵营隆隆驶下四川北路。

兵营内活动频繁，数百名海军陆战队队员持械待命。装甲车、坦克和摩托车随时准备从营地出发。

日本总领事馆内有部队守卫，人员匆忙进出频繁。整夜会议一场接一场地召开。

以下是日本海军陆战队昨日发布并张贴在百老汇路、四川北路、吴淞路和海宁路墙壁上的中文公告的译文：—

“特此通告，日本海军陆战队所采取之行动系出于自卫，其主要目的为保护日本人之生命财产。凡视我方当局及人民为敌人或扰乱和平秩序者，决不予宽恕。望上海全体市民谅解海军陆战队之真正动机，安居乐业。”

当中国记者采访张永武（Chang Yung-wu，音译，2t.疑为年龄或编号误植，此处保留原文语境）的父亲时，他强烈否认其子与“虹口事件”有任何牵连。目前被日本特别海军陆战队拘留的嫌疑犯是张家十个男孩中唯一幸存的儿子。

张父宣称，张是在东鸭绿江路桥附近经营食品摊的小贩。周三晚上他听到枪声，便赶往吴淞路查看情况，随即被日本军官逮捕。

张父说，青年被捕时穿着一件西式衬衫和一条从旧货店买来的裤子。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 27, 1936
16739
B. D. 7538
28 9 36

Police Lacking
Definite Clues
In Murder Case

Report Of Information
By Japanese Is Not
Backed By S.M.P.

While Japanes sources yesterday reported the discovery of "important clues" which might lead to the arrest of the culprits responsible for the killing of a Nipponese bluejacket and wounding of two others Wednesday night, officers of the Shanghai Municipal Police announced that their exhaustive investigation had made no material headway.

Although the nature of the widely-publicized "clues" is unrevealed, reports emanating from the local Japanese circles insist that the three men were involved in the shooting which took the life of First Class Seaman Asamitsu Taminato and which wounded Second Class Seaman Yoshitane Tawata and First Class Seaman Yoshimi Deriba.

One of these alleged clues, these sources added, indicates that the three gunmen took separate routes of escape after the shooting. One decamped along North Haining Road to North Szechuen Road, another to Chapoo Road and the third along Woosung Road to Kashing Road.

European officers who were assigned to the Special Political Section, which was created to investigate the case, confessed that they had not been informed of the new discovery.

S.M.P. Withhold Comment

Their investigation, this officer said, has been directed to various channels in order to gather information from as many angles bearing on the case as possible.

At the present time, he added, the S.M.P. is not yet prepared to speculate on any clue.

Meantime, much concern is being felt in local Chinese circles over the report that the Japanese have acquired some 100 mow of land in Chapei with the intention of building a special barracks.

This tract of land is located across the Shanghai-Woosung Railway, adjacent to the Japanese cemetery near Paitsechiao. After the shooting in Hongkew, the Japanese Naval Landing Party had installed military telephone wires connecting this place with its headquarters on Klangwan Road. Some 30 bluejackets were yesterday seen stationed inside the compound which is surrounded by black fence.

Building Material Seen

A large quantity of building material was piled on the lot, indicating that construction work is likely to start in the near future.

Paitsechiao, where the lot is located, was constantly in the news during the Sino-Japanese war in Shanghai in 1932. At that time it formed one of the important sectors of military operation.

The Hongkew area, transformed into an armed camp by the Japanese following the shooting, last Wednesday, showed further signs yesterday of returning to normalcy. The Japanese patrols were mostly withdrawn, although considerable activity was still evident after nightfall.

The only excitement yesterday was the report of a gun, belonging to a Japanese bluejacket stationed on the corner of Jukong and North Szechuen Roads which accidentally went off. The bullet lodged in a signboard of a Japanese restaurant. Although no one was injured, police started an investigation.

Suspect Released

Yu Hsu-keng, a "suspect" arrested by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party Friday night on Chapoo Road, was released by Settlement police after close questioning. At the time of his arrest, Yu was reading a poster on the wall of the Hongkew Cinema. Detained for over an hour at the Chapoo Road station of the Landing Party, he was later transferred to the Hongkew Station.

The investigation of the case is being handled by two separate groups of officers. One of these groups is the recently created Special Political Section headed by Assistant Commissioner S. Uyehara. Several other high Japanese S.M.P. officers, including Deputy Commissioner A. Tajima, is on this special body.

Another group, conducting an independent investigation is the officers attached to the Japanese Consular Police and the Landing Party.

It could not be learned last night which investigation body was responsible for unearthing the reported clues.

Many Patrols On Duty

Although Japanese naval patrols have been officially withdrawn from Chapei, an investigation shows that a large detachment of bluejackets were still touring the area. At the lot where the new barrack is reported to be located, some 400 bluejackets are stationed at night, residents in the area informed reporters.

In a two-hour emergency session yesterday the councillors of the Japanese Residents' Corporation adopted a set of unrevealed emergency measures to deal with the situation which arose as the result of the killing of the bluejacket on Wednesday.

One of these measures is to ask the Shanghai Municipal Police to increase the Japanese plainclothes detective staff.

警方在谋杀案中
缺乏明确线索

日方提供的情报报告
未获上海公共租界工部局警务处
支持

尽管日方消息来源昨日报道称发现了可能导向逮捕周三晚间杀害一名日本水兵并致伤另外两人的凶手的“重要线索”，但上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）官员宣布，其详尽调查并未取得实质性进展。

虽然这些被广泛报道的“线索”的性质尚未披露，但来自当地日侨圈子的报告坚持称，三名男子参与了枪击事件，该事件导致一等水兵田凑浅光（Asamitsu Taminato，音译）死亡，并致二等水兵多和田义种（Yoshitane Tawata，音译）和一等水兵出羽芳美（Yoshimi Deriba，音译）受伤。

这些消息来源补充说，其中一条所谓线索表明，三名枪手在枪击后分头逃窜。一人沿海宁北路逃往四川北路，另一人逃往乍浦路，第三人则沿吴淞路逃往嘉兴路。

被指派负责调查此案的特别政治科（Special Political Section）的欧籍警官承认，他们并未获悉这一新发现。

上海公共租界工部局警务处不予置评

这位警官表示，他们的调查已指向各个渠道，以便尽可能从多角度收集与案件有关的信息。

他补充说，目前上海公共租界工部局警务处尚不准备对任何线索进行推测。

与此同时，当地华人圈子对有关日方在闸北购置约100亩土地意图建造专用兵营的报告深感担忧。

这块土地位于沪宁铁路对面，毗邻白子桥附近的日本公墓。虹口枪击案发生后，日本海军陆战队已架设军用电话线，将该地与位于江湾路的总部连接起来。昨天可以看到大约30名水兵驻扎在这个被黑色围栏包围的大院内。

看到建筑材料

大量建筑材料堆积在该地块上，表明建筑工程很可能在不久的将来开始。

该地块所在的白子桥在1932年上海中日战争期间经常见诸报端。当时，它是军事行动的重要区域之一。

自上周三枪击案发生后被日方转变为武装营区的虹口地区，昨天显示出进一步恢复正常状态的迹象。日本巡逻队大多已撤走，尽管天黑后仍有相当多的活动迹象。

昨天唯一的骚动是有报告称，一名驻扎在九江路与四川北路拐角处的日本水兵的枪支意外走火。子弹嵌入一家日本餐馆的招牌中。虽然无人受伤，但警方已展开调查。

嫌疑人获释

周五晚在乍浦路被日本海军陆战队成员逮捕的“嫌疑人”余旭庚（Yu Hsu-keng，音译），在经过严密讯问后被租界警方释放。被捕时，余正在观看虹口大戏院墙上的海报。他在陆战队乍浦路站被拘留了一个多小时，随后被转移至虹口站。

此案的调查由两组独立的警官负责。其中一组是最近成立的特别政治科，由副总监S. Uyehara（上原，音译）领导。其他几位日籍上海公共租界工部局警务处高级警官，包括副总监A. Tajima（田岛，音译），也在该特别机构中任职。

另一组进行独立调查的是隶属于日本领事馆警察和海军陆战队的警官。

昨晚未能查明是哪个调查机构负责挖掘出所报道的线索。

大量巡逻队在岗

尽管日本海军巡逻队已正式从闸北撤出，但调查显示，大批水兵仍在该地区巡视。据该地区居民向记者透露，在据报道将建造新兵营的地块，夜间驻扎着约400名水兵。

在昨天举行的两小时紧急会议上，日本居留民团议员通过了一套未公开的紧急措施，以应对因周三水兵被杀而引发的局势。

其中一项措施是要求上海公共租界工部局警务处增加日籍便衣侦探人员。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 27, 1936

ADMIRABLE COMPOSURE
BY its proclamation No. 363 issued Friday, the Chinese City Government of Greater Shanghai has admonished again the people to preserve a spirit of friendliness toward foreign Powers and nationals. Particularly does it taboo expressions of opinion or acts of violence which may tend to give rise to international misunderstanding.
Brief as the proclamation is, it is clearly indicative of China's solicitude for the welfare of foreign residents of Shanghai and for the goodwill of the friendly Powers. Coming as it does in the wake of the Hongkew incident, it adds a new tone of sincerity to the previous official assurance of the Chinese authorities to assist in the attempts to have the culprits apprehended even though the scene of the murderous crime lies within the International Settlement.
Save for the patrolling of a section of Chapei and the search of Chinese buses there by members of the Japanese naval force to which the Chinese Government has rightly protested, the attitude of the Japanese authorities both here and at home has thus far been one of admirable composure in spite of apparent tension created by a certain minority of the local Japanese. As long as this composure is maintained, it would not be difficult to arrive at a solution to the problems which have arisen from the incident in question. Indeed nothing can injure the cause of Sino-Japanese amity more than mutual suspicion and periodic threat of force. Apparently the Japanese Government is fully appreciative of the need of a prompt settlement of all outstanding issues with China, and the need can be met only by the maintenance of a judicious frame of mind by both parties.
It is therefore encouraging - to learn that, although the conferences between the Japanese Ambassador and the Chinese Minister for Foreign Affairs have been "meagre" of result, efforts will be continued toward the desired end. The decision of the Japanese Government to deal with the Central Government on all problems instead of with local authorities as in the past will further help bring negotiations to an early conclusion. It is needless to point out that questions between two sovereign nations can be settled only through diplomatic channels, and Japan's belated adherence to this principle vis-a-vis China may, we hope, result ultimately in an enlightened policy in which reciprocity rather than aggressiveness will prevail.

《字林西报》，1936年9月27日，星期日

令人钦佩的沉着

大上海市政府通过周五发布的第363号公告，再次告诫民众保持对外国列强及侨民的友好精神。尤其禁止那些可能导致国际误解的意见表达或暴力行为。

尽管公告简短，但它清楚地表明了中国对上海外侨福祉以及对友好列强善意的关切。紧随虹口事件之后发布，它为中国当局此前作出的协助缉拿凶手的官方保证增添了新的诚意基调，尽管谋杀案现场位于公共租界内。

除了日本海军部队对闸北部分地区进行巡逻并搜查中国公交车——中国政府已对此提出正当抗议——之外，日本当局在此地及国内的态度迄今为止一直保持着令人钦佩的沉着，尽管当地部分日本人造成了明显的紧张局势。只要保持这种沉着，就不难找到解决由该事件引起的问题的办法。确实，没有什么比相互猜疑和周期性的武力威胁更能损害中日友好的事业了。显然，日本政府充分认识到需要迅速解决与中国的所有悬而未决的问题，而只有通过双方保持明智的心态才能满足这一需求。

因此，令人鼓舞的是，尽管日本大使与中国外交部长之间的会谈结果“寥寥”，但仍将继续努力以实现预期的目标。日本政府决定就所有问题与中央政府而非像过去那样与地方当局打交道，这将进一步有助于使谈判早日得出结论。无需指出，两个主权国家之间的问题只能通过外交渠道解决，我们希望日本迟来地坚持这一对华原则，最终能促成一种开明的政策，其中互惠而非侵略将占上风。
